mentions.heading: If we do not deliver new products, services, technologies, and customer experiences in response to increased competition, our business could suffer
mentions.detail: Start-ups, tech companies, ridesharing disrupt model; must commercialize EVs, AV, software-connected services, AI beyond core ICE business
mentions.quote: To successfully execute our long-term strategy, we must continue to develop and commercialize new products and services, including products and services that are outside of our historically core ICE business, such as EVs and AV capabilities, software-enabled connected services, future features and services based on AI, and other new businesses.

mentions.heading: Capital access needed to fund new technology development
mentions.detail: Technology development requires extensive capital; constrained or costlier capital versus peers could impair strategic plans
mentions.quote: If our access to capital were to become significantly constrained, if costs of capital increased significantly, or if our ability to raise capital is challenged relative to our peers, our ability to execute on our strategic plans could be adversely affected.

mentions.heading: Software defects and AI integration compliance
mentions.detail: Errors, bugs, vulnerabilities in vehicle software/hardware; AI integration may breach evolving regulatory standards
mentions.quote: Further, if we are unable to prevent or effectively remedy errors, bugs, vulnerabilities, or defects in our software and hardware, or fail to deploy updates to our software properly, or if we do not adequately prepare for and respond to new kinds of technological innovations, market developments, and changing customer needs and preferences, our sales, profitability, and long-term competitiveness may be materially harmed.

mentions.heading: Our ability to attract and retain talented and highly skilled employees is critical to our success and competitiveness
mentions.detail: Competition for software and hardware engineering talent for vehicles and connected services
mentions.quote: In particular, our vehicles and connected services increasingly rely on software and hardware that is highly technical and complex, and our success in this area is dependent upon our ability to retain and recruit the best talent.

mentions.heading: Our ability to maintain profitability is dependent upon our ability to timely fund and introduce new and improved vehicle models
mentions.detail: Development cycle of two years or more; EV acceptance depends on fuel prices, tax credits, infrastructure; high fixed costs
mentions.quote: The new vehicle development process can take two years or more, and a number of factors may lengthen that time period.

mentions.heading: Our long-term EV strategy is dependent upon our ability to profitably deliver a strategic portfolio of EVs.
mentions.detail: Must cut battery cell and pack costs, source battery materials, scale EV manufacturing; losses recorded on EV inventory including battery cells
mentions.quote: Our progress towards these objectives has impacted, and may continue to impact, the need to record losses on our EV-related inventory, including battery cells.

mentions.heading: The success of our long-term EV strategy is dependent on consumer adoption of EVs.
mentions.detail: Termination of U.S. EV tax incentives slowed adoption; EV realignment charges $1.6B and $6.0B in Q3/Q4 2025, $7.9B total in GMNA
mentions.quote: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we recorded total charges in GMNA of $7.9 billion. If industry-wide adoption rates continue to be slow, we may need to take additional portfolio actions to better match the consumer pace of EV adoption, such as not fully utilizing or reducing the capacity of our existing or future plants or reducing production hours or shifts, and we may become subject to claims by suppliers as a result of such actions.

drivers.name: consumer tax incentives for EV purchases

mentions.heading: Our near-term profitability is dependent upon the success of our current line of vehicles, particularly our full-size ICE SUVs and full-size ICE pickup trucks.
mentions.detail: Highest margins from full-size ICE SUVs and pickups; their cash funds EV, AV growth; oil price spikes could shift demand
mentions.quote: Any near-term shift in consumer preferences toward smaller, more fuel-efficient vehicles, whether as a result of increases in the price of oil or any sustained shortage of oil, including as a result of global political instability (such as related to ongoing conflicts globally), concerns about fuel consumption or GHG emissions, or other reasons, could weaken the demand for our higher margin vehicles.

drivers.name: full-size ICE SUVs and full-size ICE pickup trucks

mentions.heading: Fuel economy regulations could affect sales of high-margin vehicles
mentions.detail: Stricter fuel economy rules could limit sales or add material costs to full-size ICE SUVs and pickups
mentions.quote: More stringent fuel economy regulations could also impact our ability to sell these vehicles or could result in additional costs associated with these vehicles, which could be material.

mentions.heading: Highly competitive industry with historical excess manufacturing capacity
mentions.detail: High fixed labor costs, collective bargaining limits on closures; competitors' subsidized financing and incentives force GM to match, eroding margins
mentions.quote: In light of any excess capacity and high fixed costs, many industry participants have attempted to sell more vehicles by providing subsidized financing or leasing programs, offering marketing incentives, or reducing vehicle prices.

mentions.heading: Need for resilient North American-focused supply chain
mentions.detail: Raw material demand exceeds North American supply capacity; multi-year purchase commitments and higher inventory for ICE and EV supply chain
mentions.quote: Expected demand for these raw materials currently exceeds the North American capacity of the existing supply chain. If we are not successful in developing our North American supply chain, our results of operations and profitability could be negatively impacted.

mentions.heading: Low-cost manufacturers from China and India entering markets
mentions.detail: Chinese and Indian manufacturers competing in emerging and established markets, hurting pricing and share
mentions.quote: Manufacturers in countries that have lower production costs, such as China and India, have become competitors in key emerging markets and have begun offering their products in established markets, as well as low-cost alternatives to established entry-level automobiles.

mentions.heading: Foreign government protectionism and tariffs
mentions.detail: Foreign tax policies favoring domestic manufacturers and import tariffs could hurt GM and JV partners
mentions.quote: In addition, foreign governments may decide to implement tax and other policies that favor their domestic manufacturers at the expense of international manufacturers, including GM and its joint venture partners. Introduction or modification of import tariffs or tariff-related measures may lead to further challenges for GM and our global business.

mentions.heading: Refocused AV strategy on personal vehicles subject to technological, operational, regulatory and competitive risks
mentions.detail: Cruise robotaxi wound down Feb 2025; AV/ADAS efforts combined in GMNA; needs capital, AI talent, training data; competition from tech firms
mentions.quote: While we expect our refocused AV strategy to be less capital intensive than the Cruise robotaxi plan, we expect that our AV and ADAS development activities will continue to require significant capital investments and remain subject to a variety of risks inherent with the development of new technologies

mentions.heading: Regulatory and liability risks of AV commercial deployment
mentions.detail: Evolving federal, state, provincial regulation; accidents or cyber breaches of autonomous systems could cause liability and deter adoption
mentions.quote: To the extent accidents, cybersecurity breaches, or other adverse events associated with our autonomous driving systems occur, we could be subject to liability, reputational harm, government scrutiny, and further regulation, and it could deter consumer adoption of AV and ADAS technology.

mentions.heading: Risks associated with climate change, GHG emissions regulation and changing consumer demand
mentions.detail: Evolving emissions and fuel economy rules may require credit purchases or penalties, product portfolio changes, and raise ICE vehicle costs
mentions.quote: Despite recent actions taken by the U.S. federal government to reduce the stringency of emissions and fuel economy regulations, we expect such regulations at the federal, state, or local level or in international jurisdictions to continue to evolve

mentions.heading: Reduced emissions stringency slowing EV demand
mentions.detail: Relaxed emissions regulation has slowed and may continue to slow EV demand in North America
mentions.quote: In addition, the reduction in the stringency of emissions regulations has slowed and may continue to slow consumer demand for EVs in North America.

mentions.heading: Sustainability disclosure rules under legal scrutiny
mentions.detail: Shifting sustainability disclosure requirements may raise litigation, regulatory action and reputational risk
mentions.quote: Such regulations may cause disclosure requirements to shift and may increase the risk of litigation or regulatory action, which would result in increased costs (in our operations and supply chain), as well as risks to our reputation or consumer demand for our products if we do not meet demanding stakeholder expectations and standards.

mentions.heading: Climate change severe weather may disrupt production and demand
mentions.detail: Storms, droughts, wildfires may disrupt GM plants, suppliers, dealers, vehicle delivery and customer finances
mentions.quote: In addition, increased intensity, frequency, or duration of storms, droughts, wildfires, or other severe weather events as a result of climate change may disrupt our production and the production, logistics, cost, and procurement of products from our suppliers, timely delivery of vehicles to customers and operations of our dealers, and could negatively impact working conditions at our plants and those of our suppliers and dealers.

mentions.heading: Our business is highly dependent upon global automobile market sales volume, which can be volatile
mentions.detail: High fixed structural costs mean small vehicle sales volume changes disproportionately hit profitability
mentions.quote: Because we have a high proportion of relatively fixed structural costs, small changes in sales volume can have a disproportionately large effect on our profitability.

mentions.heading: Inflationary pressures and high prices and uncertain availability of commodities and inputs
mentions.detail: Steel, precious and non-ferrous metals, critical minerals, semiconductors and logistics costs raise production costs; may not pass through
mentions.quote: Increases in prices, including as a result of inflation and rising interest rates, for commodities, raw materials, energy, or other inputs that we and our suppliers use in manufacturing products, systems, components, and parts, such as steel, precious metals, non-ferrous metals, critical minerals, or other similar raw materials, or electrical subcomponents, including transistors, diodes, and other semiconductors, or increases in logistics and related costs, have led and may continue to lead to higher production costs for parts, components, and vehicles.

mentions.heading: Cost and availability of critical EV battery materials
mentions.detail: Lithium, nickel, cobalt, rare earth cost or shortage could raise EV costs and impede EV strategy
mentions.quote: In addition, elevated cost, or reduced availability, of critical materials for our EV propulsion systems, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, and certain rare earth metals, may lead to higher production costs for our EVs and could impede our ability to successfully deliver on our EV strategy.

mentions.heading: Evolving automotive tariffs could materially affect results
mentions.detail: U.S. tariffs on vehicles, parts, raw materials; USMCA review; pending legal challenges; impact may exceed estimates
mentions.quote: New or existing trade agreements, including the ongoing review of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, may also impact the tariff rate applicable to goods imported by GM or our suppliers. Additionally, certain tariffs are subject to pending legal challenges.

mentions.heading: Tariff mitigation may require footprint changes and charges
mentions.detail: Changing U.S. production plan and footprint may need significant capex, impairments, restructuring; won't fully offset tariffs near term
mentions.quote: We have made and may need to make additional changes to our global production footprint and workforce, which could require significant capital expenditures and could result in asset impairments and other charges, including restructuring charges, any of which could be material.

mentions.heading: Our business in China subjects us to unique operational, competitive, regulatory, and economic risks
mentions.detail: China JVs hit by domestic competitors; $2.1B impairment and $2.0B equity losses 2024, $0.6B charges 2025; SGM further restructuring 2026
mentions.quote: As a result of certain restructuring actions previously announced in December 2024, we recorded an other-than-temporary impairment of our equity interests of $2.1 billion and additional equity losses of $2.0 billion in the year ended December 31, 2024, and we recorded charges of $0.6 billion in the year ended December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: Our business in China subjects us to unique operational, competitive, regulatory, and economic risks
mentions.detail: U.S.-China trade tensions, weak Chinese economy, EV/software preferences and China supply chain integration may cut margins
mentions.quote: Increased competition, continued U.S.-China trade tensions, weakening economic conditions in China or China's level of integration with key components of our global supply chain, among other factors, may result in cost increases, price reductions, reduced sales, profitability, and margins, and challenges to gaining or holding market share.

mentions.heading: Our business in China subjects us to unique operational, competitive, regulatory, and economic risks
mentions.detail: Chinese government may restrict investments or critical material exports with little notice
mentions.quote: The Chinese government may adopt new regulations that may impact entities operating in China or the ability of non-Chinese entities to obtain critical materials from China, potentially with little advance notice.

mentions.heading: We benefit from many joint ventures and strategic relationships over which we may have limited control
mentions.detail: Relies on JVs for EV battery cell manufacturing and raw material access; limited control
mentions.quote: If we are unable to successfully source and execute on strategic business relationships in the future, our overall growth could be impaired, and our business, prospects, and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.

mentions.heading: We benefit from many joint ventures and strategic relationships over which we may have limited control
mentions.detail: EV raw material offtake agreements oblige purchases; low EV volumes or battery tech shifts could hurt cash flow; supplier investments may lose value
mentions.quote: If we are unable to utilize or otherwise monetize the raw materials we are obligated to purchase under these offtake agreements, whether as a result of lower than expected EV production volumes, lower than expected rates of consumer adoption, changes in battery technology that reduce the need for certain raw materials, or other reasons, it could materially adversely affect our cash flows and increase our inventory.

mentions.heading: Operations carried out by joint ventures with partners who may have different goals
mentions.detail: China and Korea operations, US/Canada battery and raw material JVs; primary China JV agreement expires 2027, renegotiation ongoing
mentions.quote: Our primary joint venture agreement for our China JVs expires in 2027, and we are in negotiations with our partner for a new agreement.

mentions.heading: Limited control over joint ventures and compliance
mentions.detail: Minority stakes limit control; JV misconduct, internal control issues could bring penalties, fines, reputational harm
mentions.quote: As a result, we may be unable to prevent violations of applicable laws or other misconduct by a joint venture, adverse human rights or other impacts, or the failure to satisfy contractual obligations by one or more parties.

mentions.heading: The international scale and footprint of our operations expose us to additional risks
mentions.detail: US-China tensions, dividend repatriation and technology export restrictions; FCPA exposure
mentions.quote: (5) political and economic tensions between governments and changes in international economic policies, including restrictions on the repatriation of dividends or in the export of technology, especially between China and the U.S.;

mentions.heading: Tariffs and trade barriers on global operations
mentions.detail: New or higher tariffs on products imported into or exported from the U.S.; free trade agreement changes
mentions.quote: (6) changes to customs requirements or procedures (e.g., inspections) or new or higher tariffs, for example, on products imported into or exported from the U.S., including under U.S. or other trade laws or measures, or other key markets;

mentions.heading: Any significant disruption at one of our manufacturing facilities could disrupt our production schedule
mentions.detail: Facilities model/market-specific with interdependencies; cannot easily shift production; weather, climate change, labor, health crises cited
mentions.quote: We may not be able to easily shift production to other facilities or to make up for lost production.

mentions.heading: Unionized hourly workforce under collective bargaining agreements
mentions.detail: Substantially all hourly employees unionized; agreements negotiated including at local facility level
mentions.quote: In addition, substantially all of our hourly employees are represented by unions and covered by collective bargaining agreements that must be negotiated from time-to-time, including at the local facility level.

mentions.heading: Disruption in our suppliers' operations could disrupt our production schedule
mentions.detail: Just-in-time minimal inventory except battery raw material offtakes; some single-source parts; could hit higher margin vehicles
mentions.quote: In some instances, we purchase systems, components, raw materials, and parts that are ultimately derived from a single source and may be at an increased risk for supply disruptions.

mentions.heading: Pandemics and other public health crises could materially adversely impact our business
mentions.detail: COVID-19 previously disrupted operations; could cause loan/lease defaults, lower auction pricing, impaired credit access
mentions.quote: Pandemics, epidemics, or disease outbreaks in the U.S. or globally, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, have previously disrupted, and may in the future disrupt, our business, which could materially affect our results of operations, financial condition, liquidity, and future expectations.

mentions.heading: Competitors may independently develop similar products despite our intellectual property
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Competitors may independently develop products and services similar to ours, and there are no guarantees that GM’s intellectual property rights would prevent competitors from independently developing or selling those products and services.

mentions.heading: Protection of intellectual property and infringement claims
mentions.detail: Trade secret theft attempts via IT intrusion, heightened by AI adoption
mentions.quote: We sometimes face attempts to gain unauthorized access to our information technology networks and systems for the purpose of improperly acquiring our trade secrets or confidential business information, and may face increased such risk from the rapid evolution and adoption of AI.

mentions.heading: Protection of intellectual property and infringement claims
mentions.detail: Targeted by patent enforcement actions including non-practicing entities; possible damages or injunctions on products
mentions.quote: In addition, we have been, and in the future may be, the target of patent enforcement actions by third parties, including aggressive and opportunistic enforcement claims by non-practicing entities. Regardless of the merit of such claims, responding to infringement claims can be expensive and time-consuming.

mentions.heading: Security breaches, cyberattacks, and disruptions to IT systems and networked products, including connected vehicles
mentions.detail: Connected vehicles, GM Financial data, third-party providers; cannot patch all vulnerabilities; acquired companies with weak security
mentions.quote: We are unable to comprehensively apply patches or mitigate all such vulnerabilities before they may be exploited by a threat actor. We have also acquired and in the future may acquire companies with vulnerabilities or unsophisticated security measures, which exposes us to potentially significant cybersecurity risks.

mentions.heading: Security breaches, cyberattacks, and disruptions to IT systems and networked products, including connected vehicles
mentions.detail: Reliance on vendors, suppliers, exchanges, clearinghouses and financial intermediaries for business activities
mentions.quote: We also face the risk of operational disruption, failure, termination, or capacity constraints of any of the service providers or third parties that facilitate our business activities, including vendors, suppliers, customers, counterparties, exchanges, clearing agents, clearinghouses, or other financial intermediaries.

mentions.heading: IT systems and connected products vulnerable to cyberattacks
mentions.detail: Regular phishing and cyber incidents at GM and third-party providers; threats amplified by AI; no material incident to date
mentions.quote: We and our third-party providers regularly experience cyberattacks and security incidents, such as phishing attacks, and we expect cyberattacks and incidents to continue in varying degrees, including due to the rapid evolution and adoption of AI.

mentions.heading: Security breaches and other disruptions of our in-vehicle systems could impact the safety of our customers
mentions.detail: Hackers have attempted to access vehicle software controlling engine, braking, steering, batteries; safety, liability, regulatory penalties
mentions.quote: However, hackers and other malicious actors have attempted, and we expect will attempt in the future, to gain unauthorized access to modify, alter, and use networks, vehicle software, or their systems to gain control of, or to change, our vehicles’ functionality, user interface, and performance characteristics, or to gain access to data stored in or generated by the vehicle.

mentions.heading: Right to repair laws could expose vehicle systems to third-party access
mentions.detail: Right to repair laws could permit third-party access to vehicle data and systems without adequate security
mentions.quote: Laws that would permit third-party access to vehicle data and related systems, including "right to repair" laws, could expose our vehicles and vehicle systems to third-party access without appropriate security measures in place, leading to new safety and security risks for our customers and reducing customer trust and confidence in our products.

mentions.heading: Enterprise data practices subject to increasingly complex, restrictive, and punitive regulations
mentions.detail: Subject to CCPA/CPRA, EU GDPR, EU AI Act, UK Data Protection Act; compliance costs rising, AI adoption intensifies risk
mentions.quote: Complying with these new laws has significantly increased, and may continue to increase, our operating costs and is driving increased complexity in our operations.

mentions.heading: Operations subject to extensive laws including vehicle emissions and fuel economy standards
mentions.detail: Fuel economy/GHG rules may limit profitable ICE sales, require credit purchases, penalties; unharmonized jurisdictions, possible sales mandates
mentions.quote: these regulations could require us to further limit the sale of certain profitable ICE products in current and future years, subsidize the sale of less profitable ones, change our manufacturing processes, pay increased penalties, purchase additional credits from our competitors or undertake other activities that may require us to incur additional expense, which may be material.

mentions.heading: Proposed GHG rule changes could impair emissions credits
mentions.detail: Proposed GHG standard changes could impair emissions credits, as with prior CAFE credit impairment
mentions.quote: In addition, proposed regulatory changes to the GHG emissions standards could result in an impairment of our emissions credits, similar to the previous impairment we recognized related to our CAFE credits.

mentions.heading: Limits on ability to achieve fuel economy improvements
mentions.detail: EV infrastructure gaps, battery raw material supply, consumer acceptance may prevent profitable EV sales needed for compliance
mentions.quote: There is no assurance that we will be able to produce and sell vehicles that use such new technologies on a profitable basis or that our customers will purchase such vehicles in the quantities necessary for us to comply with current or future regulatory requirements.

mentions.heading: Compliance costs and alleged violations of fuel economy or emission standards
mentions.detail: Alleged fuel economy/emission violations could cause recalls, fines, restricted offerings, facility idling; compliance costs not reasonably estimable
mentions.quote: Alleged violations of fuel economy or vehicle emission standards could result in legal proceedings, the recall of one or more of our products, negotiated remedial actions, fines and penalties, restricted product offerings, or a combination of any of those items.

drivers.name: fuel economy or vehicle emission standards

mentions.heading: Evolving regulation of advanced technologies including AVs
mentions.detail: Autonomous vehicle regulation evolving domestically and abroad; could impede commercialization and raise costs
mentions.quote: In addition, many of our advanced technologies, including AVs, present novel issues with which domestic and foreign regulators have only limited experience and will be subject to evolving regulatory frameworks.

mentions.heading: We could be materially adversely affected by unusual or significant litigation, governmental investigations, or other proceedings
mentions.detail: Product liability, warranty, class action, emissions, privacy, stockholder suits; see Note 16
mentions.quote: We are subject to legal proceedings in the U.S. and elsewhere involving various issues, including product liability lawsuits, warranty litigations, class action litigations alleging product defects, emissions litigations, privacy matters, stockholder litigations, labor and employment litigations, and claims and actions arising from restructurings and divestitures of operations and assets.

mentions.heading: The costs and effect on our reputation of product safety recalls and alleged defects
mentions.detail: Recall costs amplified on global platforms; AV safety concerns could trigger recalls and reputational damage
mentions.quote: The costs to complete a recall could be exacerbated to the extent that such action relates to a global platform.

mentions.heading: Supplier part quality issues and limited cost recovery
mentions.detail: Recall cost recovery from suppliers limited by supplier financial condition; defects may surface years after production
mentions.quote: Our ability to recover costs associated with recalls or other campaigns caused by parts or components purchased from suppliers may be limited by the suppliers’ financial condition or a number of other reasons or defenses.

mentions.heading: We may incur additional tax expense, become subject to additional tax exposure, or fail to fully realize available tax incentives
mentions.risk_name: Tax law change and incentive loss
mentions.detail: IRS audits; uncertainty over full realization of IRA incentives and law changes; deferred tax asset valuation
mentions.quote: the possibility of tax controversy related to adverse determinations with respect to the application of existing laws (for example, with respect to full realization of the incentives contemplated by the IRA), changes in our business or structure and changes in the valuation of our deferred tax assets and liabilities.

mentions.heading: We rely on GM Financial to provide financial services to our customers and dealers
mentions.detail: GM Financial funding via credit facilities, securitizations, debt; portfolio credit losses, used vehicle auction values, residuals, rates affect financing support for vehicle sales
mentions.quote: The primary factors that could adversely affect GM Financial’s business and operations and reduce its ability to provide financing services at competitive rates include the sufficiency, availability, and cost of sources of funding, including credit facilities, securitization programs, and secured and unsecured debt issuances;

mentions.heading: GM Financial must comply with financial services laws and regulations
mentions.detail: GM Financial subject to consumer protection laws; noncompliance risks penalties and license revocation
mentions.quote: The failure to comply with these laws could result in significant statutory civil and criminal penalties, monetary damages, attorneys’ fees and costs, revocation of licenses, and damage to reputation, brand, and valued customer relationships.

mentions.heading: Our pension funding requirements could increase significantly
mentions.detail: Plans hold significant equity and fixed income; discount rate declines or weak returns raise contributions; illiquid investments
mentions.quote: Future funding requirements generally increase if the discount rate decreases or if actual asset returns are lower than expected asset returns, assuming other factors are held constant.

mentions.heading: Non-U.S. pension plan funding requirements
mentions.detail: Certain non-U.S. plans have no assets; higher local minimum funding rules could strain liquidity
mentions.quote: Certain plans outside the U.S. do not have assets and therefore the obligation is funded as benefits are paid. If local legal authorities increase the minimum funding requirements for our non-U.S. plans, we could be required to contribute more funds, which could negatively affect our liquidity and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Rapid policy change in the United States creating uncertainty
mentions.detail: Rapid US policy change and unpredictable trade policy including tariffs hamper long-term planning and capital allocation
mentions.quote: Rapid policy change in our home market, the United States, is creating uncertainty in our operations and business outlook, and may remain a source of volatility in the future.

mentions.heading: Ford's long-term success depends on delivering the Ford+ plan, including improving cost competitiveness
mentions.detail: Ford+ transformation requires capital allocation across powertrains, services, technology; cost and quality competitiveness needed
mentions.quote: If we are unable to optimize our capital allocation among vehicles (and propulsion systems among our vehicles), services, technology, and other calls on capital, make sufficient and timely progress to become competitive on cost and quality and ensure that progress is sustainable, or we are otherwise not successful in executing Ford+ (or are delayed for reasons outside of our control), we may not be able to realize the full benefits of our plan, which could have an adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations.

mentions.heading: Slow Ford+ progress could trigger shareholder activism
mentions.detail: Failure to progress Ford+ at expected pace may increase activism and divert management
mentions.quote: Furthermore, if we fail to make progress on our plan at the pace that shareholders expect, it may lead to an increase in shareholder activism, which may disrupt the conduct of our business and divert management’s attention and resources.

mentions.heading: Product defects resulting in recalls, warranty costs, or launch delays
mentions.detail: Vehicle defects, including supplier-provided components, drive safety recalls, warranty costs and launch delays
mentions.quote: We may also be obligated to remedy defects or potentially recall our products due to defective components provided to us by our suppliers, arising from their quality issues or otherwise.

mentions.heading: NHTSA enforcement, consent orders and recall costs
mentions.detail: 2024 NHTSA consent order; independent third party monitors Safety Act adherence and reports to NHTSA
mentions.quote: For example, as part of a consent order we entered into with NHTSA in 2024, we have retained an independent third party selected by NHTSA to assess the Company’s adherence to the consent order and Safety Act over the term of the consent order and to report on Ford’s progress to NHTSA.

mentions.heading: Recall costs from potentially defective airbag inflators
mentions.detail: 3.5 million Takata inflators and 2.5 million vehicles with ARC/Delphi inflators under NHTSA review; supplier recovery limited
mentions.quote: Of these, approximately 3.5 million of the inflators are in our vehicles. In addition, NHTSA is considering action related to 52 million vehicles containing inflators from ARC Automotive and Delphi Automotive in the United States. Ford has 2.5 million vehicles within this population.

mentions.heading: Emissions-related defect reporting and warranty obligations
mentions.detail: Must report and correct emissions defects and honor regulatory emissions warranties, including in the United States
mentions.quote: Similarly, where required by regulation, we are obligated to honor certain warranties on emissions-related components, which can impose additional obligations beyond our standard warranties and increase our costs.

mentions.heading: Warranty costs may exceed accruals
mentions.detail: Vehicle complexity, new technologies, quality improvement time, ineffective remedies, parts unavailability and inflation could raise warranty costs
mentions.quote: If warranty costs are greater than anticipated as a result of increased vehicle and component complexity, the adoption of new technologies, the time it takes to improve the quality of our products and services (or if such efforts are unsuccessful), implementation of additional remedies in the event the initial one is ineffective or parts are unavailable, or otherwise (including as a result of higher repair costs driven by inflation or other economic factors), such costs could continue to have an adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations.

mentions.heading: Quality issues causing launch slowdowns and reputational harm
mentions.detail: Slowed launches to improve quality; vehicles held for quality control raise inventory and repair costs
mentions.quote: In an effort to improve quality, we have slowed down and may continue to slow down launches, which may result in lost sales, revenue, and profits and could have an adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations.

mentions.heading: Ford is highly dependent on its suppliers to deliver components
mentions.detail: 2025 production disrupted by fires at a major aluminum supplier, effects ongoing; global multi-tier supply network
mentions.quote: For example, in 2025, our production was disrupted by fires at one of our major aluminum suppliers, the effects of which are ongoing.

mentions.heading: Dependence on supply of batteries and battery raw materials
mentions.detail: EV production depends on batteries and lithium, cobalt, nickel; offtake agreements obligate purchases; mine underperformance risk
mentions.quote: For the manufacture of our electrified products, we are dependent on the supply of batteries and the raw materials (e.g., lithium, cobalt, and nickel) used by our suppliers to produce those batteries. Some of these resources are limited, and, as a result, we may be unable to acquire raw materials needed for our products in sufficient amounts that are responsibly sourced or at reasonable prices.

mentions.heading: Offtake agreements obligate minimum raw material purchases
mentions.detail: Offtake and long-term contracts require purchase of minimum output from raw materials suppliers
mentions.quote: As described in the Liquidity and Capital Resources section in Item 7 below, and elsewhere herein, we have entered into and we may, in the future, enter into offtake agreements and other long-term purchase contracts that obligate us, subject to certain conditions such as quality or minimum output, to purchase a certain percentage or minimum amount of output from certain raw materials suppliers.

mentions.heading: Shortage of key components or raw materials
mentions.detail: China rare earth export restrictions disrupted production, forced rescheduling, raised premium freight and expedited shipping costs
mentions.quote: For example, China’s restriction on the export of rare earth minerals, which we and our suppliers utilize for a number of components, has impacted (e.g., rescheduling production, changing operating patterns)

mentions.heading: Shortage of key components or raw materials
mentions.detail: Traditional and EV-specific component suppliers may face distress or exit, narrowing sourcing options
mentions.quote: Moreover, as the industry evolves, suppliers of traditional or EV-specific components may face financial distress or choose to exit certain lines of business, further narrowing our sourcing options and potentially leading to higher prices or supply shortages that could have a substantial adverse effect on our results of operations and reputation.

mentions.heading: Production could be disrupted by labor issues, disasters and other factors
mentions.detail: Ford Blue, Model e, Pro realize no revenue during suspensions while expenses continue; labor, COVID, climate, cyber causes
mentions.quote: Our Ford Blue, Ford Model e, and Ford Pro operations generally do not realize revenue while our manufacturing operations are suspended, but we continue to incur operating and non-operating expenses, resulting in a deterioration of our cash flow.

mentions.heading: Production could be disrupted by labor issues, disasters and other factors
mentions.detail: Work stoppages have occurred; collective bargaining disputes, negotiations, plant closure restructuring cited
mentions.quote: A work stoppage or other limitation on production has occurred, and could in the future occur, at Ford’s facilities, at a facility in its supply chain, or at one of its logistics providers for any number of reasons, including as a result of labor issues, such as shortages of available employees, disputes under existing collective bargaining agreements with labor unions or in connection with negotiation of new collective bargaining agreements, absenteeism, public health issues (e.g., COVID), stay-at-home orders, or in response to potential restructuring actions (e.g., plant closures);

mentions.heading: Supply chain interruptions and inconsistent production schedule
mentions.detail: Component shortages, labor shortages led to supplier claims for reimbursement beyond agreed terms; Ford has made payments
mentions.quote: As a result of this disrupted production schedule, we have received and continue to receive claims from our supply base for reimbursement of costs beyond our original agreed terms.

mentions.heading: Climate and logistics disruptions to supply chain
mentions.detail: Wildfires, droughts, flooding, extreme temperatures; freight carrier and logistics provider interruptions
mentions.quote: Given the worldwide scope of our supply chain and operations, we and our suppliers face a risk of disruption or operating inefficiencies that may increase costs due to the adverse physical effects of climate change, which are predicted to increase the frequency and severity of weather and other natural events, e.g., wildfires, extended droughts, flooding, and extreme temperatures.

mentions.heading: Single or limited source components
mentions.detail: Many components single/limited-sourced; suppliers may threaten disruption as negotiating leverage; could impact fuel economy compliance
mentions.quote: Many components used in our products are available only from a single or limited number of suppliers and, therefore, cannot be re-sourced quickly or inexpensively to another supplier (due to long lead times, specialized tooling, rigorous validation requirements, and new contractual commitments that may be required by another supplier before ramping up to provide the components or materials, etc.).

mentions.heading: Model changeover and production complexity delays
mentions.detail: Model changeovers require downtime; vehicle complexity raises delay risk; may affect fuel economy standards strategy
mentions.quote: In addition, when we undertake a model changeover, significant downtime at one or more of our production facilities may be required, and our ability to return to full production may be delayed if we experience production difficulties at one of our facilities or a supplier’s facility.

mentions.heading: Ford may not realize anticipated benefits of alliances, joint ventures, acquisitions
mentions.detail: JVs and alliances complex, capital intensive, regulatory approvals; limited control over joint ventures
mentions.quote: Further, to the extent we share ownership, control, or management with another party in a joint venture, our ability to influence the joint venture may be limited, and we may be unable to prevent misconduct or implement our compliance or internal control systems.

mentions.heading: Critical material offtake agreements and supplier investments
mentions.detail: Offtake agreements and investments in raw material and battery suppliers; suppliers in less developed markets may not adopt sustainability standards
mentions.quote: In order to secure critical materials to manufacture our products, we have entered into and may, in the future, enter into offtake agreements and other long-term purchase contracts with raw materials and other suppliers and make investments in certain raw material, battery, and suppliers; however, we may not realize the anticipated benefits of these actions

mentions.heading: Implementation of new business strategy may not succeed or may disrupt operations
mentions.detail: New battery energy storage business announced Q4 2025; alternative distribution models may underperform historical arrangements
mentions.quote: For example, the new battery energy storage business we announced in the fourth quarter of 2025 or our efforts to evaluate and implement alternative distribution models and channels for our products and services from those we have traditionally used may be challenged or may not succeed or be as successful as our historical arrangements.

mentions.heading: External factors including U.S.-China tensions and Chinese EV competition
mentions.detail: U.S.-China tensions; Chinese electrified vehicle producers exporting into Ford's key markets
mentions.quote: For example, our business and strategy are susceptible to tensions in U.S.-China relations and the rapid development of the Chinese electrified vehicle industry, with domestic Chinese producers exporting to some key markets in which we operate.

mentions.heading: Slower EV adoption leads to capacity cuts, impairments and incentive repayment
mentions.detail: EV adoption lower than anticipated; capacity reductions, program cancellations, write-downs, possible repayment of government incentives
mentions.quote: For example, we have taken, and may in the future take, such actions to better match the pace of EV adoption, which has been lower than anticipated industrywide.

mentions.heading: Charges and financial exposure following strategy changes or venture unwinds
mentions.detail: December 2025 updated EV strategy and expected disposition of BlueOval SK, LLC investment with related charges
mentions.quote: For example, in December 2025, we announced our updated EV strategy, the expected disposition of our investment in BlueOval SK, LLC, and the charges we expected to record related to those items.

mentions.heading: Ford may not realize the anticipated benefits of restructuring actions and such actions may cause significant charges
mentions.detail: Plant closures, shift reductions, program cancellations; potential claims and incentive clawbacks; savings may not materialize
mentions.quote: Such restructuring actions have caused us and may in the future cause us to incur significant costs; record impairments or other charges; subject us to potential claims from employees, suppliers, dealers, other counterparties, or governmental authorities (including a reduction or clawback of

mentions.heading: Failure to develop and deploy secure digital services that appeal to customers could hurt Ford's business
mentions.detail: Integrated software/subscription services targeted as larger revenue share; depends on modem activation and subscriber growth
mentions.quote: If we do not develop, deliver, and make available standardized technologies that customers can easily adopt and use, fail to generate sufficient demand for our integrated software and digital services, or if customers do not opt to activate the modems in our vehicles, which would hinder our ability to offer and sell such services, we may not grow revenue in line with the costs we are investing or achieve profitability on our increasingly digitally-connected products.

mentions.heading: Shifting data privacy and AI policy affecting digital services
mentions.detail: Data privacy and AI policy shifts have already caused costs and could cause service lapses across jurisdictions
mentions.quote: Shifting public policy regarding data privacy and the effects of artificial intelligence has caused and may in the future cause us to incur substantial costs to modify our operations or business practices, reduce consumers’ willingness to engage with our offerings, or cause delays or lapses in the availability of our products or services in various jurisdictions.

mentions.heading: Dependence on third-party content and technology licenses
mentions.detail: Third-party content and software licenses may not renew on reasonable terms; providers may compete
mentions.quote: This includes the right to sell, or offer subscriptions to, third-party content, as well as the right to incorporate specific content into our own services; however, continuation of these third-party licensing and other arrangements, or their renewal on commercially reasonable terms, is not guaranteed or may be unavailable.

mentions.heading: Software integration defects, outages and third-party cloud reliance
mentions.detail: Reliance on third-party cloud infrastructure; risk of failed over-the-air (OTA) updates causing widespread issues
mentions.quote: Moreover, the reliance of our services on cloud-based systems and other digital infrastructure owned by third parties creates particular risk. Any outage, misconfiguration, or loss of data within the systems or infrastructure of these third parties could impair the performance of our services from time to time.

mentions.heading: BlueCruise growth, competition and regulatory scrutiny
mentions.detail: BlueCruise hands-free system under government investigations including of Ford; failure risks unrecouped investment
mentions.quote: In addition, autonomous vehicle and driver assist technologies, including BlueCruise, continue to be scrutinized by government regulators and consumers, and actual or perceived failures or misuse of these technologies and features have led to government investigations and inquiries, including of Ford.

drivers.name: autonomous vehicle and driver assist technologies

mentions.heading: Dependence on third-party dealers for services sales
mentions.detail: Majority of connectivity, digital and software services sales go through third-party dealers; investment in dealer programs may not yield sales
mentions.quote: While we continue to invest in direct-to-consumer sales methods for our connectivity, digital and physical services, and integrated software services offerings, we are dependent on the efforts of third-party dealers for the majority of our sales in this space.

mentions.heading: Fraudulent or abusive activities by end users of digital services
mentions.detail: Stolen credentials, non-payment for services, terms-of-service violations on Ford digital services
mentions.quote: These include unauthorized use of accounts through stolen credentials, failure to pay for services accessed, or other activities that violate our terms of service.

mentions.heading: Ford's ability to maintain a competitive cost structure could be affected by labor or other constraints
mentions.detail: Recent UAW and Unifor contracts caused significant cost increases; non-union competitors; constraints on closing plants in US, Canada, Europe
mentions.quote: Our recent labor contracts, including those with the International Union, United Automobile, Aerospace and Agricultural Implement Workers of America (“UAW”) in the United States and Unifor in Canada, have resulted in significant cost increases. If we are unable to offset these costs, it could have a significant adverse effect on our business.

mentions.heading: Ford's ability to attract, develop, grow, support, and reward talent is critical
mentions.detail: Intense competition for software, electrification and integrated services talent raising compensation
mentions.quote: While we have been successful in attracting talent in recent years, as with any company, the ability to continue to attract talent is important, particularly in growth areas vital to our success such as software, electrification and adjacent technologies, and integrated services.

mentions.heading: Operational information systems, security systems, products, and services could be affected by cybersecurity incidents
mentions.detail: Includes in-vehicle systems and connected vehicles; Ford, suppliers, dealers already targeted; Ford Credit receivables systems exposed
mentions.quote: This risk exposure rises as we continue to develop and produce vehicles with increased connectivity. Moreover, we, our suppliers, service providers, and dealers have been the target of cybersecurity incidents and such threats are continuing and evolving, which may cause cybersecurity incidents to be more difficult to detect for periods of time.

mentions.heading: Multi-year commitments to raw material suppliers for electrified products
mentions.detail: Battery raw material offtake agreements (lithium, cobalt, nickel); Ford bears risk of lower EV volumes or battery tech change; charges already incurred
mentions.quote: Unlike our standard arrangements with suppliers, under multi-year offtake agreements and other long-term purchase contracts, the risks associated with lower-than-expected electrified vehicle production volumes or changes in battery technology that reduce the need for certain raw materials, batteries, or their components are borne by Ford rather than our suppliers.

mentions.heading: Raw material costs under offtake agreements for electrified vehicles
mentions.detail: Battery raw materials for EV business under offtake and long-term purchase contracts; limited ability to pass costs to customers
mentions.quote: Accordingly, we may be subject to increases in the prices we pay for those raw materials, and our ability to recoup such costs through increased pricing to our customers may be limited.

mentions.heading: Economic or geopolitical developments, including protectionist trade policies, could adversely affect Ford
mentions.detail: U.S.-China strain, rare earth minerals from China, rapid growth of Chinese EV exporters into Ford's key markets
mentions.quote: The continued strain in U.S.-China relations presents unique risks to U.S. automakers, as does China’s unique regulatory landscape, the level of integration with key components in our global supply chain, the limited availability of various components and materials (including certain rare earth minerals and related products from China), and the rapid development of the Chinese EV industry, with Chinese electrified vehicle manufacturers exporting their products to some key markets in which we operate.

mentions.heading: Changes in international trade policy, including tariffs
mentions.detail: U.S. and retaliatory tariffs on automobiles, parts and materials disrupted supply chains and raised costs for Ford, suppliers and dealers
mentions.quote: Tariffs implemented to date in the United States and elsewhere have caused significant disruption, increased costs, and uncertainty in the automotive industry, including for Ford, other OEMs, suppliers, and dealers, as well as customers.

mentions.heading: Uncertain receipt of tariff relief refunds
mentions.detail: Tariff refund receivable subject to U.S. Department of Commerce approval; delay or non-receipt hurts cash flow
mentions.quote: Accordingly, any delay in receiving the refunds could have a negative impact on our cash flow, and in the event we do not ultimately receive a refund, it could have an adverse impact on our financial condition or results of operations.

mentions.heading: Supply chain instability from China rare earth export restrictions
mentions.detail: China's export restrictions on rare earth minerals and components already caused production disruptions and cost increases
mentions.quote: In addition, instability in the supply chain exacerbated by tariffs and other industry concerns, such as China’s restriction on the export of rare earth minerals and various components, has resulted in production disruptions and increased costs and heightens the risk of future production disruptions and further cost increases.

mentions.heading: Exposure to economic, geopolitical, or other events in volatile markets and global supply chain
mentions.detail: Global operations exposed to nationalization of facilities or IP, exchange/import controls, war, terrorism disrupting supply chain
mentions.quote: This could include governmental takeover (i.e., nationalization) of our manufacturing facilities or intellectual property, restrictive exchange or import controls, changes to international trade agreements, disruption of operations as a result of systemic political or economic instability, social unrest, outbreak of war or expansion of hostilities, and acts of terrorism, each of which could impact our supply chain as well as our operations.

mentions.heading: Exposure to economic, geopolitical, or other events in volatile markets and global supply chain
mentions.detail: U.S. and other government sanctions could restrict business with countries or affiliates, disrupt production and earnings repatriation
mentions.quote: Further, the U.S. government, other governments, and international organizations could impose additional sanctions or export controls that could restrict us from doing business directly or indirectly in or with certain countries or parties, which could include affiliates, disrupt our supply chain and production, and potentially impact the repatriation of earnings.

mentions.heading: Products and services subject to market acceptance and significant competition
mentions.detail: Multi-year vehicle development cycles versus fast-changing preferences; weak demand raises inventory, pricing pressure, lower margins
mentions.quote: It takes years to design and develop a new vehicle or change an existing vehicle. Because customers’ preferences may change quickly, our new and existing products may not generate sales in sufficient quantities and at costs low enough to be profitable and recoup investment costs.

drivers.name: automotive and digital and software services industries

mentions.heading: Reputational harm from allegations amplified by social media
mentions.detail: Allegations on quality, safety, fuel efficiency, sustainability spread via internet and social media, even if unfounded
mentions.quote: With increased consumer interconnectedness through the internet, social media, and other media, mere allegations relating to quality, safety, reliability, fuel efficiency, sustainability, corporate social responsibility, or other key attributes can negatively impact our reputation or market acceptance of our products or services, even where such allegations prove to be inaccurate or unfounded.

mentions.heading: Intense competition from traditional and new entrants
mentions.detail: Chinese EV producers exporting into key markets; new competitors target pickups, utilities, commercial vehicles with lower fixed costs
mentions.quote: For example, Chinese electrified vehicle producers are exporting their products to some key markets in which we operate.

mentions.heading: Low EV adoption rates and shifting regulatory support
mentions.detail: Scaled back EV investments; industrywide EV adoption below plan; US regulatory shift away from EV support in 2025; fuel economy compliance at risk
mentions.quote: Low EV adoption rates may persist, including as a result of the regulatory framework in various markets shifting away from supporting the adoption of electrified vehicles (as was the case in the United States in 2025); any negative perception of our electrified vehicles or EVs in general; an inability to or delay in developing or embracing new technologies or processes; or shifts in consumer preference.

mentions.heading: Failure to achieve climate and decarbonization targets
mentions.detail: SBTi-approved interim emissions targets under reassessment; vehicle CO2 shortfalls could harm reputation, investment returns, customer and investor relations
mentions.quote: For example, we are exposed to reputational risk if we do not reduce vehicle CO2 emissions in line with our targets or in compliance with applicable regulations.

mentions.heading: New technologies may present challenges, recalls and erode customer trust
mentions.detail: Electrified vehicles and autonomous driving tech have led to customer claims, government investigations and recalls
mentions.quote: Moreover, new offerings, including those related to electrified vehicles and autonomous driving technologies, may present technological challenges that could be costly to implement and overcome and have subjected us and may continue to subject us to customer claims, government investigations, and recalls of our vehicles if they do not operate as anticipated.

mentions.heading: Ford may face increased price competition for its products and services
mentions.detail: Global auto overcapacity drives incentives; foreign competitors' weak currencies; inability to offset tariffs and commodity costs
mentions.quote: As a result, we are not necessarily able to set our prices to offset higher marketing incentives, commodity or other cost increases, tariffs, or the impact of adverse currency fluctuations. This risk includes cost advantages foreign competitors may have because of their weaker home market currencies, which may, in turn, enable those competitors to offer their products at lower prices.

mentions.heading: EV market evolution and lower-than-anticipated adoption
mentions.detail: US policy cut EV incentives; charges for EV supplier payments, inventory, impairments; battery facility investments may not be recouped
mentions.quote: The trend may be further exacerbated as recent policy changes in the United States have reduced or eliminated supply- and demand-side EV incentives, which may further slow the adoption of EVs.

mentions.heading: Battery facility underutilization
mentions.detail: High battery costs hinder EV price parity; underused battery plants may prevent recouping investment
mentions.quote: Furthermore, given our existing and continued investment in battery production, if we are unable to operate battery facilities at their expected capacity because EV adoption rates or the demand for such batteries is lower-than-anticipated or otherwise, we may be unable to recoup our investments.

mentions.heading: Higher EV adoption could create ICE excess capacity
mentions.detail: Rising EV adoption could create excess capacity in ICE trucks and utilities, increasing price competition
mentions.quote: Conversely, should EV adoption rates increase again in the future, the risk of excess capacity, particularly for internal combustion engine trucks and utilities, may be exacerbated. This excess capacity may further increase price competition in that segment of the market, which could have a substantial adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations.

drivers.name: internal combustion engine trucks and utilities

mentions.heading: Inflationary pressure and fluctuations in commodity and energy prices, foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates, and investment values
mentions.detail: Higher material costs; supplier claims for reimbursement beyond agreed terms paid; warranty costs up from dealer inflation
mentions.quote: Moreover, due to inflationary pressure, some of our suppliers have submitted claims to us for reimbursement of costs beyond our original agreed terms. Upon receipt, we evaluate those claims, and, in certain circumstances, we have made payments to our suppliers, and this trend may continue.

mentions.heading: Interest rate exposure at Ford Credit
mentions.detail: High rates may impair Ford Credit's funding access and competitive financing, reducing financing margin; capital-intensive business faces higher cost of capital
mentions.quote: At Ford Credit, a high interest rate environment may impact Ford Credit’s ability to source funding and offer financing at competitive rates, which could reduce its financing margin.

mentions.heading: Market value fluctuations of investments
mentions.detail: Unrealized gains and losses on marketable securities could be material in any period
mentions.quote: In addition, our results are impacted by fluctuations in the market value of our investments, with unrealized gains and losses that could be material in any period.

mentions.heading: Ford’s results are dependent on sales of larger, more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States
mentions.detail: Profits depend on ICE trucks and utilities in US; shift in preferences or faster EV adoption could cause asset charges
mentions.quote: A shift in consumer preferences away from larger, more profitable vehicles with internal combustion engines (including trucks and utilities) to other vehicles in our portfolio that may be less profitable could result in an adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations.

mentions.heading: Emissions regulations and ICE vehicle restrictions
mentions.detail: ZEV mandates, low emission zones, city access restrictions could raise vehicle costs and limit sales of profitable ICE vehicles
mentions.quote: In addition, government regulations aimed at reducing emissions and increasing fuel efficiency (e.g., ZEV mandates and low emission zones) and other factors that accelerate the transition to EVs in various markets may increase the cost of vehicles by more than the perceived benefit to consumers and dampen margins.

mentions.heading: Disruption at facilities producing larger, more profitable vehicles
mentions.detail: Stoppage, launch delay or stop ship at plants building profitable large vehicles would have outsized impact
mentions.quote: While a suspension or disruption of our manufacturing operations at any facility could have an adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flow, such an occurrence at one of our facilities where our larger, more profitable vehicles are produced, or in the event a launch is delayed or a stop ship is initiated for those vehicles, the impact may be particularly significant.

mentions.heading: Industry sales volume can be volatile and could decline
mentions.risk_name: Cyclical demand with high fixed costs
mentions.detail: High fixed structural costs; sales sensitive to rates, tariffs, inflation affordability, ridesharing trends
mentions.quote: Because we, like other manufacturers, have a higher proportion of fixed structural costs, relatively small changes in industry sales volume can have a substantial effect on our cash flow and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Ford's receipt of government incentives could be subject to reduction, termination, or clawback
mentions.detail: Grants, forgivable loans, tax abatements; repayment if programs cancelled or job targets missed
mentions.quote: Further, we may lose or be required to repay incentives or forgivable loans as a result of a change we make to our business strategy, e.g., if we elect not to proceed with a previously planned program or project or do not create as many jobs as initially anticipated.

mentions.heading: Brazil incentive assessments and tax challenges
mentions.detail: Brazil federal assessments on prior incentives; São Paulo challenges Bahia tax incentives; collateral posted, more may be required
mentions.quote: The federal government in Brazil has levied assessments against us concerning the federal incentives we previously received, and the State of São Paulo has challenged the grant to us of tax incentives by the State of Bahia.

mentions.heading: Elimination of U.S. EV purchaser tax credits
mentions.detail: Up to $7,500 per-vehicle credit eliminated in 2025; battery supply chains built to avoid China lose rationale
mentions.quote: In 2025, Congress eliminated these credits, ending the incentives for purchasers and likewise changing the business rationale to use and create battery supply chains with less control by China.

mentions.heading: Changes to advanced manufacturing production tax credit for batteries
mentions.detail: Battery production credit restricted by prohibited foreign entity rules; years to comply with new criteria for U.S. battery plants
mentions.quote: The 2025 legislation preserved the advanced manufacturing production tax credit for the domestic manufacture of batteries and battery components (first established in the 2022 legislation), but restricted the eligibility criteria going forward, most notably by imposing criteria for “prohibited foreign entities,” which concern China and other countries.

mentions.heading: Access to debt, securitization, or derivative markets could be affected by downgrades or disruption
mentions.risk_name: Funding access and credit rating downgrade
mentions.detail: Ford Credit relies on unsecured funding, committed ABS programs and derivatives; reduced originations would hurt vehicle sales support
mentions.quote: A significant reduction in the amount of receivables Ford Credit purchases or originates would significantly reduce its ongoing results of operations and could adversely affect its ability to support the sale of Ford vehicles.

mentions.heading: An increasing interest rate environment may have an adverse effect on borrowing costs for Ford Credit
mentions.detail: Ford Credit captive finance arm funding costs; higher rates may be passed to customers
mentions.quote: An increasing interest rate environment may have an adverse effect on borrowing costs for Ford Credit, making it more expensive to fund our operations or leading to higher rates charged to our customers if these costs are passed on.

mentions.heading: Ford Credit could experience higher-than-expected credit losses
mentions.detail: Ford Credit customer and dealer defaults tied to unemployment, consumer debt, dealer profitability, used car prices
mentions.quote: Credit risk (which is heavily dependent upon economic factors including unemployment, consumer debt service burden, personal income growth, dealer profitability, and used car prices) has a significant impact on Ford Credit’s business.

mentions.heading: Lower-than-anticipated residual values or higher return volumes for leased vehicles
mentions.detail: Lease returns affected by auction values, propulsion technology changes and related regulation
mentions.quote: If auction values decrease significantly in the future, return volumes could exceed Ford Credit’s expectations.

mentions.heading: Pension and OPEB experience could be worse than Ford has assumed
mentions.detail: Year-end mark-to-market of pension/OPEB on discount rates, asset returns, mortality could produce substantial losses
mentions.quote: To the extent actual results are less favorable than our assumptions, we may recognize a remeasurement loss in our results, which could be substantial.

mentions.heading: Pension and other postretirement liabilities could adversely affect Ford’s liquidity
mentions.detail: US defined benefit plans, non-US pensions mainly Europe, retiree health OPEB; may force capex cuts, dividend suspension, refinancing
mentions.quote: If our cash flows and capital resources are insufficient to meet any pension or OPEB obligations, we could be forced to reduce or delay investments and capital expenditures, suspend dividend payments, seek additional capital, or restructure or refinance our indebtedness.

mentions.heading: Ford and Ford Credit could experience significant litigation, investigations, or adverse publicity
mentions.detail: Past violations by affiliated individuals caused civil or criminal liability; product defect, safety, environmental, financial regulation exposure
mentions.quote: We spend substantial resources to comply with governmental safety regulations, environmental regulatory obligations concerning our products and operations, consumer and automotive financial regulations, labor and employment regulations and practices, and other standards, but we have experienced employees, contractors, agents, and other individuals affiliated with us violating such laws or regulations from time to time, which at times has resulted in civil or criminal liability, and we cannot ensure that any such violations have not occurred or will not occur in the future, which may further result in civil or criminal liability.

mentions.heading: Government investigations have resulted in fines, penalties, orders, or oversight
mentions.detail: 2024 NHTSA consent order requires independent third party monitoring Safety Act adherence and reporting progress
mentions.quote: For example, as part of a consent order we entered into with NHTSA in 2024, we have retained an independent third party selected by NHTSA to assess the Company’s adherence to the consent order and Safety Act over the term of the consent order and to report on Ford’s progress to NHTSA.

mentions.heading: Litigation and class actions despite regulatory compliance
mentions.detail: Larger jury verdicts, punitive damages, growing international class actions; insurance may be insufficient
mentions.quote: Furthermore, regulatory investigations and litigation, including class actions, are becoming more prevalent in some international markets, potentially leading to increasing fines, damage awards, and settlement costs. While we have an insurance program that provides coverage for certain claims, it may not be sufficient to cover the losses incurred.

mentions.heading: Need to modify product plans and facilities to comply with shifting regulations
mentions.detail: US rollback of GHG/EV rules vs California ZEV mandates; 2025 federal law ending state authority under challenge
mentions.quote: In parallel, California continues to enact increasingly strict emissions standards and requirements for ZEVs (standards that some other states are adopting), and those actions are also the subject of legal challenges. In 2025, federal legislation, which is currently subject to challenge, eliminated the authority of California and other states to implement and enforce most of their standards and ZEV sales requirements.

mentions.heading: Local content and import requirements
mentions.detail: Governments regulate local product content or impose import requirements to protect domestic producers
mentions.quote: In addition, many governments regulate local product content or impose import requirements with the aim of creating jobs, protecting domestic producers, and influencing the balance of payments.

mentions.heading: Limits to ability to reduce emissions and increase fuel economy over given time frames
mentions.detail: Electrification core to compliance; low fuel prices and weak EV adoption could constrain sales of profitable ICE vehicles
mentions.quote: If fuel prices are relatively low and market conditions or the consumer attributes of our vehicles do not lead consumers to purchase electrified vehicles and other highly fuel-efficient vehicles in sufficient numbers, it may be difficult to meet applicable environmental standards in various markets and may constrain our ability to sell internal combustion engine vehicles, including some of the more profitable vehicles in our portfolio.

mentions.heading: Regulatory compliance credit purchase agreements
mentions.detail: Credit purchase agreements depend on seller delivery; purchases may be significant cash; credits already written off after policy changes
mentions.quote: If the seller under a credit purchase agreement does not deliver the credits contracted for, it may cause us to be out of compliance with emissions standards or other requirements. Such noncompliance may result in fines, penalties, or other costs, and/or we may need to modify our product plans and be unable to sell certain products.

mentions.heading: EV growth and disruptions may force product plan changes or credit purchases
mentions.detail: EV growth rates, stop ships, supply limits may require credit purchases (already done) to meet ZEV and fuel economy rules
mentions.quote: Moreover, the rates of EV growth, production disruptions, stop ships, supply chain limitations, lower-than-planned market acceptance of our vehicles, and/or other circumstances may cause us to modify product plans, or, in some cases, purchase credits, which we have done, in order to comply with emissions standards, fuel economy standards, or ZEV requirements, which could have an adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations and cause reputational harm.

mentions.heading: Increased regulatory scrutiny of automaker emission compliance
mentions.detail: Stricter enforcement, field actions, approval delays; criminal liability possible in some jurisdictions; third-party vehicle testing
mentions.quote: Increased scrutiny of automaker emission compliance by regulators around the world has led to new regulations, more stringent enforcement programs, additional field actions, demands for reporting on the field performance of emissions components and higher scrutiny of field data, and delays in regulatory approvals.

mentions.heading: Autonomous vehicle and driver assist regulation and scrutiny
mentions.detail: NHTSA and NTSB information requests about BlueCruise; state patchwork rules; crash reporting could lead to recalls, fines
mentions.quote: Further, autonomous vehicle and driver assist technologies continue to be scrutinized by the government and consumers, and actual or perceived failures or misuse of these technologies and features have led to government investigations and inquiries, including of Ford, which has responded to information requests from NHTSA and the National Transportation Safety Board about our BlueCruise system.

mentions.heading: Ford and Ford Credit could be affected by more stringent privacy, data and AI laws
mentions.detail: Privacy, data access and AI laws across US and other countries; vendor liability; AI adoption intensifies risk
mentions.quote: The rapid evolution and increased adoption of artificial intelligence technologies may intensify these risks.

mentions.heading: Ford Credit could be subject to new or increased credit and consumer protection regulations
mentions.detail: Ford Credit subject to Truth-in-Lending, Consumer Leasing, Equal Credit Opportunity, Fair Credit Reporting Acts
mentions.quote: In the United States, for example, Ford Credit’s operations are subject to regulation and supervision under various federal, state, and local laws, including the federal Truth-in-Lending Act, Consumer Leasing Act, Equal Credit Opportunity Act, and Fair Credit Reporting Act.

mentions.heading: CFPB supervision of Ford Credit under Dodd-Frank
mentions.detail: CFPB supervises Ford Credit as large nonbank auto lender; possible consent orders, customer remuneration, fines
mentions.quote: The CFPB has authority to supervise and examine the largest nonbank automotive finance companies, such as Ford Credit, for compliance with consumer financial protection laws.

mentions.heading: We may experience issues or delays in developing, launching and ramping the production of our products, services and features
mentions.risk_name: Product launch and production ramp delays
mentions.detail: Depends on autonomous driving, Cybercab Robotaxi, mass-market vehicles, Bots; past ramp bottlenecks; cost and profitability targets at risk
mentions.quote: In particular, our future business depends on development of our driver assistance systems and autonomous driving solutions and increasing the production of mass-market vehicles, including Cybercab, our purpose-built Robotaxi product.

mentions.heading: AI development challenges including energy and processing power for data centers
mentions.detail: AI services face energy availability and cost, processing power limitations and substantial data center power requirements
mentions.quote: In addition, as we continue to develop our artificial intelligence services and products, we may face many additional challenges, including the availability and cost of energy, processing power limitations and the substantial power requirements for our data centers.

mentions.heading: Dependence on global suppliers including single-source suppliers for components
mentions.detail: Thousands of parts from hundreds of suppliers incl. single-source; supplier insolvency, allocation, localization at new factories
mentions.quote: Our products contain thousands of parts purchased globally from hundreds of suppliers, including single-source direct suppliers, which exposes us to multiple potential sources of component shortages.

mentions.heading: Dependence on global suppliers including single-source suppliers for components
mentions.detail: 2025 U.S. trade policy changes, heightened tariffs and retaliatory export controls raised supply chain costs
mentions.quote: U.S. trade policy alterations in 2025, including heightened import tariffs and subsequent retaliatory measures, have impacted our supply chain costs, and may impact the availability of certain technologies or components, depending on the exact scope of the tariffs ultimately implemented and retaliatory export controls.

mentions.heading: Dependence on global suppliers including single-source suppliers for components
