mentions.detail: AI advances demand exponentially greater compute, memory, energy and thermal resources that may be insufficient or unaffordable
mentions.quote: For example, as companies, including Tesla, have made rapid advancements in AI in recent years, such innovation demands exponentially greater compute, memory, energy and thermal resources, which may prove insufficient in scale or affordability to meet our requirements.

mentions.heading: Dependence on global suppliers including single-source suppliers for components
mentions.detail: May fail to negotiate supplier cost reductions amid rising materials pricing
mentions.quote: Additionally, we may be unsuccessful in our continuous efforts to negotiate with existing suppliers to obtain cost reductions and avoid unfavorable changes to terms, source less expensive suppliers for certain parts and redesign certain parts to make them less expensive to produce, especially in the case of increases in materials pricing.

mentions.quote: For example, as a result of the rapidly evolving trade policies and tariff actions, the uncertainty in the automotive industry has increased, which could adversely affect our business and financial results.

mentions.heading: The cyclical nature of automotive sales and production can adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Business tied to automotive OEM vehicle production; lower global auto sales directly cut earnings and cash flows
mentions.quote: Lower global automotive sales would be expected to result in substantially all of our automotive OEM customers lowering vehicle production schedules, which has a direct impact on our earnings and cash flows.

mentions.heading: Economic declines reducing automotive sales and production
mentions.detail: 2025 global production +4% (Aptiv-weighted +1%); China +10%, North America -2%, Europe -1%; could force plant shutdowns, impairments
mentions.quote: Global automotive vehicle production increased 4% from 2024 to 2025 (1% on an Aptiv weighted market basis, which represents global vehicle production weighted to the geographic regions in which the Company generates its revenue), reflecting increased vehicle production of 10% in China and 1% in South America, our smallest region, partially offset by declines of 2% in North America and 1% in Europe.

mentions.heading: OEM inventory and production level fluctuations
mentions.detail: Sales depend on unpredictable OEM inventory and production level decisions
mentions.quote: Our sales are also affected by inventory levels and OEMs’ production levels. We cannot predict when OEMs will decide to increase or decrease inventory levels or whether new inventory levels will approximate historical inventory levels.

mentions.heading: Downturn could require additional financing that may not be available
mentions.detail: Prolonged auto downturn or credit market instability may require external financing on unfavorable terms
mentions.quote: Any significant negative cash flow or instability in the global credit markets and global economic pressure could limit our ability to obtain external financing on favorable terms. There can be no assurance that we would be able to secure such financing on terms acceptable to us, or at all.

mentions.heading: Impairment charges from deteriorating conditions and market capitalization
mentions.risk_name: Asset impairment and tax valuation charges
mentions.detail: Downturn could cause plant shutdowns, impairments, restructuring, deferred tax valuation allowance changes
mentions.quote: Any such adverse impacts could require us to shut down plants or result in impairment charges, restructuring actions or changes in our valuation allowances against deferred tax assets, which could be material to our financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: A drop in the market share and changes in product mix offered by our customers can impact our revenues.
mentions.detail: Dependent on automotive OEM customers; loss if demand shifts to models without Aptiv supply contracts
mentions.quote: For instance, a shift in sales demand favoring a particular OEMs’ vehicle model for which we do not have a supply contract may negatively impact our revenue.

mentions.heading: OEM delays in electrification strategies
mentions.detail: High voltage electrification a key market; OEMs delaying software-defined vehicle investment amid weaker demand
mentions.quote: For example, while we have identified high voltage electrification systems as a key product market, certain of our OEM customers have recently announced delays in or changes to their software-defined vehicle investment strategies amidst reduced expectations for future consumer demand for these products, which could adversely impact the growth of this product market within our business.

mentions.heading: Maintaining a strong position in the Chinese market
mentions.risk_name: Customer market share loss in key market
mentions.detail: Domestic Chinese OEMs gaining share; GM restructured China operations in 2025; traditional OEMs among largest customers
mentions.quote: For example, in 2025, General Motors (“GM”) restructured their operations in China given challenges in the Chinese market. As GM, along with other traditional OEMs, are among our largest customers, our business and financial results may be adversely affected by decreases in their

mentions.heading: Maintaining a strong position in the Chinese market
mentions.detail: Moderating Chinese economic growth lowered automotive production growth; exposure to China vehicle demand
mentions.quote: Our business in China is sensitive to economic and market conditions that drive automotive sales volumes in China and may be impacted if there are reductions in vehicle demand in China.

mentions.heading: Highly competitive automotive technology and component supply industry
mentions.detail: New disruptive entrants from China and in automated driving and software; OEM consolidation; past resourcing to competitors
mentions.quote: Furthermore, the rapidly evolving nature of the markets in which we compete has attracted, and may continue to attract, new and disruptive entrants from outside the traditional automotive supply industry, particularly in countries such as China or in areas of evolving vehicle technologies such as automated driving technologies and advanced software.

mentions.heading: Evolution toward autonomous vehicles and mobility on demand
mentions.detail: High development cost of active safety and autonomous driving; car- and ride-sharing may reduce vehicles per capita
mentions.quote: There has also been an increase in consumer preferences for mobility on demand services, such as car- and ride-sharing, as opposed to automobile ownership, which may result in a long-term reduction in the number of vehicles per capita.

mentions.heading: Future growth depends on making the right investments at the right time
mentions.detail: Substantial investments targeting China/Asia Pacific and ADAS, autonomous driving, software, high voltage electrification; losses possible if markets underperform
mentions.quote: If we are unable to deepen existing and develop additional customer relationships in the Asia Pacific region, or if we are unable to develop and introduce market-relevant advanced driver assistance or autonomous driving technologies, we may not only fail to realize expected rates of return on our existing investments, but we may incur losses on such investments and be unable to timely redeploy the invested capital to take advantage of other markets or product categories, potentially resulting in lost market share to our competitors.

mentions.heading: We may not be able to respond quickly enough to changes in regulations, technology and to develop IP into viable products.
mentions.detail: Disruptive technologies like autonomous driving, ADAS and alternative-fuel vehicles; innovation requires extensive capital investment
mentions.quote: Our ability to respond to competitive pressures and react quickly to other major changes in the marketplace, including the potential introduction of disruptive technologies such as autonomous driving solutions or consumer desire for and availability of vehicles with advanced driver assistance technologies or which use alternative fuels is also a risk to our future financial performance.

mentions.heading: Changes in regulations may render products obsolete
mentions.detail: DOT guidance on automated driving systems; possible pre-approval requirements and divergent jurisdictional rules
mentions.quote: There remains potential for the continued introduction of new and expanded regulations in this space, including potential requirements for autonomous vehicle systems to receive approval from the DOT or other regulatory agencies prior to commercial introduction. It is also possible that regulations in this space may diverge among jurisdictions, leading to increased compliance costs.

mentions.heading: Failure to launch new product programs on schedule
mentions.detail: Equipment certification and facility transitions for new programs; dependence on customer launch schedules
mentions.quote: Our failure to successfully launch new products, or a failure by our customers to successfully launch new programs, could adversely affect our results.

mentions.heading: Certain of our businesses rely on collaborative partners and third-parties for product development, which could fail to perform.
mentions.detail: Partners may underinvest, be acquired, compete, or not renew; could delay or cancel development programs
mentions.quote: If we or any of our collaborative partners terminate a collaborative arrangement, we may be required to devote additional resources to product development and commercialization or may need to cancel certain development programs, which could adversely affect our business and operational results.

mentions.heading: Dependence on five largest customers
mentions.detail: Five largest customers ~42% of 2025 net sales; GM, Ford, Stellantis among largest
mentions.quote: Our five largest customers accounted for approximately 42% of our total net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025. Accordingly, our revenues may be adversely affected by decreases in any of their businesses or market share.

mentions.heading: Dependence on five largest customers
mentions.detail: Worldwide semiconductor shortage cut vehicle production, hurting 2023 results
mentions.quote: For instance, the worldwide semiconductor shortage adversely impacted the automotive industry in recent years resulting in reduced vehicle production schedules and sales from historical levels, which adversely impacted our financial condition, operating results and cash flows for portions of the year ended December 31, 2023.

mentions.heading: Dependence on five largest customers
mentions.detail: UAW strikes at GM, Ford, Stellantis Sept 2023 lasting over six weeks hurt 2023 results
mentions.quote: In addition, certain United Automobile, Aerospace and Agricultural Implement Workers of America (“UAW”) represented employees at GM, Ford Motor Company (“Ford”) and Stellantis N.V. (“Stellantis”) initiated labor strikes in September 2023, lasting more than six weeks in duration.

mentions.heading: We may not realize sales represented by awarded business.
mentions.detail: Awarded business based on projected volumes; customers don't guarantee volumes and can terminate without penalty
mentions.quote: Our customers generally do not guarantee volumes. In addition, awarded business may include business under arrangements that our customers have the right to terminate without penalty.

mentions.heading: Continued pricing pressures, OEM cost reduction initiatives and re-sourcing may lower margins
mentions.detail: Supply agreements require annual price step-downs of 1-3%; Tier I supplier facing OEM leverage
mentions.quote: Our customer supply agreements generally require step-downs in component pricing over the period of production, typically one to three percent per year.

mentions.heading: Requirements contracts expose revenues to decline in OEM production
mentions.detail: OEMs buy requirements without minimums; contracts 1 year to model life (3-7 years), terminable for convenience
mentions.quote: In most instances our OEM customers agree to purchase their requirements for specific products but are not required to purchase any minimum amount of products from us.

mentions.heading: Difficulties launching new programs to customers' timing, performance and quality standards
mentions.detail: Automotive program launches depend on customer design changes, tooling readiness, skilled labor; failures may trigger commercial or litigation claims and reputational harm
mentions.quote: Given the complexity of new program launches, we may experience difficulties managing product quality, timeliness and associated costs. Failure by us to successfully launch a new product could result in commercial or litigation claims against us which could have a material adverse effect on our profitability.

mentions.heading: New program launch costs ahead of customer vehicle introductions
mentions.detail: Significant cost ramp for new programs while sales depend on timing and success of customers' new vehicle introductions
mentions.quote: In addition, new program launches require a significant ramp up of costs; however, our sales related to these new programs generally are dependent upon the timing and success of our customers’ introduction of new vehicles.

mentions.heading: Adverse developments affecting one or more of our suppliers could harm our profitability.
mentions.detail: Sole-source suppliers may fail under commodity cost volatility or volume swings, causing delays or non-conforming products
mentions.quote: Any significant disruption in our supplier relationships, particularly relationships with sole-source suppliers, could harm our profitability. Some of our suppliers may not be able to handle commodity cost volatility and/or sharply changing volumes while still performing as we expect.

mentions.heading: Discontinuation or loss of business for a product where we are a significant supplier
mentions.detail: Purchase orders cover annual or life-of-model requirements, not fixed quantities; OEM customers may in-source components
mentions.quote: If our OEM customers successfully in-source products currently manufactured by us, the discontinuation or loss of business for products which we are a significant supplier could reduce our sales and harm our profitability.

mentions.heading: Increases in costs of the materials and other supplies that we use in our products may have a negative impact on our business.
mentions.detail: Copper, resin, semiconductors, fuel price swings; limited pass-through especially with U.S. OEMs; demand driven by China
mentions.quote: In recent periods there have been significant fluctuations in the global prices of copper, petroleum-based resin products, semiconductors and fuel charges, which have had and may continue to have an unfavorable impact on our business, results of operations or financial condition.

mentions.heading: Our hedging activities to address commodity price fluctuations may not be successful
mentions.detail: Hedges only near-term raw material exposure; no protection from long-term price increases
mentions.quote: Our hedging activities are not designed to mitigate long-term commodity price fluctuations and, therefore, will not protect from long-term commodity price increases.

mentions.heading: We may encounter manufacturing challenges.
mentions.detail: Customers do not commit to long-term production schedules, hampering capacity utilization
mentions.quote: Due in part to these factors, many of our customers do not commit to long-term production schedules. Our inability to forecast the level of customer orders with certainty makes it difficult to schedule production and maximize utilization of manufacturing capacity.

mentions.heading: We may encounter manufacturing challenges.
mentions.detail: Relies on third-party suppliers and contract manufacturers for components, assemblies and finished products
mentions.quote: We rely on third-party suppliers for components used in our products, and we rely on third-party manufacturers to manufacture certain of our assemblies and finished products.

mentions.heading: Underutilized manufacturing lines and excess capacity
mentions.detail: Underutilized manufacturing lines raise fixed costs; some lines in China face rising labor costs and instability
mentions.quote: This excess capacity means we incur increased fixed costs in our products relative to the net revenue we generate, which could have an adverse effect on our results of operations, particularly during economic downturns.

mentions.heading: Changes in factors that impact the determination of our non-U.S. pension liabilities may adversely affect us.
mentions.detail: Mexico and UK plans underfunded by $128 million; non-U.S. pension and retirement obligations net $423 million at Dec 31, 2025
mentions.quote: Our primary funded non-U.S. plans are located in Mexico and the United Kingdom and were underfunded by $128 million as of December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: We may suffer future asset impairment and other restructuring charges
mentions.detail: Ongoing restructuring to realign production capacity and cost structure; may not achieve desired results
mentions.quote: Charges related to these actions or any further restructuring actions may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition. We cannot ensure that any current or future restructuring actions will be completed as planned or achieve the desired results.

mentions.heading: We may suffer future asset impairment and other restructuring charges
mentions.detail: Q3 2025 $648 million goodwill impairment on Wind River reporting unit due to higher discount rates and lower forecast cash flows
mentions.quote: The assessment indicated that the carrying value of this reporting unit exceeded its estimated fair value, and as a result, during the third quarter of 2025, the Company recorded a non-cash, pre-tax goodwill impairment charge of approximately $648 million related to the Wind River reporting unit.

mentions.heading: Labor-intensive business with unions; strikes or work disruptions could hurt operations
mentions.detail: Unionized, works council workforce; customer plant strikes matter—UAW strikes at GM, Ford, Stellantis in September 2023 lasted over six weeks
mentions.quote: In addition, certain UAW-represented employees at GM, Ford and Stellantis initiated labor strikes in September 2023, lasting more than six weeks in duration.

mentions.heading: Labor strikes and collective bargaining at customers and suppliers
mentions.risk_name: Labor strikes and union cost pressure
mentions.detail: GM, Ford and Stellantis strikes hurt 2023 results; CBA renegotiation could raise labor costs
mentions.quote: GM, Ford and Stellantis are among our largest customers, these labor strikes adversely impacted our financial condition, operating results and cash flows for the year ended December 31, 2023.

mentions.heading: Public health crises could adversely impact our business
mentions.detail: References COVID-19; no prolonged plant shutdowns in 2023-2025
mentions.quote: A significant public health crisis, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, could adversely impact our business as well as those of our suppliers and customers.

mentions.heading: Exposure to foreign currency fluctuations from global operations
mentions.detail: About 64% of 2025 revenue outside U.S.; key exposures Euro, Chinese Yuan, Mexican Peso
mentions.quote: Accordingly, significant changes in currency exchange rates, particularly the Euro, Chinese Yuan (Renminbi) and Mexican Peso, could cause fluctuations in the reported results of our businesses’ operations that could negatively affect our results of operations.

mentions.heading: Risks associated with doing business in various jurisdictions
mentions.detail: Most plants in Mexico, China, Asia Pacific, Europe, South America, Northern Africa; Ukraine-Russia, Middle East conflicts
mentions.quote: The majority of our manufacturing and distribution facilities are in Mexico, China and other countries in Asia Pacific, Eastern and Western Europe, South America and Northern Africa.

mentions.heading: Trade barriers and tariffs on global operations
mentions.detail: Tariffs, quotas, sanctions and export restrictions across global manufacturing footprint
mentions.quote: •tariffs, quotas, customs and other import or export restrictions and other trade barriers;

mentions.heading: Anti-bribery compliance in global operations
mentions.detail: Subject to U.S. FCPA, U.K. Bribery Act and similar laws
mentions.quote: •compliance with the requirements of an increasing body of applicable anti-bribery laws, including the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the U.K. Bribery Act and similar laws of various other countries.

mentions.heading: Mexico labor reforms increasing labor costs
mentions.risk_name: Labor cost inflation from wage regulation
mentions.detail: Mexico minimum wage up ~13%, 12%, 20% in 2026/2025/2024; proposed 48-to-40 hour work week from 2027
mentions.quote: The government of Mexico has indicated it may implement other labor reforms, such as an initiative to shorten the work week from 48 to 40 hours, as early as January 1, 2027, through a gradual reduction of two hours per year.

mentions.heading: Changes in trade laws and tariffs on imports
mentions.detail: Manufacturing in China and Mexico; USMCA benefits; U.S. tariffs of at least 10% from April 2, 2025 and retaliation
mentions.quote: Changes in laws or policies governing the terms of trade, and in particular increased trade restrictions, tariffs, taxes or non-tariff barriers on imports from countries where we manufacture products, such as China and Mexico, could have a material adverse effect on our business and financial results.

mentions.heading: Armed conflicts in the Middle East
mentions.detail: Middle East conflicts since October 2023 could spread and affect global economy and supply chains
mentions.quote: The outbreak of armed conflicts in the Middle East beginning in October 2023 has also created numerous uncertainties, including the risk that the conflicts spread throughout the broader region, and their impact on the global economy and supply chains.

mentions.heading: Russia-Ukraine conflict and sanctions
mentions.detail: E.U. and U.S. sanctions on Russia; possible Russian retaliation incl. energy restrictions, asset expropriation
mentions.quote: While the sanctions announced to date have not had a material adverse impact on us, any further sanctions imposed or actions taken by these countries, and any retaliatory measures by Russia in response, including restrictions on energy supplies from Russia to countries in the region and asset expropriations, could increase our costs, reduce our sales and earnings or otherwise have an adverse effect on our operations.

mentions.heading: Raw material supply from Ukraine and Russia
mentions.detail: Copper, aluminum, palladium and neon gases sourced from Ukraine/Russia; price volatility and logistics costs
mentions.quote: Ukraine and Russia are significant global producers of raw materials used in our supply chain, including copper, aluminum, palladium and neon gases.

mentions.heading: European economic weakness from the conflict
mentions.detail: Europe ~32% of 2025 net sales; $11 million Ukraine asset impairment in 2023
mentions.quote: However, the impacts of the conflict have adversely impacted, and may continue to adversely impact, global economies, and in particular, the European economy, a region which accounted for approximately 32% of our net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: Expanding manufacturing footprint in Asian markets including China
mentions.detail: Strategy grows footprint in China, Asia and lower-cost regions, increasing exposure to geopolitical and country risks
mentions.quote: Increasing our manufacturing footprint in Asian markets, including China, and our business relationships with Asian automotive manufacturers are important elements of our long-term strategy. In addition, our strategy includes increasing revenue and expanding our manufacturing footprint in lower-cost regions. As a result, our exposure to the risks described above may be greater in the future.

mentions.heading: Failure to manage growth or integrate acquisitions could harm business
mentions.detail: Acquired Wind River and Intercable Automotive Solutions in 2022; continues pursuing possibly material deals
mentions.quote: We have completed a number of acquisitions in recent years, including the acquisitions of Wind River and Intercable Automotive Solutions S.r.l. in 2022.

mentions.heading: Failure to manage growth or integrate acquisitions could harm business
mentions.detail: Failure to integrate acquired companies profitably may impair goodwill and intangibles
mentions.quote: Likewise, our failure to integrate and manage acquired companies profitably may lead to future impairment of any associated goodwill and intangible asset balances.

mentions.heading: Cybersecurity risks for infrastructure and products
mentions.detail: Covers infrastructure and products; AI-enabled attacks and remote work raise vulnerability
mentions.quote: Cyberattacks are continually increasing in their frequency, sophistication and intensity. Additionally, some actors are using artificial intelligence technology to launch more automated, targeted and coordinated attacks which further heightens these risks.

mentions.heading: Cyberattacks targeting connected vehicle products
mentions.detail: Safety-critical products with complex digital technologies for connected vehicles may be targeted by cyberattacks, harming brand and customers
mentions.quote: Some of our products, including but not limited to safety-critical products, contain complex digital technologies designed to support today’s increasingly connected vehicles.

mentions.heading: Cybersecurity breaches and IT system failures (continued)
mentions.detail: Generic statement; no material breach to date; Board oversight
mentions.quote: While we continuously seek to expand and improve our information technology systems and maintain adequate disclosure controls and procedures, there can be no assurance that we can adequately anticipate all trends of the market, technology landscapes and threat landscapes, and there can be no assurance that such measures will prevent interruptions or security breaches that could adversely affect our business.

mentions.heading: We may incur material losses and costs as a result of warranty claims, product recalls, product liability and intellectual property infringement actions
mentions.detail: Complex fabrication; product flaws could cause re-work, replacement costs, lost revenue and order cancellations
mentions.quote: If flaws in either the design or manufacture of our products were to occur, we could experience a rate of failure in our products that could result in significant delays in shipment and product re-work or replacement costs.

mentions.heading: We may incur material losses and costs as a result of warranty claims, product recalls, product liability and intellectual property infringement actions
mentions.detail: OEMs seek supplier contribution for recalls; global vehicle recalls above historical levels; NHTSA can mandate recalls
mentions.quote: However, as suppliers become more integrally involved in the vehicle design process and assume more of the vehicle assembly functions, OEMs continue to look to their suppliers for contribution when faced with recalls and product liability claims. The number of vehicles recalled globally by OEMs has increased above historical levels.

mentions.heading: We may incur material losses and costs as a result of warranty claims, product recalls, product liability and intellectual property infringement actions
mentions.detail: OEMs may hold company responsible for repair/replacement under new vehicle warranties; final amounts may differ from reserves
mentions.quote: Depending on the terms under which we supply products to a vehicle manufacturer, a vehicle manufacturer may attempt to hold us responsible for some or all of the repair or replacement costs of products under new vehicle warranties when the OEM asserts that the product supplied did not perform as warranted.

mentions.heading: We may incur material losses and costs as a result of warranty claims, product recalls, product liability and intellectual property infringement actions
mentions.detail: Adoption of new technology raises exposure to third-party IP infringement claims
mentions.quote: In addition, as we adopt new technology, we face an inherent risk of exposure to the claims of others that we have allegedly violated their intellectual property rights.

mentions.heading: We may be adversely affected by laws or regulations, including environmental, health and safety and climate change
mentions.detail: Customers affected by curtailment of U.S. government incentives for electric and hybrid vehicles
mentions.quote: For example, certain of our customers may be affected by the curtailment in the United States of government incentives for electric and hybrid vehicles.

mentions.heading: We may be adversely affected by laws or regulations, including environmental, health and safety and climate change
mentions.detail: Cleanup at multiple present and former facilities; environmental reserves about $4 million at December 31, 2025 may be exceeded
mentions.quote: While we have environmental reserves of approximately $4 million at December 31, 2025 for the cleanup of presently-known environmental contamination conditions, it cannot be guaranteed that actual costs will not significantly exceed these reserves.

mentions.heading: We may be adversely affected by laws or regulations, including environmental, health and safety and climate change
mentions.detail: Greenhouse gas rules could require emission controls, credits, raise energy costs; sustainability goal shortfall reputational risk
mentions.quote: For example, adoption of greenhouse gas or climate change rules in jurisdictions in which we operate facilities could require installation of emission controls, acquisition of emission credits, emission reductions, or other measures that could be costly, and could also impact utility rates and increase the amount we spend annually for energy.

mentions.heading: Additional environmental remediation or demolition obligations from facility divestiture and closure
mentions.detail: Facility sales, closures and demolitions worldwide may uncover unknown contamination; costs may exceed reserves
mentions.quote: We may identify previously unknown environmental conditions or further delineate known conditions that may require us to undertake remediation or incur additional costs related to demolition or decommissioning activities. Such costs may exceed our current reserves.

mentions.heading: Legal proceedings and commercial or contractual disputes
mentions.detail: Warranty claims and disputes with customers and suppliers, IP, personal injury, EHS, tax, employment matters
mentions.quote: While we believe our reserves are adequate, the final amounts required to resolve these matters could differ materially from our recorded estimates and our results of operations could be materially affected.

mentions.heading: Developments or assertions relating to intellectual property rights
mentions.detail: Large patent and trade name portfolio and numerous licensing arrangements; technological developments by others
mentions.quote: Developments or assertions by or against us relating to intellectual property rights could negatively impact our business. Significant technological developments by others also could materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Taxing authorities could challenge historical and future tax positions
mentions.risk_name: Tax law change and rate increase
mentions.detail: OECD Pillar Two, expiry of tax holidays/incentives, EU and G20 changes to income allocation
mentions.quote: Our future effective tax rates could be affected by changes in the mix of earnings in countries with differing statutory rates and changes in tax laws, or their interpretation, including the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (“OECD”) Pillar Two Framework, and changes related to tax holidays or tax incentives.

mentions.heading: Taxing authorities could challenge historical and future tax positions
mentions.detail: Tax authorities may interpret laws differently and assess additional taxes beyond uncertain tax reserves
mentions.quote: While we believe that we have complied with all applicable tax laws, there can be no assurance that a taxing authority will not have a different interpretation of the law and assess us with additional taxes.

mentions.heading: Changes in tax laws, tax rates and adverse positions taken by taxing authorities
mentions.detail: U.S. Congress action could override treaties or deem company U.S. resident; reliance on Switzerland tax treaties
mentions.quote: If proposals were enacted that had the effect of limiting our ability to take advantage of the tax treaties between Switzerland and other jurisdictions (including the United States), we could be subjected to increased taxation.

mentions.heading: Our tax burden could increase as a result of ongoing or future tax audits.
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Therefore, there can be no assurance that we will accurately predict the outcomes of any tax audit or other tax dispute or that issues raised by tax authorities will be resolved at a financial cost that does not exceed our related reserves.

mentions.heading: Our ability to use deferred tax assets may be subject to limitation.
mentions.detail: Generic statement; depends on taxable income in certain countries
mentions.quote: We have deferred tax assets in certain countries, and our ability to use such assets will depend on our taxable income generation in the relevant countries.

mentions.heading: We may be subject to various Swiss taxes as a result of the reorganization transaction.
mentions.detail: New Jersey parent tax-resident in Switzerland; up to ~15% effective rate in Schaffhausen in 2025 plus capital taxes
mentions.quote: The overall (federal, cantonal, communal) effective corporate income tax rate may vary, but amount to a maximum of approximately 15% in 2025 for companies resident in Schaffhausen, Switzerland, depending on the amount of taxable net profit and respective cantonal/communal multiplier.

mentions.heading: We may be subject to various Swiss taxes as a result of the reorganization transaction.
mentions.detail: 35% Swiss withholding on dividends/buybacks unless paid from capital contribution reserves, partly transferred to EDS business in Separation
mentions.quote: If it does not have qualifying capital contribution reserves (Reserven aus Kapitaleinlagen) and is not able to secure an efficient second virtual line of trading, then any dividends paid by Aptiv or share repurchases by Aptiv will generally be subject to a Swiss withholding tax at a rate of 35% which can be reduced depending on the tax residency of the dividend recipient.

mentions.heading: We may be subject to various Swiss taxes as a result of the reorganization transaction.
mentions.detail: 1% Swiss issuance stamp tax on share issuances and equity increases; also VAT and securities transfer stamp tax
mentions.quote: Finally, Aptiv is also subject to a Swiss issuance stamp tax levied at a rate of 1% on the fair value of share issuances and increases of our equity, other than in connection with qualifying restructurings like the Transaction.

mentions.heading: The proposed Separation is contingent upon conditions, may not be completed on timeline, or at all, and may not achieve intended benefits
mentions.detail: Planned spin-off of Electrical Distribution Systems as Versigent; about $178 million separation costs in 2025, incurred even if not completed
mentions.quote: We have incurred, and expect to continue to incur, significant expenses in connection with the Separation, a significant portion of which has already been incurred or will be incurred even if the Separation is not completed, including costs of approximately $178 million during the year ended December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: Separated companies will be smaller and less diversified
mentions.detail: Post-Separation Aptiv and Versigent smaller, concentrated in industries, lose shared costs and face standalone public-company costs
mentions.quote: As a result, each company could be more vulnerable to global economic trends, geopolitical risks, demand or supply shocks, and changing industry or market conditions, which could have a material adverse effect on its business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.

mentions.heading: If distribution of Versigent shares fails to qualify as tax-free, subsidiaries and shareholders could face significant tax liabilities
mentions.detail: Relies on tax opinions under Code Section 355(a)(1); no IRS ruling sought; also intended tax-free for Swiss purposes
mentions.quote: We do not intend to seek a ruling from the Internal Revenue Service (the “IRS”) with respect to the U.S. federal income tax treatment of the Separation.

drivers.name: Section 355(a)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code

mentions.heading: Separation from Versigent may not qualify as tax-free
mentions.detail: IRS could deem Versigent Separation taxable under Section 355; subsidiaries and U.S. holders face significant tax liabilities
mentions.quote: In addition, certain of our subsidiaries could be subject to U.S. federal income tax if the Separation and/or certain related transactions were determined not to qualify for non-recognition under Section 355 and related provisions of the Code. These amounts could be material, and could adversely affect our business, financial conditions, cash flows and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Versigent may fail to meet Tax Matters Agreement indemnification
mentions.detail: Reliance on Versigent indemnity under Tax Matters Agreement for taxes if its representations or covenants breached
mentions.quote: However, if Versigent fails to satisfy its indemnification obligations to us in respect of such taxes and expenses, our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations could be adversely affected.

mentions.heading: Any changes in consumer credit availability or cost of borrowing could adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Reduced consumer credit and higher borrowing costs depress global automotive sales and customer production volumes
mentions.quote: Declines in the availability of consumer credit and increases in consumer borrowing costs have negatively impacted global automotive sales and resulted in lower production volumes in the past.

mentions.heading: Banking sector volatility may impair credit availability
mentions.detail: Recent U.S. financial institution volatility hurt equity and credit markets; recurrence could restrict consumer credit
mentions.quote: Any reoccurrence of these conditions has the potential to adversely impact consumer credit availability or the cost of borrowing, which in turn could adversely impact our business.

mentions.heading: We may lose or fail to attract and retain key salaried employees and management personnel.
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: The loss of the services of any member of senior management or a key salaried employee could have an adverse effect on our business.

mentions.heading: Our portfolio strategy may prove unsuccessful.
mentions.detail: Significant investments in eProducts may fail to earn returns or incur losses if electric vehicle adoption stays slower than expected.
mentions.quote: If the overall adoption of electric vehicles continues to be slower as compared to our expectations, we may not only fail to realize expected rates of return on our existing investments, we may also incur further losses on such investments.

mentions.heading: Our portfolio strategy may prove unsuccessful.
mentions.detail: Ongoing pursuit of ventures, acquisitions and alliances; limited diligence information and inexact pricing.
mentions.quote: However, the amount of information we can obtain about a potential growth opportunity can be limited, and we can give no assurance that past or future business ventures, acquisitions, and strategic alliances will positively affect our financial performance or will perform as planned.

mentions.heading: Our portfolio strategy may prove unsuccessful.
mentions.detail: Shared control in joint ventures; partner defaults, conflicts and reduced FCPA compliance control.
mentions.quote: Additional risks associated with joint ventures include one or more partners failing to satisfy contractual obligations, the ability to enforce such obligations, conflicts arising between us and any of our partners, a change in the ownership of any of our partners and less of an ability to control compliance with applicable rules and regulations, including the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and related rules and regulations.

mentions.heading: Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets represent a significant portion of total assets; impairment could have material adverse impact.
mentions.detail: Impairment charges already recorded in 2025 and 2024; thin headroom after acquisitions.
mentions.quote: Any charges relating to such impairments, such as those recorded for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, could adversely affect our results of operations in the periods recognized.

mentions.heading: Success of acquisitions depends on realizing expected benefits from combining businesses
mentions.detail: Generic statement; integration of acquired businesses may fail to deliver synergies, cause unknown liabilities and costs
mentions.quote: If we are unsuccessful in combining companies, the anticipated benefits of the acquisitions may not be realized fully or at all or may take longer to realize than expected. Further, there is potential for unknown or inestimable liabilities relating to the acquired businesses.

mentions.heading: We may not be able to execute dispositions of assets or businesses successfully.
mentions.detail: Generic statement; buyer indemnities may not protect; negative synergies from separation possible
mentions.quote: We cannot be assured that any of these indemnification provisions will fully protect us, and, as a result, may face unexpected liabilities that adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: We may not be able to execute dispositions of assets or businesses successfully.
mentions.detail: Disposition closings require regulatory and governmental approvals in jurisdictions worldwide
mentions.quote: Such regulatory and governmental approvals may be required in jurisdictions around the world, and any delays in the timing of such approvals could materially delay or prevent the transaction.

mentions.heading: Conditions in the automotive industry may adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Depends on global automotive and truck production; sensitive to interest rates, consumer credit, trade issues
mentions.quote: Economic declines that result in significant reduction in automotive or truck production would result in a decline in the production levels of our major customers and, by extension, in our sales to OEMs which would adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Competition from global manufacturers and OEM insourcing
mentions.detail: Competitors include OEM vertically integrated units, well-funded start-ups and low-cost foreign suppliers; major OEMs intend to insource components
mentions.quote: Although many OEMs have indicated that they will continue to rely on outside suppliers, a number of major OEM customers have indicated their intent to insource certain components that we produce, and many do manufacture products for their own uses that directly compete with our products.

mentions.heading: If we do not respond appropriately, the evolution of the automotive industry could adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Shift to hybrid/electric vehicles, ADAS, autonomous driving, mobility-on-demand; need to innovate including AI and machine learning
mentions.quote: While we are focused on driving growth through our ability to capitalize on certain potential trends, such as the move toward hybrid and electric vehicles, some of the focuses and trends are not part of our product line or strategy.

mentions.heading: We may be subject to potential governmental investigations and related proceedings relating to vehicle emissions standards.
mentions.detail: Industry emissions-violation investigations could lead to recalls, fines, disgorgement, restricted offerings
mentions.quote: Any potential alleged violations by BorgWarner of existing or future emissions standards could result in government investigations and other legal proceedings, the recall of one or more of our products, negotiated remedial actions, fines, disgorgement of profits, restricted product offerings, reputational harm or a combination of any of those items.

mentions.heading: We are under substantial pressure from OEMs to reduce the prices of our products.
mentions.detail: OEMs demand annual price reductions; raw material and inflation cost recovery often under 100% and delayed
mentions.quote: Our ability to pass through increased raw material or other inflationary costs to our OEM customers is limited, with cost recovery often less than 100% and often on a delayed basis.

mentions.heading: Commodity cost increases and availability of raw materials
mentions.detail: Aluminum, copper, nickel, resins, steel, energy, castings, forgings; relies on pass-through provisions and selective hedging
mentions.quote: While we seek to alleviate the impact of increasing costs by including material pass-through provisions in our customer contracts wherever possible and by selectively hedging certain commodity exposures, we may not be successful in these efforts.

mentions.heading: Falling commodity prices may cause supply interruptions
mentions.detail: Rapid commodity price falls may lead suppliers, carriers and energy providers to withdraw capacity
mentions.quote: From time to time, commodity prices may also fall rapidly. If this happens, suppliers may withdraw capacity from the market until prices improve, which may cause periodic supply interruptions.

mentions.heading: Elevated inflation increases input costs
mentions.detail: Cost-recovery agreements in 2022-2024 did not recover 100% of increased costs, hurting margins
mentions.quote: Following non-contractual negotiations, we reached cost-recovery agreements with various customers in 2024, 2023 and 2022, but these agreements did not enable us to recover 100 percent of our increased costs, and as a result, our operating margins were negatively impacted.

mentions.heading: We may not achieve the expected benefits of our restructuring plans
mentions.detail: Ongoing capacity and cost realignment; risks of labor unrest, lost key employees, unrealized savings
mentions.quote: Implementation of any restructuring action may be costly and disruptive to our business, and we may not be able to realize the cost savings, operational improvements and estimated workforce reductions that we anticipate within the projected timing or at all.

mentions.heading: Changes in trade policy, including tariffs, may have an adverse effect
mentions.detail: 2025 U.S. tariffs on EU, Canada, Mexico, China raised material costs; Chinese retaliatory tariffs; recovery from customers uncertain
mentions.quote: In 2025, the U.S. announced significant tariffs on imports from a broad range of countries, including the European Union, Canada, Mexico and China. These tariffs have increased the cost of raw materials and components we purchase

mentions.heading: Trade policy, tariffs and USMCA renewal
mentions.detail: USMCA renewal due 2026; $918 million imported to U.S. in 2025, 68% from Mexico, 9% Canada, 6% South Korea
mentions.quote: In 2025, we imported approximately $918 million in value to the U.S. Approximately 68% of that value originated in Mexico, approximately 9% originated in Canada and approximately 6% originated in South Korea.

mentions.heading: U.S.-China relations and supply chain integration
mentions.detail: China integrated with key components in global supply chain; strained U.S.-China relations
mentions.quote: Also, China presents unique risks to U.S. automotive manufacturers due to the strain in U.S.-China relations and the level of integration with key components in our global supply chain.

mentions.heading: Inability to protect intellectual property or IP assertions
mentions.detail: Expansion into jurisdictions with weaker IP enforcement increases duplication risk
mentions.quote: Further, as we expand our operations in jurisdictions where the enforcement of intellectual property rights is less robust, the risk of others duplicating our proprietary technologies increases, despite efforts we undertake to protect them.

mentions.heading: Business continuity risks from centralized IT systems
mentions.detail: Regionally centralized invoicing, payroll and general management systems
mentions.quote: If the centralized systems are disrupted or disabled, key business processes could be interrupted, which could adversely affect our business.

mentions.heading: Failure or disruption of IT infrastructure including cybersecurity
mentions.detail: Has been subjected to attacks; none material to date; risks of production downtime and supply shortages
mentions.quote: Future attacks or disruptions could potentially lead to the inappropriate disclosure of confidential information, including our intellectual property or employee data, improper use of our systems and networks, access to and manipulation and destruction of our or third-party data, production downtimes, lost revenues, inappropriate disbursement of funds and both internal and external supply shortages.

mentions.heading: Cyber-attacks targeting connected vehicle products
mentions.detail: Products contain complex digital technologies for connected vehicles
mentions.quote: Additionally, some of our products contain complex digital technologies designed to support today’s increasingly connected vehicles.

mentions.heading: AI and information technology systems risks
mentions.detail: Incorporating AI into systems and product development; risks of IP loss, inaccurate outputs, and competitors using AI more effectively
mentions.quote: The use of AI in the development of our products and services could also cause loss or theft of intellectual property as well as subject us to risks related to intellectual property infringement or misappropriation, data privacy and cybersecurity.

mentions.heading: Our business success depends on attracting and retaining qualified personnel.
mentions.detail: Need for engineering, technical and software skilled employees worldwide
mentions.quote: In particular, any unplanned turnover or inability to attract and retain key employees and employees with engineering, technical and software capabilities in numbers sufficient for our needs could adversely affect our business.

mentions.heading: Our profitability and results of operations may be adversely affected by new business launch difficulties.
mentions.detail: Failed launches could delay or shut down customer vehicle production, triggering penalties and work shifting to competitors
mentions.quote: To the extent we are not able to successfully launch new business, vehicle production at our customers could be significantly delayed or shut down.

mentions.heading: Part of our workforce is unionized, which could subject us to work stoppages.
mentions.detail: About 13% of U.S. workforce unionized; New York facility agreement expires September 2028; some international sites unionized
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, approximately 13% of our U.S. workforce was unionized. We have a domestic collective bargaining agreement for one facility in New York, which expires in September 2028.

mentions.heading: Work stoppages, production shutdowns and similar events could significantly disrupt our business.
mentions.detail: Just-in-time automotive delivery; shutdowns at own plants, customers or suppliers halt purchases
mentions.quote: Because the automotive industry relies heavily on just-in-time delivery of components during the assembly and manufacture of vehicles, a work stoppage or production shutdown at one or more of our manufacturing and assembly facilities could have adverse effects on our business.

mentions.heading: Our benefit plan expenses and obligations may fluctuate depending on various factors
mentions.detail: Unfunded defined benefit pension obligations; falling rates could require significant additional contributions
mentions.quote: The valuation of our future payment obligations under the plans and the related plan assets is subject to significant adverse changes if the credit and capital markets cause interest rates and

mentions.heading: Our benefit plan expenses and obligations may fluctuate depending on various factors
mentions.detail: Unfunded U.S. post-employment medical benefit plans exposed to rising medical costs
mentions.quote: We also sponsor post-employment medical benefit plans in the U.S. that are unfunded. If medical costs continue to increase or actuarial assumptions are modified, this could have an adverse effect on our business.

mentions.heading: We are subject to extensive environmental regulations that are subject to change and involve significant risks.
mentions.detail: Automotive parts plants; acquired facilities may carry pre-ownership environmental liabilities
mentions.quote: Through various acquisitions over the years, we have acquired a number of manufacturing facilities, and we cannot assure that we will not incur material costs and liabilities relating to activities that predate our ownership.

mentions.heading: Our operations may be affected by greenhouse emissions and climate change and related regulations.
mentions.detail: Plants use electricity and natural gas; GHG rules could raise energy costs, restrict gas use, require allowances
mentions.quote: Greenhouse gas regulation could increase the price of the electricity we purchase, increase costs for use of natural gas, potentially restrict access to or the use of natural gas, require us to purchase allowances to offset our own emissions or result in an overall increase in costs of raw materials

mentions.heading: Our operations may be affected by greenhouse emissions and climate change and related regulations.
mentions.detail: Extreme weather may damage facilities, disrupt supply chain materials, raise insurance costs
mentions.quote: In addition, extreme weather events may damage a facility or surrounding infrastructure, making the facility unusable for a time. These factors may impact our decisions to construct new facilities.

mentions.heading: We have been and are exposed to liabilities related to environmental, product warranties, product recalls, litigation and other claims.
mentions.detail: Named potentially responsible party by EPA and state agencies at hazardous waste sites under CERCLA
mentions.quote: We and certain of our current and former direct and indirect corporate predecessors, subsidiaries and divisions have been identified by the United States Environmental Protection Agency and certain state environmental agencies and private parties as potentially responsible parties at various hazardous waste disposal sites under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act and equivalent state laws

drivers.name: Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act

mentions.heading: We have been and are exposed to liabilities related to environmental, product warranties, product recalls, litigation and other claims.
mentions.detail: Auto manufacturers increasingly seek supplier contribution for recalls; costs may exceed insurance or accruals
mentions.quote: As suppliers become more integrally involved in the vehicle design process and assume more of the vehicle assembly functions, auto manufacturers are increasingly looking to their suppliers for contribution when faced with recalls and product warranty claims.

mentions.heading: We are involved, from time to time, in legal proceedings and commercial or contractual disputes, which could have an adverse impact on our business.
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: While we maintain insurance for certain risks, the amount of insurance may not be adequate to cover all insured claims and liabilities. The incurrence of significant liabilities for which there is no, or insufficient, insurance coverage could adversely affect our business.

mentions.heading: Changes in legal and business environments, including anti-corruption compliance
mentions.detail: FCPA exposure; acquired operations may lack compliance training; risk from JV partners and agents
mentions.quote: Compliance-related issues in certain countries associated with laws such as the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and other anti-corruption laws could adversely affect our business.

mentions.heading: Changes in legal environment including trade, sanctions and climate laws
mentions.detail: Import/export controls, exchange controls, sanctions restrictions, greenhouse gas emission limits
mentions.quote: Changes that could impact the legal environment include new legislation, new regulations, new policies, investigations and legal proceedings, and new interpretations of existing legal rules and regulations, in particular, changes in import and export control laws or exchange control laws, additional restrictions on doing business in countries subject to sanctions, additional limitations on greenhouse gas emissions or other matters related to climate change and other changes in laws in countries where we operate or intend to operate.

mentions.heading: Changes in tax laws or tax rates and outcome of tax audits
mentions.detail: OBBBA enacted July 2025 extended TCJA provisions incl. R&D expensing; future changes could affect results
mentions.quote: On July 4, 2025, the U.S. government enacted tax legislation commonly referred to as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (the “OBBBA”). The OBBBA made permanent or extended several provisions from the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, including the restoration of expensing of domestic research and development expenditures.

drivers.name: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017

mentions.heading: Changes in tax laws or tax rates and outcome of tax audits
mentions.detail: Received assessments from various authorities, in appeals/litigation; company views some as arbitrary
mentions.quote: We have received tax assessments from various taxing authorities and are currently at varying stages of appeals and/or litigation regarding these matters. These audits may result in assessment of additional taxes that are resolved with the authorities or through the courts.

mentions.heading: We are subject to risks related to our international operations
mentions.detail: About 84% of 2025 net sales outside U.S.; facilities in Europe, Asia, Americas
mentions.quote: We have manufacturing and technical facilities in many regions, including Europe, Asia, and the Americas. For 2025, approximately 84% of our consolidated net sales were outside the U.S.

mentions.heading: We are subject to risks related to our international operations
mentions.detail: Exposure particularly to Euro, Korean Won and Chinese Renminbi
mentions.quote: Additionally, significant changes in currency exchange rates, particularly the Euro, Korean Won and Chinese Renminbi, could cause fluctuations in the reported results of our businesses’ operations that could negatively affect our results of operations.

mentions.heading: We are subject to risks related to our international operations
mentions.detail: U.S. holding company relies on distributions from non-U.S. subsidiaries; exchange controls could block conversion
mentions.quote: Because we are a U.S. holding company, one significant source of our funds is distributions from our non-U.S. subsidiaries.

mentions.heading: Maintaining a strong position in the Chinese market
mentions.detail: About 21% of 2025 net sales from China; aggressive competition, Chinese OEMs gaining share and insourcing Tier 1 components
mentions.quote: Domestic Chinese OEMs continue to expand their market share in and outside of China, and are increasingly insourcing certain components once sourced from Tier 1 suppliers.

mentions.heading: A downgrade in the ratings of our debt could restrict our ability to access the debt capital markets
mentions.detail: Revolver interest cost tied to rating grid; falling below investment grade would restrict market access and raise borrowing costs
mentions.quote: Our revolving credit agreement includes an increase in interest rates if the ratings for our debt are downgraded. The interest cost on our revolving credit agreement is based on a rating grid.

mentions.heading: Reliance on major customers under requirements contracts
mentions.detail: Volkswagen 13% and Ford 12% of 2025 sales; top ten customers 71%; requirements contracts with no minimum purchases
mentions.quote: Our worldwide sales in 2025 to Volkswagen and Ford constituted approximately 13% and 12% of our 2025 consolidated net sales, respectively. Sales to the Company’s top ten customers represented 71% of sales for the year ended December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: We are sensitive to the effects of our major customers’ labor relations
mentions.detail: Ford, Stellantis, GM depend on UAW; 2023 UAW strikes affected business
mentions.quote: Because of domestic OEMs’ dependence on a single union, we are affected by labor difficulties and work stoppages at OEMs’ facilities, such as the UAW strikes that occurred in 2023.

mentions.heading: We could be adversely affected by supply shortages of components from our suppliers
mentions.detail: Supply base rationalization leaves dependence on fewer sources for certain components
mentions.quote: In an effort to manage and reduce the cost of purchased goods and services, we have been rationalizing our supply base. As a result, we remain dependent on fewer sources of supply for certain components used in the manufacture of our products.

mentions.heading: Supplier shortages or delays in supply of components
mentions.detail: Prolonged shortage of critical components could disrupt production schedules for key products; fewer sources give suppliers pricing leverage amid OEM price-down pressure
mentions.quote: If we experience a prolonged shortage of critical components from any of our suppliers and cannot procure the components from other sources, we may be unable to meet the production schedules for some of our key products and could miss customer delivery expectations.

mentions.heading: Suppliers' economic distress could result in supply interruptions
mentions.detail: EV adoption volatility, OEM price-down pressure, tariffs and commodity costs strain suppliers; company sometimes provides financial support to distressed suppliers
mentions.quote: In certain instances, it would be difficult and expensive for us to change suppliers that are critical to our business. On occasion, we must provide financial support to distressed suppliers or take other measures to protect our supply lines.

mentions.heading: Possible insolvency of financial counterparties
mentions.detail: Exposure via insurance, letters of credit, credit lines, derivatives and investment management agreements
mentions.quote: We are subject to the risk that one or more of these counterparties may become insolvent and, therefore, be unable to meet its obligations under such contracts.

mentions.heading: Spin-off of PHINIA may not achieve anticipated tax benefits
mentions.detail: PHINIA spin-off intended tax-free for U.S. federal purposes; if taxable, significant income tax liabilities
mentions.quote: If the spin-off is ultimately determined to be taxable, the Company, PHINIA, or the Company’s stockholders could incur income tax liabilities that could be significant.

mentions.heading: Potential liabilities pursuant to the spin-off of PHINIA
mentions.detail: Lawsuit over ~$120 million VAT refunds settled for $78 million; net $40 million charge recorded at December 31, 2025
mentions.quote: On October 15, 2025, the Company entered into a settlement agreement (the “Settlement Agreement”) with PHINIA, pursuant to which PHINIA agreed to pay the Company $78 million, resolving the lawsuit and certain other matters relating to the spin-off.

mentions.heading: Indemnification obligations and rights under PHINIA spin-off agreements
mentions.detail: Indemnity from PHINIA may be insufficient or unpaid; court could reallocate PHINIA liabilities to BorgWarner
mentions.quote: In addition, with respect to the liabilities for which PHINIA and the other parties have agreed to indemnify us under these agreements, the indemnity rights we have against PHINIA and such other parties may not be sufficient to protect us against the full amount of the liabilities, further PHINIA or such other parties may not be able to fully satisfy their indemnification obligations.

mentions.heading: A variety of other factors could adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Loss of supply contracts, vehicle program start-up costs, delays or cancellations, low plant utilization tied to single product line or customer
mentions.quote: Any of the following could materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations: the loss of or changes in supply contracts or sourcing strategies of our major customers or suppliers; start-up expenses associated with new vehicle programs or delays or cancellation of such programs; low levels of utilization of our manufacturing facilities, which can be dependent on a single product line or customer; inability to recover engineering and tooling costs; market and financial consequences of recalls that may be required on products we supplied; delays or difficulties in new product development; the possible introduction of similar or superior technologies by others; global excess capacity and vehicle platform proliferation; and the impact of fire, flood, or other natural disasters, including pandemics and quarantines.

mentions.heading: Our industry is cyclical and a decline in production levels of our major customers could adversely affect our financial performance
mentions.detail: Sales tied to automaker production volumes and content per vehicle; sensitive to rates, inflation, EV/hybrid preferences, tariffs
mentions.quote: Our sales are driven by the number of vehicles produced by our automotive manufacturer customers and our content per vehicle. The automotive industry is cyclical and sensitive to general economic conditions, including interest rates, inflation, consumer demand and spending levels, and geopolitical issues.

mentions.heading: Chinese automakers gaining share from traditional automaker customers
mentions.detail: Chinese domestic automakers expanding via EVs in and outside China, eroding share of traditional automakers that are Lear's largest customers
mentions.quote: Chinese domestic automakers, in particular, continue to expand their market share in China (through electric vehicles) and outside of China with both innovative designs and attractive pricing. As a result, several traditional automakers have experienced declines in revenue and market share.

mentions.heading: Concentration of business and need to diversify
mentions.detail: Must diversify by customer, product, platform and geography; may not succeed
mentions.quote: Further, our ability to reduce the risks inherent in certain concentrations of business, and thereby maintain our financial performance in the future, will depend, in part, on our ability to continue to diversify our sales on a customer, product, platform and geographic basis to reflect the market overall. We may not be successful in such diversification.

mentions.heading: Increases in the costs and restrictions on the availability of raw materials, energy, commodities, components and labor
mentions.detail: Mitigation strategies and customer negotiations may not offset cost increases; supply affected by policy, disasters
mentions.quote: Increases in the costs of raw materials, energy, commodities, product components and labor, or restrictions on the availability thereof, could adversely affect our financial condition, operating results and cash flows.

mentions.heading: Our failure to execute our strategic objectives could adversely affect our financial performance
mentions.detail: Four pillars: Seating features leadership, E-Systems margin expansion, automation/digital investments, employee and sustainability initiatives
mentions.quote: Our strategy is based on four pillars designed to drive growth and profitability: (1) extend our market leadership position in Seating with priceable features, including modularity and thermal comfort systems; (2) expand margins in E-Systems through a focused portfolio that leverages our strong operating capabilities and customer relationships;

mentions.heading: Failure to execute strategic objectives
mentions.detail: Failure to identify, develop, complete or integrate organic investments and acquisitions
mentions.quote: Our failure to execute our strategic objectives could adversely affect our financial condition, operating results and cash flows. Moreover, there can be no assurances that, even if implemented, our strategic objectives will be successful.

mentions.heading: The lack of commercial success of or an increase in directed component sourcing for a vehicle model for which we are a significant supplier could adversely affect our financial performance.
mentions.detail: Purchase orders cover life-of-program requirements, not fixed quantities; risk of model failure, OEM insourcing or directed sourcing
mentions.quote: It is possible that a particular vehicle model is not successful with consumers or that our customers elect to manufacture our products internally, purchase our products from other suppliers or increase the extent to which they require us to utilize specific suppliers or materials in the manufacture of our products.

mentions.heading: Our inability to achieve product cost reductions to offset customer-imposed price reductions could adversely affect our financial performance.
mentions.detail: Automotive OEM contracts require annual price reductions over vehicle production life while supplier bears design and engineering
mentions.quote: Our customer contracts generally provide for annual price reductions over the production life of the vehicle, while requiring us to assume significant responsibility for the design, development and engineering of our products.

mentions.heading: International trade policies, such as tariffs, sanctions, export controls and other trade restrictions, could adversely affect our financial performance.
mentions.detail: U.S. tariffs since January 2025 affect China, Mexico, Canada and steel, aluminum, automobile parts; may raise costs and hit customer production
mentions.quote: As of the date of this Report, many of the tariffs announced, implemented or threatened by the current U.S. administration apply to (a) the countries in which we do business or from which we purchase, either directly or indirectly, materials or components, including China, Mexico and Canada, and (b) the materials or components that we purchase, either directly or indirectly, or produce, including steel, aluminum and automobile parts, among others, and therefore could adversely impact our business by increasing our operating costs, requiring us to incur significant costs to transition to alternative suppliers if our mitigation efforts are unsuccessful, or negatively impacting our customers' production.

mentions.heading: Sanctions, export controls and other trade restrictions
mentions.detail: U.S. and foreign sanctions and export controls affecting the automotive industry
mentions.quote: In addition to tariffs, the U.S. and foreign governments have implemented sanctions, export controls and other trade restrictions that impact industries around the world, including the automotive industry.

mentions.heading: Tariffs and trade restrictions could adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Contracts recover substantially all tariff costs to date; future US actions may hurt customer production or mitigation
mentions.quote: To date, our mitigation efforts have been successful, but we cannot provide any assurance that future government actions will not adversely impact our customers' production or undermine our mitigation efforts, which could in turn adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: USMCA review and renewal in 2026
mentions.detail: USMCA subject to trilateral review and renewal in 2026; CAFTA-DR status also uncertain
mentions.quote: In addition to potential increases in customs duties and tariffs in the United States and other countries, the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement ("USMCA") is subject to trilateral review and renewal in 2026. There can be no assurances that the USMCA will be renewed or, if renewed, any newly negotiated terms in the USMCA will not adversely affect our business.

mentions.heading: U.S.-China relations and supply chain integration
mentions.detail: China integrated in key supply chain components; China retaliatory tariffs; possible sanctions and export controls
mentions.quote: Also, China presents unique risks to U.S. automotive manufacturers due to the strain in U.S.-China relations and the level of integration with key components in our global supply chain.

mentions.heading: Adverse developments affecting or financial distress of suppliers
mentions.detail: Sole-source and customer-directed suppliers difficult to re-source; force majeure and tariffs affect capacity
mentions.quote: Furthermore, unfavorable economic or industry conditions in one or more of the regions in which we operate could result in financial distress within our supply base, which could cause a supply disruption and thereby adversely affect our financial condition, operating results and cash flows.

mentions.heading: Significant labor dispute involving us, customers or suppliers
mentions.detail: About 75,000 employees under labor agreements; ~67% of unionized workforce agreements expire in 2026
mentions.quote: We have labor agreements covering approximately 75,000 employees globally. In the United States and Canada, each of our unionized facilities has a separate collective bargaining agreement with the union that represents the workers at such facility, with each such agreement having an expiration date that is independent of the other agreements. Labor agreements covering approximately 67% of our global unionized work force are scheduled to expire in 2026.

mentions.heading: Our ability to attract, develop, engage and retain qualified employees could affect our ability to execute our strategy.
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Failure to attract, develop, engage and retain qualified employees, whether as a result of an insufficient number of qualified applicants, difficulty in recruiting new employees or inadequate resources to train, integrate and retain qualified employees, could impair our ability to execute our business strategy and could adversely affect our business.

mentions.heading: Our substantial international operations make us vulnerable to risks associated with volatile economic and political environments.
mentions.detail: Facilities in Mexico, Africa, Asia, Central/South America, Europe; strategy expands in lower-cost regions; cartel violence noted
mentions.quote: We have substantial international operations, with manufacturing and distribution facilities in many foreign countries, including Mexico and countries in Africa, Asia, Central and South America, and Europe. Some of the markets in which we do business may have volatile economic and/or political environments.

mentions.heading: Trade wars, tariffs, sanctions and export controls in international operations
mentions.detail: Listed among international risks; lower-cost region expansion increases exposure
mentions.quote: –trade wars, tariffs, sanctions, export controls or other trade restrictions;

mentions.heading: Currency fluctuations and controls in international operations
mentions.detail: Currency fluctuations, controls, hedging ability, commodity pricing discrepancies across exchanges
mentions.quote: –currency exchange rate fluctuations, discrepancies in commodity pricing between different exchanges, currency controls and the ability to economically hedge currencies;

mentions.heading: Certain of our operations are conducted through joint ventures which have unique risks.
mentions.detail: Joint ventures particularly in Asia; shared ownership and decision making with partners
mentions.quote: Certain of our operations, particularly in Asia, are conducted through joint ventures. With respect to our joint ventures, we may share ownership and management responsibilities with one or more partners that may not share our goals and objectives.

mentions.heading: Joint venture risks (continuation)
mentions.risk_name: Joint venture partner and control risk
mentions.detail: Partner conflicts, ownership changes, FCPA compliance control, limits on selling JV interests
mentions.quote: Additionally, our ability to sell our interest in a joint venture may be subject to contractual and other limitations.

mentions.heading: Our inability to effectively manage the timing, quality and costs of new program launches could adversely affect our financial performance.
mentions.detail: Tier 1 supplier coordinating numerous suppliers; launch cost ramp ahead of customer vehicle introduction timing
mentions.quote: In addition, new program launches require a significant ramp up of costs; however, our sales related to these new programs generally are dependent upon the timing and success of our customers' introduction of new vehicles.

mentions.heading: We operate in a highly competitive industry and efforts by our competitors, as well as new entrants to the industry, to gain market share could adversely affect our financial performance.
mentions.detail: Chinese automakers and lower-return Chinese suppliers gaining share; new EV entrants pressure pricing and margins
mentions.quote: Traditional automakers are experiencing increased competitive pressures as Chinese domestic automakers continue to expand their market share both in and beyond China. Chinese domestic suppliers that may have lower financial return expectations are also challenging traditional automotive suppliers for market share.

mentions.heading: If we do not respond appropriately, the evolution of the global transportation industry toward electrification could adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Slower EV adoption in United States due to emissions rule and tax incentive changes; program volume cuts and cancellations
