mentions.quote: The adoption of such vehicles, particularly electric vehicles, has been slower than anticipated, particularly in the United States, as a result of, among other things, changes in government carbon emissions regulations and tax incentives, as well as prevailing consumer preferences.

drivers.name: carbon emissions regulations and tax incentives

mentions.heading: Our increasing use of AI and other emerging technologies may expose us to operational, legal and regulatory risks that could adversely affect our business and reputation.
mentions.detail: AI tools used in production processes and administrative functions; flawed algorithms, data, privacy risks
mentions.quote: We currently incorporate AI-powered tools into certain internal business operations, such as in our production processes and in certain of our administrative functions. AI algorithms may be flawed, and datasets may be insufficient, inaccurate, biased or otherwise problematic.

mentions.heading: AI adoption risks including hardware constraints and third-party dependence
mentions.detail: AI depends on third-party models, cloud, infrastructure; GPU availability and power capacity constraints; competitive AI adoption risk
mentions.quote: Because our AI capabilities currently depend in part on third-party providers of models, cloud services and infrastructure, changes in their performance, pricing, licensing terms or availability could materially increase our costs.

mentions.heading: A disruption in our information technology systems, including cybersecurity, could adversely affect our financial performance
mentions.detail: Ransomware targeting manufacturers; connected vehicle systems hold end-user data; extortion payments may be legally prohibited
mentions.quote: In particular, ransomware or other attacks that are intended to disrupt our and our customers' business operations are becoming increasingly prevalent, particularly for manufacturing companies, and can lead to significant interruptions in operations and the ability to provide products or services, loss of sensitive data and income, reputational harm and diversion of funds.

mentions.heading: Cyber incidents at customers reduce demand
mentions.detail: 2025 cybersecurity incident at a major customer disrupted its production, reducing demand for Lear components and hitting results
mentions.quote: Additionally, in 2025, a cybersecurity incident affecting one of our major customers disrupted its production systems, which in turn reduced demand for our components and impacted our operating results.

mentions.heading: Compromise of products could affect many customers simultaneously
mentions.detail: Embedded in many customers' supply chains globally; contracts may lack liability limits; large-scale event could be catastrophic
mentions.quote: Our contracts with customers and others may not contain limitations of liability, and even where they do, there can be no assurances that limitations of liability in our contracts are sufficient to protect us from liabilities, damages or claims related to our security obligations.

mentions.heading: Cybersecurity attacks may be difficult to anticipate and remediate
mentions.detail: Generic statement; no specific systems, incidents or magnitudes named
mentions.quote: It may also be difficult and/or costly to detect, investigate, mitigate, contain and remediate a security incident. Our efforts to do so may not be successful.

mentions.heading: Cybersecurity incidents and IT system disruptions
mentions.risk_name: Cybersecurity breach and data privacy liability
mentions.detail: Disruption could affect vehicle systems supplied and plants; exposure under EU GDPR, China PIPL, India IT Act, California CCPA
mentions.quote: To the extent that our business is interrupted, including the vehicle systems and components that we supply to our customers or our plant operations, or data is lost, destroyed or inappropriately accessed, used or disclosed, such disruptions could adversely affect our competitive position, operating capacity, ability to provide our goods and services, relationships with our customers, financial condition, operating results and cash flows

drivers.name: European Union General Data Privacy Regulation

mentions.heading: Dependence on third parties' security measures
mentions.detail: Relies on customers, suppliers and service providers' security; limited monitoring ability; damages recovery may be insufficient
mentions.quote: Our ability to monitor these third parties' information security practices is limited, and these third parties may not have adequate information security measures in place.

mentions.heading: Pandemics and public health crises have disrupted our business
mentions.detail: Past suspension of operations; risks of component shortages, labor disruption, demand decline, impaired credit access
mentions.quote: Any such events may adversely impact our global supply chain and global manufacturing operations and cause us to again suspend our operations.

mentions.heading: Stakeholder perspectives on climate change and sustainability
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Our failure, or that of our supply base, to adequately meet stakeholder expectations or address stakeholder concerns, including concerns about environmental impacts and similar matters, may result in, among other things, negative sentiment toward us or our products, the loss of business, diluted market valuation, an inability to attract customers or an inability to attract and retain top talent.

mentions.heading: Global climate change could adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Extreme weather could affect material availability and cost, insurance costs, facility siting
mentions.quote: Such effects could disrupt our operations by, among other things, impacting the availability and cost of materials needed for manufacturing and could increase insurance and other operating costs.

mentions.heading: Impairment charges relating to goodwill and long-lived assets
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: We regularly monitor our goodwill and long-lived assets for impairment indicators.

mentions.heading: Impairment of goodwill or long-lived assets
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: In the event that we determine that our goodwill or long-lived assets are impaired, we may be required to record a significant charge to earnings that could adversely affect our financial condition and operating results.

mentions.heading: Significant changes in discount rates, the actual return on pension assets and other factors related to our global defined benefit plans could adversely affect our financial performance.
mentions.detail: Global defined benefit plans; interest rates and asset values affect expense and required contributions
mentions.quote: Because interest rates and the values of these pension assets have fluctuated and will continue to fluctuate in response to changing market conditions, pension and other postretirement benefit expense in subsequent periods, the funded status of our pension plans and the future minimum required pension contributions, if any, could adversely affect our financial condition, operating results and cash flows.

mentions.heading: Unanticipated changes in our effective tax rate, the adoption of new tax legislation or exposure to additional income tax liabilities could adversely affect our profitability.
mentions.detail: Deferred tax assets predominantly in U.S., dependent on U.S. taxable income; global tax audits; tax holidays
mentions.quote: The carrying value of deferred tax assets, which are predominantly in the United States, is dependent on our ability to generate future taxable income in the United States. We are also subject to ongoing tax audits globally.

mentions.heading: OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax
mentions.detail: 15% Pillar Two minimum tax; side-by-side system lets U.S.-parented MNEs opt out from 2026; not expected material
mentions.quote: The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development ("OECD") issued guidelines on the Global Anti-Base Erosion Model Rules, known as "Pillar Two," to implement a 15% global corporate minimum tax to address gaps in current tax laws and ensure that large multinational enterprises pay a minimum level of tax in the countries in which they operate.

mentions.heading: Our existing indebtedness and the inability to access capital markets could restrict our business activities
mentions.detail: About $2.7 billion debt outstanding; $2.0 billion undrawn revolver; covenant default and rating downgrade risk
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately $2.7 billion of outstanding indebtedness, as well as $2.0 billion available for borrowing under our revolving credit facility.

mentions.heading: A significant product liability lawsuit, warranty claim or product recall could adversely affect financial performance
mentions.detail: No insurance for warranty or recall; customers may seek contribution; limited product liability coverage
mentions.quote: We carry insurance for certain product liability claims, but such coverage may be limited. We do not maintain insurance for warranty or recall matters.

mentions.heading: Involvement in various legal and regulatory proceedings and claims
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: No assurances can be given that such proceedings and claims will not adversely affect our financial condition, operating results and cash flows.

mentions.heading: Focus on human rights and environmental laws and customer requirements could cause significant costs
mentions.risk_name: ESG and supply chain compliance costs
mentions.detail: Customer-imposed supply chain transparency requirements; complexity of global automotive supply chains
mentions.quote: Significant challenges may exist to comply with new legislative efforts and increasing customer requirements around supply chain transparency due to the inherent complexity of global automotive supply chains.

mentions.heading: New laws or regulations or changes in existing laws could adversely affect financial performance
mentions.detail: Generic statement; mentions tariffs, sanctions, data privacy, taxes
mentions.quote: The introduction of new laws or regulations or changes in existing laws or regulations, or the interpretation thereof, could increase the costs of doing business for us or our customers or suppliers or restrict our actions and adversely affect our financial condition, operating results and cash flows.

mentions.heading: Violations of anti-bribery, trade sanctions and other laws by employees or partners
mentions.detail: Exposure under U.S. FCPA and U.K. Bribery Act; operates in regions with government corruption; reliance on third-party conduct
mentions.quote: In particular, the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the U.K. Bribery Act and similar anti-bribery laws in other jurisdictions generally prohibit companies and their intermediaries from making improper payments to government officials for the purpose of obtaining or retaining business, and we operate in many parts of the world that have experienced government corruption to some degree.

mentions.heading: Compliance with environmental laws could cause significant costs
mentions.detail: Generic statement; manufacturing facilities subject to environmental laws and possible remediation of unknown conditions
mentions.quote: Material future expenditures may be necessary if compliance standards change or material unknown conditions that require remediation are discovered.

mentions.heading: Intellectual property developments or assertions could hurt performance
mentions.detail: Large patent, trademark portfolio and numerous licensing arrangements; generic infringement exposure
mentions.quote: Also, while we believe we have the necessary rights to use all of the intellectual property we use, if we are found to infringe on the rights of others, we could be adversely impacted.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical.
mentions.detail: Semiconductor capacity cycles cause overcapacity, high inventory, under-utilization and accelerated ASP erosion
mentions.quote: These downturns have been characterized by diminishing demand for end-user products, high inventory levels, under-utilization of manufacturing capacity and accelerated erosion of average selling prices.

mentions.heading: Significantly increased volatility and instability and unfavorable economic conditions may adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: 2020 automotive demand collapse from pandemic shutdowns; 2020-2022 rebound unmet; softening demand 2023-2025 from macro and geopolitics
mentions.quote: In the first half of 2020, demand in the automotive market steeply declined as a result of manufacturing shutdowns by automotive customers due to the coronavirus pandemic, resulting in an unforeseen negative impact to our results of operations.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is highly competitive; failure to introduce new technologies timely could hurt business
mentions.detail: Rapid change, price erosion, rising R&D costs from inflation; larger competitors and consolidation; need for on-device AI capability
mentions.quote: Meeting evolving industry requirements, including the increasing use of AI and machine learning technologies (including the need to run complex AI-based applications on devices), and introducing new products to the market in a timely manner and at prices that are acceptable to our customers are significant factors in determining our competitiveness and success.

mentions.heading: Risks from introduction and incorporation of AI technologies
mentions.detail: AI may give biased outputs, become obsolete, raise cybersecurity exposure; undeveloped AI legal landscape may impose costs
mentions.quote: In addition, AI and machine learning are still in relatively early stages, and the introduction and incorporation of AI technologies may result in unintended consequences or other new or expanded risks and liabilities.

mentions.heading: The demand for our products depends to a significant degree on the demand for our customers' end products
mentions.detail: Revenue mostly from Automotive, Industrial & IoT, Mobile, Communication Infrastructure; customers vary orders, postpone deliveries; custom products may be unsellable
mentions.quote: The vast majority of our revenue is derived from sales to manufacturers in the Automotive, Industrial & IoT, Mobile, and Communication Infrastructure end markets. Demand in these markets fluctuates significantly, driven by consumer spending, consumer preferences, the development of new technologies and prevailing economic conditions.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is historically characterized by continued price erosion
mentions.detail: Intense pricing pressure on older-technology products; may be contractually unable to cease production, bearing losses
mentions.quote: Moreover, we may not be able to cease production of such products, either due to contractual obligations or for customer relationship reasons, and as a result may be required to bear reduced profitability, or even a loss on such products.

mentions.heading: We depend on winning selection processes, and failure to be selected could adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Lengthy bids with upfront design spend; automotive long design cycles can lock out a customer for years
mentions.quote: This risk is particularly pronounced in markets where there are only a few potential customers and in the automotive market, where, due to the longer design cycles involved, failure to win a design-in could prevent access to a customer for several years.

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: Tariffs on imports by United States and China, export controls and sector sanctions
mentions.quote: negative economic developments in economies around the world and the instability of governments and international trade arrangements, such as the increase of barriers to international trade including the imposition of new or increased tariffs on imports by the United States and China and other countries, enhanced export controls on certain products and sanctions on certain industry sectors and parties;

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: Middle East hostilities and Ukraine conflict affect customers, supply chain, energy prices and demand
mentions.quote: social and political instability in a number of countries around the world, including continued hostilities in the Middle East and the armed conflict in Ukraine.

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: China-Taiwan tensions, restricted entity lists could decouple trade and technology supply chains
mentions.quote: Sustained geopolitical tensions, such as the current geopolitical tensions involving China and Taiwan, could lead to long-term changes in global trade and technology supply chains and decoupling of global trade networks;

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: Coronavirus-type outbreaks affecting workforce, suppliers and customers
mentions.quote: epidemics and pandemics, such as the coronavirus outbreak, which may adversely affect our workforce, as well as our suppliers and customers;

mentions.heading: Global business operations expose us to international business risks
mentions.detail: U.S. dollar exchange rate volatility; transfer restrictions in mainland China
mentions.quote: volatility in foreign currency exchange rates, in particular with respect to the U.S. dollar, and transfer restrictions, in particular in mainland China; and

mentions.heading: Recently announced and future tariffs and other trade restrictions could materially and adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: 2025 U.S. tariffs and reciprocal measures; U.S.-China trade dynamics; April 2025 Section 232 semiconductor investigation expected to bring additional tariffs
mentions.quote: For example, in April 2025, the Department of Commerce launched an investigation into the national security impacts of imported semiconductors and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. While the results of this investigation remain unknown, it is expected to result in additional tariffs and trade restrictions that may adversely impact our business.

drivers.name: Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962

mentions.heading: Goodwill and other identifiable intangible assets represent a significant portion of our total assets
mentions.detail: Significant acquisition-related goodwill and intangibles; impairment triggers include IP validity challenges and regulatory changes
mentions.quote: Depending on future circumstances, it is possible that we may never realize the full value of our intangible assets. Any future determination of impairment of goodwill or other identifiable intangible assets could have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations and stockholders’ equity.

mentions.heading: In difficult market conditions, our high fixed costs combined with low revenue may negatively affect our results
mentions.detail: Own fabs incur full-capacity fixed costs at low utilization, as in first half of 2020
mentions.quote: During such periods, our fabrication plants could operate at lower loading level, while the fixed costs associated with the full capacity continue to be incurred, resulting in lower gross profit.

mentions.heading: We may from time to time restructure parts of our organization
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: The costs of implementing any restructurings, changes or cost savings steps may differ from our estimates and any negative impacts on our revenues or otherwise of such restructurings, changes or steps, such as situations in which customer satisfaction is negatively impacted, may be larger than originally estimated.

mentions.heading: Failure to renegotiate collective bargaining agreements or consult works councils could harm business
mentions.detail: Collective bargaining agreements, social plans; works council consultation required for restructurings, acquisitions and divestitures
mentions.quote: We are also required to consult with our employee representatives, such as works councils, on items such as restructurings, acquisitions and divestitures.

mentions.heading: Our working capital needs are difficult to predict.
mentions.detail: Long development-to-delivery cycle drives high inventory and WIP; stockpiling across many specifications
mentions.quote: The comparatively long period between the time at which we commence development of a product and the time at which it may be delivered to a customer leads to high inventory and work-in-progress levels.

mentions.heading: Costs relating to product defects, product liability and warranty claims
mentions.detail: Software-enabled semiconductors; replacement costs exceed device value; customer recall cost recovery; personal injury exposure
mentions.quote: Moreover, since the cost of replacing defective semiconductor devices is often much higher than the value of the devices themselves, we may at times face damage claims from customers in excess of the amounts they pay us for our products, including consequential damages.

mentions.heading: We face risks related to security vulnerabilities in our products.
mentions.detail: Processors used in cloud, IoT, critical infrastructure and automotive applications; third-party IP and components also vulnerable
mentions.quote: As we have become a more data-centric company, our processors and other products are being used in additional and new and critical application areas that create new or increased cybersecurity, privacy or safety risks. This includes applications that gather and process large amounts of data, such as the cloud or Internet of Things, and critical infrastructure and automotive applications.

mentions.heading: Our business has suffered, and could in the future suffer, from manufacturing problems.
mentions.detail: Austin, Texas fabs disrupted by February 2021 winter storm; utility rationing of electricity, gas, water risk
mentions.quote: Further, we may suffer disruptions in our manufacturing operations, either due to production difficulties such as those described above or as a result of external factors beyond our control, such as the disruption to our Austin, Texas manufacturing facilities caused by the February 2021 winter storm.

mentions.heading: Reliance on timely supply of equipment and materials from limited suppliers
mentions.detail: Shortages of silicon wafers or specialized chemicals; equipment hard to substitute; tariffs may raise material costs
mentions.quote: Supply disruptions may also occur due to shortages in critical materials, such as silicon wafers or specialized chemicals. In addition, the imposition of tariffs or other trade restrictions may significantly increase the costs, and otherwise adversely impact the availability of certain raw materials and supplies needed for our manufacturing operations.

mentions.heading: Failure of our third party suppliers to perform could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Could not obtain sufficient silicon wafers from foundry partners in 2022 shortage; unable to fully supply demand
mentions.quote: For example, as part of the industry-wide shortage of semiconductors during 2022 we could not obtain sufficient silicon wafers from our foundry partners to meet the demand for our products, causing us not to fully supply the demand for our products, and negatively affecting our results of operations.

mentions.heading: Failure of our third party suppliers to perform could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Foundry prices vary with supplier utilization; costs rose significantly in 2022 shortage, pressuring gross margin
mentions.quote: Furthermore, these outsourcing costs can vary materially from quarter to quarter and, in cases of industry shortages like we experienced in 2022, they can increase significantly, which may negatively affect our gross profit if we are not able to increase the price of our products.

mentions.heading: Failure of our third party suppliers to perform could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Long-term supply agreements with key manufacturing partners; supplier non-performance or demand drop could hurt results
mentions.quote: In addition, we have entered into long-term supply agreements with certain key manufacturing partners. The failure of these suppliers to perform under these agreements or an unexpected reduction in demand for these products could result in a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Disruptions in our relationships with any one of our key customers could adversely affect our business.
mentions.detail: Substantial revenue from top customers including distributors
mentions.quote: A substantial portion of our revenue is derived from our top customers, including our distributors. We cannot guarantee that we will be able to generate similar levels of revenue from our largest customers in the future.

mentions.heading: We receive subsidies and grants in certain countries, and a reduction in governmental funding or demands for repayment could increase our costs.
mentions.detail: Receives government subsidies in some countries; curtailment or repayment demands if grant conditions unmet or operations terminated
mentions.quote: In such event that we don't meet the subsidies grant conditions, such government agencies could seek to recover such subsidies from us, and they could cancel or reduce other subsidies we receive from them.

mentions.heading: Natural disasters and climate change may negatively impact our business
mentions.detail: Factories in earthquake, flood or storm zones in Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia, Thailand; 2011 Japan tsunami hit supply chains
mentions.quote: The impact of any such natural disasters depends on the specific geographic circumstances but could be significant, as some of our factories are located in areas with known earthquake fault zones, flood or storm risks, including but not limited to Singapore, Taiwan, Malaysia or Thailand.

mentions.heading: Climate change may cause more natural disasters affecting operations
mentions.detail: February 2021 winter storm disrupted Austin, Texas fabs and their water and utilities
mentions.quote: Such natural disasters pose physical risks to our manufacturing, IT facilities or our suppliers’ facilities, or could disrupt the availability of water and utilities necessary for the operation of our manufacturing facilities or our suppliers’ facilities resulting in increased operating costs and business disruption, such as the disruption to our Austin, Texas manufacturing facilities caused by the February 2021 winter storm and weather-related disruption of water and utilities to these facilities.

mentions.heading: Water scarcity in semi-arid manufacturing regions
mentions.detail: Water-intensive semiconductor manufacturing; many own and supplier sites in semi-arid regions vulnerable to drought
mentions.quote: In addition, semiconductor manufacturing is a water-intensive process. Many of our manufacturing sites and those of our suppliers are located in semi–arid regions that may become increasingly vulnerable to prolonged droughts associated with evolving changes to the climate, which may lead to water scarcity.

mentions.heading: Acquisitions and strategic transactions could adversely affect results
mentions.detail: Routine acquisitions, joint ventures, minority equity stakes and loans; integration of employees, R&D, systems challenging
mentions.quote: If we do not achieve the anticipated benefits of business acquisitions or other strategic activities, or if we are unable to consummate acquisitions or strategic investments that we consider important to the future of our business, our business and results of operations may be adversely affected and our growth strategy may not be successful.

mentions.heading: Government approval required for acquisitions
mentions.detail: Agencies have previously denied or delayed approval of transactions
mentions.quote: Certain agencies in the past have, and may in the future, deny the transaction or fail to approve in a timely manner, resulting in delays in closing and us not realizing the anticipated benefits of the proposed transactions.

mentions.heading: We rely on joint ventures to meet our current and future manufacturing requirements
mentions.detail: Manufacturing JVs SSMC (TSMC), VSMC (Vanguard), ESMC (TSMC, Bosch, Infineon); funding and take-or-pay obligations; ramp timing risk
mentions.quote: If we do not achieve the anticipated benefits of these joint ventures, or if newly established joint ventures are not able to begin production in the expected timing or achieve expected efficiency and quality, our business and results of operations may be adversely affected.

mentions.heading: As our business is global, we need to comply with laws and regulations in countries across the world
mentions.detail: U.S. EAR and EU sanctions; previously halted shipments to Huawei in 2020; new U.S. administration policy changes
mentions.quote: For example, in 2020, due to regulations imposed by the U.S. government, we ceased shipments of our products to Huawei pending approval of export licenses.

mentions.heading: As our business is global, we need to comply with laws and regulations in countries across the world
mentions.detail: EU GDPR and expanding global privacy rules could impose significant compliance costs
mentions.quote: Furthermore, global privacy legislation, enforcement, and policy activity, such as the EU General Data Privacy Regulation, are rapidly expanding and creating a complex regulatory compliance environment. Costs to comply with and implement these privacy-related and data protection measures could be significant.

mentions.heading: As our business is global, we need to comply with laws and regulations in countries across the world
mentions.detail: Dutch foreign investment control regime and U.S. outbound investment rules may limit acquisitions and alliances
mentions.quote: In addition, governments are increasingly imposing restrictions on cross-border investments in semiconductor businesses and technology, such as the Dutch foreign investment control regime and U.S. outbound investment rules, that may limit our ability to execute strategic acquisitions, investments and alliances, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business.

mentions.heading: Legal proceedings are pending in various jurisdictions; adverse outcome might affect results
mentions.detail: Past claims of injuries to children of former employees from clean room chemical exposure; facilities operated by NXP or former parents Philips and Motorola
mentions.quote: For example, in the past we have been involved in legal proceedings claiming personal injuries to the children of former employees as a result of employees’ alleged exposure to chemicals used in semiconductor manufacturing clean room environments operated by us or our former parent companies, Philips and Motorola.

mentions.heading: Manufacturing operations are subject to environmental laws and regulations
mentions.detail: Strict, joint and several liability at current and historical manufacturing facilities; permits required
mentions.quote: Certain environmental laws impose strict, and in certain circumstances, joint and several liability on current or previous owners or operators of real property for the cost of investigation, removal or remediation of hazardous substances as well as liability for related damages to natural resources.

mentions.heading: Initiatives to address climate change
mentions.detail: Possible energy price increases, carbon taxes, carbon offsets and lower-carbon equipment and materials raising production costs
mentions.quote: Public and private initiatives to address climate change may result in an increase in the cost of production due to increase in the prices of energy, introduction of energy or carbon tax or the purchase of carbon offsets.

mentions.heading: Interruptions in our information technology systems could adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Any significant interruption in our business applications, systems or networks, including but not limited to new system implementations, computer viruses, cyberattacks, security breaches, facility issues or energy blackouts could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Our computer systems and networks are subject to attempted security breaches and other cybersecurity incidents
mentions.detail: Has experienced cyber-attacks; AI-enabled phishing and malicious code cited as evolving threat
mentions.quote: We have, from time to time, experienced cyber-attacks attempting to obtain access to and misuse our computer systems and networks. Such incidents could result in the misappropriation of our proprietary information and technology, the compromise of personal and confidential information of our employees, customers or suppliers or interrupt our business.

mentions.heading: Employee misappropriation of proprietary technology
mentions.detail: Identified former employees' theft of proprietary technology, possibly violating export controls, reported to authorities
mentions.quote: We have identified instances of employee misappropriation or theft of certain proprietary technology by individuals who are no longer employed by NXP. In some cases, such misappropriation may result in the violation of applicable export control regulations, which we report to relevant authorities as appropriate.

mentions.heading: We may not be able to protect our proprietary intellectual property against improper use
mentions.detail: Patents may be challenged or circumvented; weak enforcement in some countries where it operates
mentions.quote: In particular, intellectual property rights are difficult to enforce in countries where the application and enforcement of the laws governing such rights may not have reached the same level as compared to other jurisdictions where we operate.

mentions.heading: AI technology intellectual property uncertainty
mentions.detail: AI built into products; IP ownership of AI unsettled by U.S. or foreign courts, risking loss of IP rights
mentions.quote: Finally, the intellectual property ownership and license rights, including copyrights and patents, surrounding AI technologies, which we are and may in the future continue to build into our products, have not been fully addressed by U.S. or foreign courts, laws or regulations

mentions.heading: We may become party to intellectual property claims or litigation that could cause us to incur substantial costs, pay substantial damages or prohibit us from selling our products.
mentions.detail: Possible treble damages in the United States, injunctions, product redesign or sales stoppage
mentions.quote: In the event that we cannot obtain or take the view that we don’t need a license, these parties may file lawsuits against us seeking damages (and potentially treble damages in the United States) or an injunction against the sale of our products that incorporate allegedly infringed intellectual property or against the operation of our business as presently conducted.

mentions.heading: IP claims arising from use of AI technologies
mentions.detail: Use of AI in productivity and products may trigger copyright claims amid uncertain legal framework
mentions.quote: Additionally, and in part due to ongoing uncertainties in the legal framework around AI, our use of AI technologies for productivity and in our products and services may expose us to copyright infringement or other intellectual property misappropriation claims.

mentions.heading: Loss of our key management and other personnel, or an inability to attract such management and other personnel, could affect our business.
mentions.detail: Dependence on senior engineers; competitive market for skilled engineers
mentions.quote: The market for qualified employees, including skilled engineers and other individuals with the required technical expertise to succeed in our business, is highly competitive and the loss of qualified employees or an inability to attract, retain and motivate the additional highly skilled employees required for the operation and expansion of our business could hinder our ability to successfully conduct research activities or develop marketable products.

mentions.heading: CEO transition risk
mentions.detail: Kurt Sievers retired October 28, 2025; Rafael Sotomayor succeeded as President and CEO
mentions.quote: Effective October 28, 2025, Kurt Sievers voluntarily retired as our CEO and executive director and Rafael Sotomayor succeeded Mr. Sievers as President and CEO and temporary executive director of the Company.

mentions.heading: United States civil liabilities may not be enforceable against us.
mentions.detail: Incorporated in the Netherlands; no US-Netherlands treaty on mutual enforcement; claims must be relitigated in Dutch courts
mentions.quote: In order to obtain a judgment which is enforceable in the Netherlands, the claim must be relitigated before a competent court of the Netherlands; the relevant Netherlands court has discretion to attach such weight to a judgment of the courts of the United States as it deems appropriate

mentions.heading: We are a Dutch public company with limited liability; stockholder rights may differ from U.S. jurisdictions.
mentions.detail: Dutch naamloze vennootschap; board must consider stakeholders including employees, not only stockholders
mentions.quote: In the performance of its duties, our board of directors is required by Dutch law to consider the interests of our company, its stockholders, its employees and other stakeholders, in all cases with due observation of the principles of reasonableness and fairness.

mentions.heading: Our debt obligations expose us to risks that could adversely affect our financial condition.
mentions.risk_name: High leverage and debt service burden
mentions.detail: $12,290 million aggregate principal debt outstanding as of December 31, 2025
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had outstanding indebtedness with an aggregate principal amount of $12,290 million. Our substantial indebtedness could have a material adverse effect on our business by:

mentions.heading: Debt obligations expose us to increased interest rates on revolving facility
mentions.detail: $2,500 million RCF restated to $3,000 million on February 6, 2026; variable-rate borrowings
mentions.quote: exposing us to the risk of increased interest rates in the event we have borrowings under our $2,500 million revolving credit facility agreement (the “RCF Agreement”), which was restated to $3,000 million as per February 6, 2026, because loans under the RCF Agreement may bear interest at a variable rate;

mentions.heading: Consequences of substantial indebtedness (continuation of bullet list)
mentions.detail: Leverage may trigger covenant defaults, restrict acquisitions, limit financing and create competitive disadvantage versus less leveraged peers
mentions.quote: limiting our flexibility in planning for, or reacting to, changes in our business or market conditions and placing us at a competitive disadvantage compared to our competitors who are less highly leveraged

mentions.heading: Despite our level of indebtedness, we may still incur significantly more debt
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: Despite our level of indebtedness, we may still incur significantly more debt, which could further exacerbate the risks described above and affect our ability to service and repay our debt.

mentions.heading: If we do not comply with the covenants in our debt agreements or fail to generate sufficient cash to service and repay our debt
mentions.detail: RCF Agreement, EIB loan facilities and unsecured note indentures carry covenants; default could trigger acceleration and cross defaults
mentions.quote: The RCF Agreement, European Investment Bank (EIB) loan facilities and the indentures governing our unsecured notes or any other debt arrangements that we may have require us to comply with various covenants.

mentions.heading: Insufficient cash flow to service debt
mentions.detail: May need asset sales, refinancing at higher rates with more onerous covenants; dependent on capital markets
mentions.quote: Our ability to restructure or refinance our debt will depend on the condition of the capital markets and our financial condition at such time. Any refinancing of our debt could be at higher interest rates and may require us to comply with more onerous covenants, which could further restrict our business operations.

mentions.heading: The rating of our debt by major rating agencies may further improve or deteriorate
mentions.detail: Downgrades or review announcements could raise borrowing costs and affect market value

mentions.heading: Evolving AI laws and regulations

mentions.quote: New and existing frameworks in the United States, the European Union and China - including the EU AI Act’s risk‑based approach - may impose additional compliance, transparency, conformity assessment, monitoring or usage‑restriction obligations on AI‑enabled products.

mentions.heading: AI-related risks in acquisitions and talent competition
mentions.detail: Intensified competition for AI-skilled personnel critical to product roadmap; acquired companies' AI use risks
mentions.quote: In addition, competition for talent with AI expertise has intensified, and our ability to attract, retain and train personnel with appropriate AI skills and literacy is critical to our innovation and product roadmap.

mentions.heading: Uncertainty in IP law relating to AI-created works
mentions.detail: Inconsistent IP protection for innovations developed with AI could impair commercialization
mentions.quote: Uncertainty in intellectual property law relating to works created using AI technology may result in changing or inconsistent IP protections, which could adversely affect our ability to protect or commercialize innovations developed with AI.

mentions.heading: We face risks related to security vulnerabilities in our products.
mentions.detail: Chips used in cloud, IoT, automotive, defense and AI systems; vulnerabilities in firmware may surface after large-scale deployment
mentions.quote: Our products are being used in application areas that create new or increased cybersecurity, privacy or safety risks including applications that gather and process data, such as the cloud or IoT, automotive applications, and applications that use AI.

mentions.heading: We face risks to our business and proprietary confidential information due to use of AI.
mentions.detail: Unauthorized employee/partner use of tools like ChatGPT could expose confidential, ITAR or export-controlled data
mentions.quote: Use of AI tools may result in claims related to violation of privacy or third-party intellectual property rights, unauthorized access to or use of proprietary information, or government regulated data (e.g., controlled unclassified information, ITAR, export-controlled data), and noncompliance with actual or asserted legal, contractual, or other obligations (including open source requirements).

mentions.heading: Differing opinions and regulations regarding responsible use of technologies including AI
mentions.detail: AI-enabled products may draw controversy over human rights, privacy, employment; may slow AI adoption and market acceptance
mentions.quote: AI introduces new legal, social and ethical issues, risks and challenges that may slow adoption of AI-enabled products and services, reduce market acceptance, delay commercialization, alter customer purchasing behavior, or adversely affect our business model, competitive position and operating results.

mentions.heading: Failure to comply with privacy, data protection and cybersecurity laws
mentions.detail: Subject to GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, EU Cyber Resilience Act; fines up to 4% of worldwide revenue or EUR20 million
mentions.quote: Substantial fines may be imposed for breaches of data protection requirements, which can be up to 4% of a company’s worldwide revenue or 20 million Euros, whichever is greater, and classes of individuals or consumer protection organizations may initiate litigation related to our processing of their personal data.

mentions.heading: Failure to comply with CMMC cybersecurity requirements
mentions.detail: Non-compliance with CMMC required by U.S. Department of War and prime customers may bar government contracts
mentions.quote: Over time, failure to comply with CMMC requirements required by the U.S. Department of War and its prime customers may make us ineligible for government contracts.

mentions.heading: Restrictions on cross-border transfers of personal data from the EEA
mentions.detail: Relies on SCCs; Schrems II invalidated Privacy Shield; EU-U.S. DPF faces legal challenge; may need costly EEA processing capacity
mentions.quote: If we are unable to implement sufficient safeguards to ensure that our transfers of personal information from the EEA are lawful, we may face increased exposure to regulatory actions and substantial fines and injunctions against processing personal information from the EEA.

mentions.heading: Privacy, data protection and cybersecurity laws may increase costs and liabilities
mentions.detail: CCPA/CPRA in California, other state laws, federal rules on controlled unclassified and export-controlled data
mentions.quote: The CPRA, which became operative January 1, 2023, expands the CCPA’s requirements, including applying to personal information of business representatives and employees and establishing a new regulatory agency to implement and enforce the law.

mentions.heading: Cross-border personal data transfer restrictions
mentions.detail: GDPR transfer limits could block data flows from Europe to U.S., require costly European processing; customers may refuse data
mentions.quote: The inability to transfer personal data to the U.S. could significantly and negatively impact our business operations, limit our ability to collaborate with parties that are subject to European and other data privacy and security laws, or require us to increase our personal data processing capabilities in Europe and/or elsewhere at significant expense.

mentions.heading: We are exposed to various risks related to legal proceedings, investigations or claims.
mentions.detail: IP, product defect, contract, tax, export control and sanctions matters; indemnification demands; past substantial costs; possible injunction on product sales
mentions.quote: These legal proceedings and claims, even if meritless, have in the past and could in the future result in unexpected and substantial costs to us.

mentions.heading: Claims related to the manufacture, performance, or use of our products
mentions.detail: Damages may exceed revenue since integrated systems cost more; some contracts don't exclude consequential damages; insurance insufficient
mentions.quote: Because the systems into which our products are integrated have a higher cost of goods than the products we sell, the expenses and damages we are asked to pay may be significantly higher than the revenue and profits we received.

mentions.heading: Exposure to claims in safety-critical end markets
mentions.detail: Sales into automotive, aerospace, defense, safety, security, medical where failures could damage property or persons
mentions.quote: Further, we sell to customers in industries such as automotive, aerospace, defense, safety, security, and medical, where failure of the application could cause damage to property or persons.

mentions.heading: Our contractual relationships with our customers expose us to risks and liabilities
mentions.detail: No long-term contracts; ~101,000 customers, top ten ~11% of fiscal 2026 revenue; backlog push-outs fiscal 2023-2025
mentions.quote: Also, many of our customers felt the effects of slowing economic activity and increasing business uncertainty, and customer requests to push-out or cancel backlog and our accommodation of their requests increased in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2023 and continued throughout fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025.

mentions.heading: Unfavorable negotiated customer contract terms
mentions.detail: Agreed to uncapped IP infringement/product failure liability and liquidated damages to win designs
mentions.quote: In order to win important designs, avoid losing business to competitors, maintain existing business, or be permitted to bid on new business, we have, and may in the future, have to agree to uncapped liability for such items as intellectual property infringement or product failure, or have to agree to liquidated damage provisions.

mentions.heading: Ability to obtain and protect patents and intellectual property rights
mentions.detail: Patents may lack scope; interference proceedings in USPTO and foreign courts; weaker IP laws in certain foreign countries
mentions.quote: In addition, the laws of certain foreign countries do not protect our intellectual property rights to the same extent as the laws of the U.S. Infringement of our intellectual property rights by a third-party could result in harm to our competitive position, uncompensated lost market and revenue opportunities for us.

mentions.heading: Use of open source software in our software
mentions.detail: Some software derived from open source; non-compliance could force source code release or stop distribution
mentions.quote: While we believe we have complied with our obligations under the various applicable licenses for open source software, in the event that the copyright holder of any open source software were to legally establish that we had not complied with the terms of a license for a particular work, we could be required to release the source code of that work to the public and/or stop distribution of that work if the license is terminated which could adversely impact our business and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Our reported financial results may be adversely affected by new accounting pronouncements
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: New accounting pronouncements or a change in the interpretation of accounting standards or practices may have a significant effect on our reported financial results and may affect our reporting of transactions completed before the change is effective.

mentions.heading: Regulatory authorities could issue new export controls or trade sanctions
mentions.detail: October 2022 Commerce rules restrict advanced IC and semiconductor manufacturing activity involving China, Hong Kong, Macau; license delays from shutdowns
mentions.quote: For example, in October 2022, the U.S. Department of Commerce published a regulation that imposed restrictions on activities in or involving China, Hong Kong, and Macau related to advanced computing integrated circuits (ICs), advanced-node ICs, computers and other commodities that contain such ICs, certain semiconductor manufacturing items, and supercomputers.

mentions.heading: Trade and anti-bribery compliance penalties
mentions.detail: Subject to FCPA, EAR, ITAR; violations may bring denial of export privileges, fines, product seizure
mentions.quote: Further, determination by a government that we have failed to comply with trade regulations or anti-bribery regulations can result in penalties which may include denial of export privileges, fines, penalties, and seizure of products, or loss of reputation, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, sales and earnings.

mentions.heading: Export controls, sanctions, and trade restrictions are complex and subject to changing interpretation
mentions.detail: BIS semiconductor rules since Oct 2022/Nov 2023, entity lists, Huawei ban, slower license processing, Russia sanctions, VCS restrictions
mentions.quote: The result of these additional restrictions and the change in the U.S. administration in 2025 is that there has been a slow-down in the processing of export license applications by the U.S. Government and an increased burden on us to conduct additional due diligence imposed by the regulations, as well as by sanctions imposed on Russia for invading Ukraine.

mentions.heading: U.S. government procurement bans on Chinese telecom equipment
mentions.detail: FAR and National Defense Authorization Act bar contracts with firms using covered Chinese telecommunications equipment
mentions.quote: In July 2020, this was expanded to prohibit U.S. governmental agencies from entering into a contract with any company that uses covered telecommunications equipment whether or not the Chinese technology is related to the procurement.

mentions.heading: Tariffs and U.S.-China trade tensions
mentions.detail: U.S.-China reciprocal tariffs since 2018, 10% baseline tariff; mitigation through supply chain adjustments may be incomplete
mentions.quote: Trade tensions between the U.S. and China, have continued to escalate from 2018 to present, and include the U.S. increasing tariffs on Chinese origin goods and China increasing tariffs on U.S. origin goods. Additionally, the U.S. has imposed a baseline 10% tariff on almost all imported goods globally.

mentions.heading: Potential Section 232 semiconductor tariffs
mentions.detail: Section 232 investigation expected to raise semiconductor tariffs; uncertain IEEPA tariff refunds; copper tariffs, de minimis suspension
mentions.quote: Although semiconductors remain exempt from most of the recent tariff actions, an increase in tariffs on semiconductors is expected to be imposed once the Section 232 investigation into the impact on U.S. national security by imports of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and their derivative products is concluded.

mentions.heading: Increased tariffs and government restrictions could reduce demand for our products
mentions.detail: China restrictions on raw materials and Micron-containing products; possible revived antidumping probe on US analog chips; buy-Chinese directives
mentions.quote: The Chinese government may also re-initiate the suspended antidumping investigation into imports of analog chips originating in the United States and aggressively enforce the new regulation intended to combat the extraterritorial application of foreign trade controls, sanctions and other measures

mentions.heading: Evolving U.S. export controls may harm competitiveness
mentions.detail: Non-US customers may shift to suppliers not subject to US export controls; foreign competitors gain investment
mentions.quote: It is also possible that evolving U.S. export controls may encourage our non-U.S. customers to purchase from companies not subject to U.S. export controls, thereby harming our business, market position, and financial results.

mentions.heading: Trade barriers may limit access to equipment and raw materials
mentions.detail: Retaliatory trade measures could limit access to rare earth minerals, equipment, components and M&A approvals
mentions.quote: Further changes in trade or national security protection policy, tariffs, additional taxes, restrictions on exports or other trade barriers, including those taken against the U.S. in retaliation for U.S. policies, may limit our ability to obtain equipment, components or raw materials (including rare earth minerals), limit our ability to produce products

mentions.heading: Outcome of income tax examinations and disputes
mentions.detail: IRS transfer pricing disputes fiscal 2007-2015 settled September 2025; returns open from fiscal 2007
mentions.quote: The disputed amounts for fiscal 2013 to fiscal 2016 largely relate to transfer pricing matters. In December 2023, we filed a petition in the U.S. Tax Court challenging the 2014 to 2015 Notice. In September 2025, we reached a settlement with the IRS for fiscal 2007 to fiscal 2015.

mentions.heading: Malaysian tax assessment dispute
mentions.detail: Malaysian IRB fiscal 2020 assessment up to MYR 1.9 billion (~$480.2 million); decision possibly within 18 months
mentions.quote: If the adjustment is upheld by the highest court that has jurisdiction over this matter in Malaysia, it could result in income taxes and penalties up to MYR 1.9 billion (approximately $480.2 million based on the exchange rate as of March 31, 2026).

mentions.heading: Exposure to greater income tax liabilities and tax law changes
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: We are a U.S.-based multinational company subject to tax in many U.S. and foreign jurisdictions. Our income tax obligations could be affected by many factors, including changes to our operating structure, intercompany arrangements and tax planning strategies.

mentions.heading: Changes in effective tax rates and tax laws
mentions.detail: Exposure to OECD BEPS-aligned jurisdictions, transfer pricing challenges, tax incentive performance obligations, deferred tax asset valuation
mentions.quote: These include changes in tax rates, tax laws, and tax regulations and how those laws are interpreted in jurisdictions where our income is earned. This also applies to jurisdictions that align with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Base Erosion Profit Shifting recommendations.

mentions.heading: Policies implemented globally by current or future administrations
mentions.detail: U.S. and global changes to tariffs, taxes, trade, labor, environment could raise tax rate and costs, reduce revenue
mentions.quote: If implemented, these changes could increase our effective tax rate, decrease our revenue and increase our selling, general, administrative and/or manufacturing costs, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations or financial conditions.

mentions.heading: Policies implemented globally by current or future administrations
mentions.detail: Ceased shipments to Russia and Belarus; sales into region hurt but not material; possible Russian retaliatory cyber-attacks
mentions.quote: Because the actions by Russia against Ukraine are in conflict with our Guiding Values, we chose to cease shipments into Russia and Belarus, and we will continue to comply with applicable U.S. sanctions imposed on Russia, Belarus, and Russia-controlled areas of Ukraine.

mentions.heading: Policies implemented globally by current or future administrations
mentions.detail: EU AI Act conformity assessments, China generative AI rules, U.S. federal and state AI/cybersecurity frameworks
mentions.quote: The EU AI Act, which has a phased implementation schedule, imposes requirements on AI systems based on their risk classification, and may require conformity assessments, registration, and ongoing monitoring for certain AI systems.

mentions.heading: We are subject to stringent environmental, climate change and other regulations
mentions.detail: Hazardous substances, greenhouse gas emissions limits, GHG reporting with third-party assurance; possible material substitution
mentions.quote: Regulations could require us to change manufacturing processes, substitute materials which may cost more or be less available, obtain new permits and undertake other costly activities.

mentions.heading: Failure to comply with environmental regulations could result in fines and liabilities
mentions.detail: Emission restrictions, carbon taxes, cap and trade; customer contracts constrain speed of abatement changes; possible ramp-down of operations
mentions.quote: If we are unable to implement the necessary abatement plan, we may be required to ramp down our existing operations significantly or risk noncompliance with regulations.

mentions.heading: Expanding laws on energy efficiency, recycling and chemicals in electronics
mentions.detail: Electronics recycling, chemical reduction and packaging laws may leave insufficient compliant products and unsaleable inventory
mentions.quote: It may be difficult for us to timely comply with these laws and we may have insufficient quantities of compliant products to meet customers' needs, thereby adversely impacting our sales and profitability. We may have to write off inventory if we hold unsaleable inventory as a result of changes to regulations.

mentions.heading: Sustained adverse climate change poses risks that could harm our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Operations in arid or tropical regions exposed to fires, storms, floods, droughts; water and utility shortages
mentions.quote: Certain of our operations are located in arid or tropical regions, which some experts believe may become vulnerable to more frequent fires, storms, severe floods and droughts.

mentions.heading: Voluntary ESG initiatives could require costly activities
mentions.detail: ESG initiatives may require emission limits, process changes, costlier material substitution and offset funding
mentions.quote: Voluntary actions we may take or have taken as part of our ESG initiatives could require us to limit emissions, change manufacturing processes, substitute materials which may cost more or be less available, fund offset projects, or undertake other costly activities.

mentions.heading: Conflict minerals disclosure and sourcing requirements
mentions.detail: SEC Dodd-Frank conflict minerals rules on DRC-sourced minerals; annual Form SD since 2014; customers may disqualify supplier, inventory write-offs
mentions.quote: If we are unable to meet customer requirements, customers may disqualify us as a supplier, resulting in a permanent or temporary loss of sales to such customer or a reduction in purchases from us, and we may have to write off inventory if it cannot be sold.

mentions.detail: Stopped sales to Russia and Belarus in March 2022, but Russian entities still indirectly obtained products
mentions.quote: However, we have been made aware that there are entities in Russia that indirectly obtained our products after March 2022 despite the preventative measures we took and continue to take.

mentions.heading: Failure to meet ESG expectations could adversely affect business
mentions.detail: California climate disclosure rules and EU CSRD; net zero and renewable energy goals expose company to scrutiny
mentions.quote: In addition, we are or expect to become subject to various new or proposed climate-related and other sustainability laws and regulations, including, for example, the state of California's new climate change disclosure requirements and the EU's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive.

mentions.heading: Failure to meet evolving stakeholder expectations or corporate responsibility goals
mentions.detail: Risks include customer loss, unfavorable ESG ratings, compliance costs, and impaired access to and cost of capital
mentions.quote: Any failure, or perceived failure, to meet evolving stakeholder expectations or industry standards, or achieve our corporate responsibility goals could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition, reputation, or stock price.

mentions.heading: The future trading price of our common stock could be subject to wide fluctuations
mentions.detail: Volatility could also affect Convertible Debt, Series A Preferred Stock and Depositary Shares
mentions.quote: The foregoing factors could also cause the market price of our Convertible Debt, Series A Preferred Stock or Depositary Shares to decline or fluctuate substantially.

mentions.heading: The future trading price of our common stock could be subject to wide fluctuations
mentions.detail: Volatile stock price could prompt class actions, costing money and management attention
mentions.quote: If we are sued in a securities class action, we could incur substantial costs, and it could divert management's attention and resources and have an adverse impact on our financial performance and the price of our common stock or Series A Preferred Stock.

mentions.heading: The amount and timing of our share repurchases may fluctuate
mentions.detail: $4.00 billion authorization with $1.56 billion remaining; no repurchases in fiscal 2026
mentions.quote: Although our Board of Directors has authorized share repurchases of up to $4.00 billion, of which $1.56 billion is still available, the authorization does not obligate us to acquire any particular amount of shares.

mentions.heading: Outstanding indebtedness and refinancing of fixed rate debt
mentions.detail: $5.54 billion debt: $3.00B Senior Notes, $2.19B Convertible Debt, $349M commercial paper; $2.25B revolver undrawn to 2030
mentions.quote: Changes in interest rates will have a more significant impact on our interest expense if we refinance our fixed rate debt with variable rate debt. There can be no assurance that we will be able to refinance our current or future debt on reasonable terms, if at all.

mentions.heading: Servicing our debt requires a significant amount of cash
mentions.risk_name: Insufficient cash flow for debt service
mentions.detail: Borrowings used to fund part of quarterly dividends in recent quarters; may cut dividends, buybacks or sell assets
mentions.quote: In several recent quarters, we have used borrowings to finance a portion of our quarterly dividend payments and we may continue to do so in future periods.

mentions.heading: Adverse changes in credit ratings could increase borrowing costs
mentions.detail: Investment grade maintained but downgraded by one rating agency in March 2025; affects Senior Notes and Commercial Paper
mentions.quote: While we have maintained our investment grade rating, in March 2025 we were downgraded by one rating agency and there is no assurance that we will maintain our current credit ratings.

mentions.heading: Conversion of Convertible Debt or Series A Preferred Stock will dilute stockholders
mentions.detail: 2017 Senior Convertible Debt principal settled in cash; Series A Preferred dividends payable in stock; may encourage short selling
mentions.quote: Following our irrevocable settlement election made on April 1, 2022 with respect to the 2017 Senior Convertible Debt, upon conversion, we are required to satisfy our conversion obligation with respect to such converted Convertible Debt by delivering cash equal to the principal amount of such converted Convertible Debt and cash and shares of common stock or any combination, at our option, with respect to any conversion value in excess thereof (i.e., the conversion spread).

mentions.heading: The market price of our common stock is likely to be influenced by our Convertible Debt, Series A Preferred Stock or Depositary Shares
mentions.detail: Conversion of Convertible Debt, Series A Preferred Stock or Depositary Shares and hedging/arbitrage may depress common stock price
mentions.quote: The market price of our common stock could become more volatile and could be depressed by: (1) investors’ anticipation of the potential resale in the market of a substantial number of additional shares of common stock received upon conversion of the Convertible Debt, Series A Preferred Stock or Depositary Shares;

mentions.heading: Our common stock ranks junior to our Series A Preferred Stock
mentions.detail: Series A Preferred liquidation preference of $1,000 per share plus accumulated dividends; common dividends blocked until preferred dividends paid
mentions.quote: Likewise, in the event of our voluntary or involuntary liquidation, winding-up or dissolution, no distribution of our assets may be made to holders of our common stock until we have paid to holders of our Series A Preferred Stock a liquidation preference equal to $1,000 per share plus accumulated and unpaid dividends.
