mentions.quote: Conversely, some of our facilities are single source facilities that only produce one of our end-products, and a disruption at any such facility would materially delay or cease production of the related product.

mentions.heading: Dependence on third-party suppliers for components and raw materials
mentions.detail: Limited number of highly specialized suppliers for key technologies; forecast-based purchase commitments, some long-term
mentions.quote: We are also dependent upon a limited number of highly specialized third-party suppliers for required components and materials for certain of our key technologies. Arranging for replacement manufacturers and suppliers can be time-consuming and costly, and the number of qualified alternative providers can be extremely limited.

mentions.heading: Shortages or cost increases of essential raw materials
mentions.detail: Generic statement; no minimum supply obligations from raw material suppliers
mentions.quote: However, shortages could occur in various essential raw materials, and if we are unable to obtain adequate supplies of raw materials in a timely manner, the costs of our raw materials increase significantly, their quality deteriorates or they give rise to compatibility or performance issues in our products, our results of operations could be materially adversely affected.

mentions.heading: Disruptions to supply chain, manufacturing and product shipments
mentions.detail: Absenteeism, quarantines, factory closures, port disruptions affecting manufacturing and suppliers, distributors, sub-contractors
mentions.quote: Any associated worker absenteeism, quarantines and restrictions on certain of our employees’ ability to perform their jobs, office and factory closures or restrictions, labor shortages, disruptions to ports and other shipping infrastructure, border closures and/or other travel or health-related restrictions could, depending on the magnitude of such effects on our manufacturing activities (or activities of our suppliers, third-party distributors or sub-contractors), cause disruption and delay to our supply chain, manufacturing and product shipments.

mentions.heading: Underutilization of manufacturing facilities and minimum purchase obligations
mentions.detail: Underused own fabs, test facilities and external manufacturers at minimum purchase obligation levels raise unit costs, cut gross profit
mentions.quote: In addition, if we are unable to utilize our manufacturing facilities, testing facilities and external manufacturers at expected or minimum purchase obligation levels, or if production capacity increases while revenue does not, the fixed costs and other operating expenses associated with these facilities and arrangements will not be fully absorbed, resulting in higher average unit costs and lower gross profits, which could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.

mentions.heading: Demand forecasting errors and inventory obsolescence
mentions.detail: Inaccurate forecasts, order cancellations and rapid technological change may cause inventory charges
mentions.quote: If we purchase or commit to purchase inventory in anticipation of customer demand that does not materialize, or such inventory is rendered obsolete by the rapid pace of technological change, or if customers reduce, delay or cancel orders, we may incur excess or obsolete inventory charges.

mentions.heading: We may be unable to implement certain business strategies and restructuring initiatives
mentions.detail: Restructuring may relocate production, exit product lines; capacity expansion may raise capex
mentions.quote: Because our strategies and restructuring activities may involve changes to many aspects of our business, including the location of our production facilities and personnel and the potential exit of certain product lines and businesses, our ability to successfully execute these activities depends on a number of factors, many of which are outside of our control.

mentions.heading: Transition services risks from prior divestitures
mentions.detail: Several transition services provided to acquirers of prior divestitures; acquirer failure or financial difficulty could disrupt operations
mentions.quote: Similarly, the contingent risks associated with transferring our existing operations to an acquirer, as is the case with several transition services being provided in connection with some of our prior divestitures, could materially impact our financial condition or results of operations and/or could disrupt our existing operations, especially if the acquirer is unable to meet its commitments under any transition services agreements or if the acquirer encounters financial difficulty.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry requires substantial investment in research and development
mentions.detail: Lengthy development cycles; design wins may not yield sales or recover development investment
mentions.quote: In addition, design wins do not guarantee that we will make customer sales or generate sufficient revenue to recover design and development investments, realize a return on the capital expended or achieve expected gross margins, as expenditures for technology and product development are generally

mentions.heading: Selling to new customers including government entities adds regulations
mentions.detail: Expansion to government entities may impose additional regulations and legal obligations
mentions.quote: Developing and selling new products or expanding sales to new customers, including government entities, may subject us to additional regulations and legal obligations. Our failure to comply with such requirements could increase our operational risks and reduce our competitiveness.

mentions.heading: Rapidly evolving technologies and short product life cycles
mentions.detail: Older product prices fall; contractual obligations may force loss-making production of older products
mentions.quote: In certain limited cases, we may not be able to cease production of older products, either due to contractual obligations or for customer relationship reasons and, as a result, may be required to bear a loss on such products for a sustained period of time.

mentions.heading: The semiconductor industry is highly competitive and has experienced significant consolidation
mentions.detail: Competition from global semiconductor majors and niche players; limits price increases and gross margin
mentions.quote: Competitive pressures may limit our ability to raise prices, and any inability to maintain revenue or raise prices to offset increases in costs could have a significant adverse effect on our gross margin.

mentions.heading: Industry consolidation and customer vertical integration
mentions.detail: Semiconductor competitor consolidation and customer vertical integration could erode market share and force restructuring
mentions.quote: Consolidation among competitors and integration among customers could erode our market share, impair our capacity to compete and require us to restructure our operations, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business.

mentions.heading: Competitors may receive governmental subsidies or incentives
mentions.detail: US and EU semiconductor funding legislation; risk of not accessing, reduction or clawback of awards, or competitors receiving more
mentions.quote: For example, the United States and the European Union have enacted legislation to provide funding and incentives for semiconductor research, development, and manufacturing in their respective regions.

mentions.heading: Dependence on automotive and industrial end-markets
mentions.detail: Automotive ~51% and industrial ~28% of 2025 revenue; exposure to EV demand fluctuations
mentions.quote: Sales into the automotive and industrial end-markets represented approximately 51% and 28% of our revenue, respectively, for the year ended December 31, 2025.

mentions.heading: Dependence on automotive and industrial end-markets
mentions.detail: One distributor accounted for ~11% of 2025 and 10% of 2024 revenue
mentions.quote: We had one customer, a distributor, whose revenue accounted for approximately 11% and 10% of the total revenue for the years ended 2025 and 2024, respectively, across all reportable segments.

mentions.heading: Dependence on automotive and industrial end-markets
mentions.detail: Long-term supply agreements with fixed pricing; customers seek to amend or cancel delivery terms
mentions.quote: Further, to the extent we have long-term supply agreements with our customers that include fixed pricing, we could be subject to fluctuating manufacturing costs that could negatively impact our profitability. Additionally, under our long-term supply agreements, we could incur certain obligations if we are not able to fulfill our commitments.

mentions.heading: Our operating results depend, in part, on the performance of independent distributors.
mentions.detail: Distributors not bound by minimum sales; reliance on distributor sales reports for revenue recognition
mentions.quote: These independent distributors also generally represent product lines offered by several companies and are not subject to any minimum sales requirements or obligation to market our products to their customers. Accordingly, distributors could reduce their sales efforts for our products or choose to terminate their representation of us.

mentions.heading: Tariffs, trade policies or geopolitical conditions could reduce demand
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: The imposition of or increase in tariffs, export controls and other trade restrictions as a result of international trade disputes or changes in trade policies or political conditions may adversely affect our sales and profitability.

mentions.heading: Leshan, China facility exposed to US-China trade restrictions
mentions.detail: Leshan, China assembly/test facility owned by 80%-owned JV Leshan-Phoenix; entity list additions, export licenses for China customers
mentions.quote: The U.S. Department of Commerce may add additional Chinese companies to its restricted entity list or unverified list and regulatory bodies of either country may take other actions that could expand licensing requirements or otherwise impact the market for our products and our revenue.

mentions.heading: Tariffs on imported components may reduce profitability
mentions.detail: Tariffs on imported components may force price increases, hurting competitiveness
mentions.quote: In addition, tariffs on components that we import from certain nations that have imposed, or may in the future impose, tariffs may adversely affect our profitability unless we are able to exclude such components from the tariffs or we raise prices for our products, which may result in our products becoming less attractive relative to products offered by our competitors.

mentions.heading: Compliance with import and export laws
mentions.detail: U.S. Export Administration Act; penalties up to denial of export privileges or government contract debarment
mentions.quote: For example, licenses or proper license exceptions are required for the shipment of our products to certain countries under applicable export control regulations, including the provisions of the U.S. Export Administration Act.

mentions.heading: Our power technologies designed for AI use may not capture market share as expected
mentions.detail: Power products for AI data centers; intense competition, possible slower AI adoption due to insufficient power or customer scale-backs
mentions.quote: In addition, if AI-related technologies fail to achieve the effectiveness or adoption levels currently anticipated, including due to insufficient available power or other utilities, or if our customers delay or scale back their AI deployments, demand for our AI-related products and solutions and returns on associated investments could be materially lower than we currently expect.

mentions.heading: Issues related to the responsible use of AI may adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Association with AI infrastructure may bring reputational harm and regulatory scrutiny; AI regulation may limit adoption
mentions.quote: Further, because AI has become the focus of significant societal and regulatory debate, including concerns about safety, bias, misuse and environmental impact, our association with AI infrastructure could expose us to reputational harm, stakeholder criticism or increased regulatory scrutiny, even if we do not control the design or use of AI systems that incorporate our products.

mentions.heading: Incorporating AI tools may subject us to competitive, legal, regulatory and other risks
mentions.detail: Risks from flawed algorithms, IP and data loss, competitors' superior AI use, and emerging AI laws
mentions.quote: The jurisdictions in which we conduct business have and may adopt laws and regulations related to AI, which could cause us to incur greater compliance costs, limit our use of AI tools, or subject us to legal liabilities.

mentions.heading: We may be unable to attract and retain highly skilled personnel.
mentions.detail: Intense competition for experienced semiconductor design engineers; tight labor markets; most employees lack employment agreements
mentions.quote: In the semiconductor industry, the competition for qualified personnel, particularly experienced design engineers and other technical employees, is intense. Furthermore, we have operations in many parts of the world that are currently experiencing a tight labor market for skilled employees.

mentions.heading: Warranty claims, product liability claims, product recalls, and contract non-compliance could harm our business
mentions.detail: Manufacturing impurities can cause defects; OEMs increasingly expect suppliers to warrant products and contribute to recalls
mentions.quote: As suppliers become more integrally involved in electrical design, OEMs are increasingly expecting them to warrant their products and are looking to them for contributions when faced with product liability claims or recalls.

mentions.heading: Warranty claims, product liability claims, product recalls, and contract non-compliance could harm our business
mentions.detail: Defects may trigger customer-chain consequential damages exceeding product revenue; contractual liability limits may fail
mentions.quote: Since a defect or failure in our products could give rise to failures in the goods that incorporate them (and claims for consequential damages against our customers from their customers), we may face claims for damages that are disproportionate to the revenue and profits we receive from the products involved.

mentions.heading: Currency fluctuations and foreign exchange regulations
mentions.detail: Revenue mostly USD but significant costs in foreign currencies from Asia/Pacific and European operations
mentions.quote: We have sizeable operations in the Asia/Pacific region and Europe and, although a majority of our revenue is denominated in U.S. dollars, a significant portion of our cost of revenue and operating expenses are payable in foreign currencies.

mentions.heading: Repatriation of funds held outside the United States
mentions.detail: Lower US cash could impair ability to make interest and principal payments on debt
mentions.quote: If we have a lower amount of cash and cash equivalents in the United States, our financial flexibility may be reduced, which could have a material adverse effect on our ability to make interest and principal payments due under our various debt obligations.

mentions.heading: Claims of infringement on the IP rights of others
mentions.detail: Generic statement; possible damages, injunctions, customer indemnification, suspension of manufacture
mentions.quote: The failure to obtain a license from a third party for IP that we use could cause us to incur substantial liabilities or to suspend the manufacture or shipment of products or our use of processes requiring such technologies.

mentions.heading: Failure to adequately protect developed or licensed IP
mentions.detail: Patents, mask works, trademarks may lapse or be invalidated; enforcement may provoke counterclaims
mentions.quote: Further, our assertion of IP rights often results in the other party seeking to assert alleged IP rights of its own against us, which may materially and adversely impact our business.

mentions.heading: Inadequate protection of unpatented IP (continuation)
mentions.detail: Some products and technologies not covered by patents; relies on confidentiality agreements that may be breached
mentions.quote: In addition, some of our products and technologies are not covered by any patents or pending patent applications.

mentions.heading: Disruptions or breaches of our information technology systems could irreparably damage our reputation and business
mentions.detail: Has experienced breaches; AI and quantum computing used to craft attacks; malware could attack products; cyber insurance may be insufficient
mentions.quote: Further, AI and quantum computing capabilities are increasingly being used to identify vulnerabilities and

mentions.heading: We are subject to governmental laws, regulations and other legal obligations related to privacy and data protection
mentions.detail: Collects PII; EU and US state privacy laws more restrictive; fines and reputational damage possible
mentions.quote: Many foreign countries and governmental bodies, including the European Union and other relevant jurisdictions where we conduct business, have laws and regulations concerning the collection and use of PII and other data obtained from their residents or by businesses operating within their jurisdictions that are currently more restrictive than those in the United States.

mentions.heading: Reliance on information technology systems and third-party service providers
mentions.detail: Systems partly managed by third-party providers including cloud platform providers; failures could cause disruption and data loss
mentions.quote: Some of these systems are managed or provided by third-party service providers, including certain cloud platform providers. Failure by these third-party service providers to meet their contractual, regulatory and other obligations to us, or our failure to adequately monitor their performance, could result in our inability to achieve expected efficiencies and result in additional costs to correct errors made by such service providers.

mentions.heading: Investments in IT systems including new ERP implementation
mentions.detail: New enterprise resource planning system implemented Q3 2025; replacing legacy systems, outsourcing, testing generative AI
mentions.quote: In addition, we are currently making, and will continue to make, substantial investments in our information technology systems, infrastructure and personnel, including a new enterprise resource planning system implemented in the third quarter of 2025, in certain cases with the assistance of strategic partners and other third-party service providers.

mentions.heading: Environmental and health and safety liabilities and expenditures could materially adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
mentions.detail: PFAS regulation could reduce availability of PFAS-containing inputs used in products and manufacturing; conflict minerals rules also apply
mentions.quote: For example, a number of domestic and foreign jurisdictions regulate, or may seek to regulate, the use of a class of chemicals known as per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (“PFAS”), which are currently used in our products or the manufacture of some of our products, which may negatively impact our supply chain due to the potentially decreased availability, or non-availability, of PFAS-containing products or suitable alternatives.

mentions.heading: Environmental and health and safety liabilities and expenditures could materially adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
mentions.detail: Indemnities and environmental insurance for historical contamination may not cover all costs
mentions.quote: We have indemnities from third parties for certain environmental and health and safety liabilities for periods prior to our operations at some of our current and past sites, and we have also purchased environmental insurance to cover certain claims related to historical contamination and future releases of hazardous substances. However, we cannot assure you that such indemnification arrangements and insurance will cover any or all of our material environmental costs.

mentions.heading: Environmental, health and safety compliance costs and liabilities
mentions.detail: Unknown contamination clean-up, fines; costs not covered by indemnities or insurance borne fully
mentions.quote: To the extent that we face unforeseen environmental or health and safety compliance costs or remediation expenses or liabilities that are not covered by indemnities or insurance, we may bear the full effect of such costs, expenses and liabilities, which could materially adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Our failure to comply with anti-corruption laws could result in penalties
mentions.detail: FCPA exposure including via intermediaries and acquired businesses
mentions.quote: If we are not in compliance with the FCPA and other laws governing the conduct of business with government entities (including local laws), we may be subject to criminal and civil penalties and other remedial measures, which could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, results of operations and liquidity.

mentions.heading: Changes in tax legislation or exposure to additional tax liabilities
mentions.detail: Global transfer pricing exposure; OECD BEPS; FDII deduction could shrink if customers move manufacturing to U.S.
mentions.quote: Most of our income is taxable in the United States with a significant portion qualifying for preferential treatment as foreign-derived intangible income (“FDII”). If our customers move manufacturing operations to the United States, our FDII deduction may be reduced.

mentions.heading: Tax legislation changes including OBBBA and CAMT
mentions.detail: Subject to Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax with no current liability; OBBBA interpretation could create CAMT liability
mentions.quote: While we are subject to the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (“CAMT”), we currently have no CAMT liability. However, future changes in our financial results, business operations, or the interpretation and implementation of the OBBBA could result in a CAMT liability in subsequent periods.

mentions.heading: Social and environmental responsibility regulations may complicate supply chain
mentions.detail: OEMs demand minerals not sourced from conflict areas such as Democratic Republic of Congo, affecting mineral availability and pricing
mentions.quote: In addition, an increasing number of OEMs are seeking to source products that do not contain minerals sourced from areas where proceeds from the sale of such minerals are likely to be used to fund armed conflicts, such as in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

mentions.heading: Social and environmental responsibility regulations may complicate supply chain
mentions.risk_name: ESG ratings and cost of capital
mentions.detail: Unfavorable ESG ratings could hurt stock price, access to and cost of capital
mentions.quote: In addition, unfavorable ratings or assessment of our corporate social and environmental policies and programs, including our compliance with certain voluntary disclosure standards and frameworks, may lead to negative investor sentiment toward us, which could have a negative impact on our stock price and our access to and cost of capital.

mentions.heading: Social and environmental responsibility regulations may complicate supply chain
mentions.detail: Net zero emissions goal by 2040 may require material expenditures and disrupt operations
mentions.quote: Furthermore, in pursuit of our goal to achieve net zero emissions by 2040, or in response to future customer or investor expectations and regulatory requirements, we may take certain actions that may result in material expenditures that could impact our financial condition or results of operations and/or disrupt our existing operations.

mentions.heading: Our debt could materially adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations
mentions.detail: $3,004.9 million principal outstanding at Dec 31, 2025; about $1.5 billion available under Revolving Credit Facility
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had $3,004.9 million of outstanding principal relating to our indebtedness.

mentions.heading: Inability to meet Credit Agreement obligations could materially affect us
mentions.detail: Credit Agreement secured by substantially all guarantor assets and subsidiary equity pledges; mandatory prepayment if draws exceed commitments
mentions.quote: The obligations under the Credit Agreement are collateralized by a lien on substantially all of the assets of the guarantors under the Credit Agreement, including a pledge of the equity interests in certain of our domestic and first-tier foreign subsidiaries.

mentions.heading: Debt agreements may restrict our ability to operate our business
mentions.detail: Credit Agreement and 3.875% Notes covenants limit debt, liens, M&A, distributions; financial ratio maintenance tests
mentions.quote: Our debt agreements, including the Credit Agreement and the 3.875% Notes, contain, and any future debt agreements may include, a number of restrictive covenants that impose significant operating and financial restrictions on us and our subsidiaries.

mentions.heading: May not generate sufficient cash flow to meet debt service obligations
mentions.risk_name: Insufficient cash flow for debt service
mentions.detail: May need refinancing, asset sales or capex cuts; refinancing may be barred by debt instruments
mentions.quote: If we do not generate sufficient cash to satisfy our debt obligations as they come due, we may have to undertake alternative financing plans, such as refinancing or restructuring our debt, selling assets, reducing or delaying capital investments, or seeking to raise additional capital.

mentions.heading: Change of control repurchase and collateral enforcement
mentions.detail: Debt repurchase on change of control may exceed resources; secured holders could seize collateral; Credit Agreement borrowing could be cut
mentions.quote: If we are unable to repay, refinance or restructure our indebtedness under our collateralized debt, the holders of such debt could proceed against the collateral securing that indebtedness, which could materially negatively impact our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Event of default could cross default other indebtedness
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: If there were an event of default under certain of our agreements relating to our outstanding indebtedness, the holders of the defaulted debt could cause all amounts outstanding with respect to that debt to be due and payable immediately, which default or acceleration of debt could cross default other indebtedness.

mentions.heading: Operating subsidiaries may not make cash available for debt repayment
mentions.detail: Holding company reliant on subsidiary distributions; non-guarantor subsidiaries have no repayment obligation
mentions.quote: Repayment of our indebtedness is dependent on the generation of cash flow by our subsidiaries and their ability to make such cash available to us, by dividend, debt repayment or otherwise.

mentions.heading: Dependence on subsidiaries for cash to service indebtedness
mentions.detail: Legal, contractual or regulatory restrictions may limit cash upstreamed from subsidiaries to service debt
mentions.quote: Each subsidiary is a distinct legal entity, and, under certain circumstances, legal, contractual, governmental, or regulatory restrictions may limit our ability to obtain cash from our subsidiaries.

mentions.heading: If interest rates increase, our debt service obligations under our variable rate indebtedness could increase significantly
mentions.detail: Credit Agreement borrowings at variable rates; swaps may not cover all variable debt
mentions.quote: Borrowings under certain of our facilities from time to time, including under our Credit Agreement, are at variable rates of interest and as a result expose us to interest rate risk.

mentions.heading: Cash payments to service the 0%, 0.50% and 3.875% Notes may require significant cash
mentions.detail: $804.9M 0% Notes, $1,500.0M 0.50% Notes, $700.0M 3.875% Notes; holder put rights, refinancing uncertain
mentions.quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had outstanding approximately $804.9 million aggregate principal amount of our 0% Notes, $1,500.0 million aggregate principal amount of our 0.50% Notes and $700.0 million aggregate principal amount of our 3.875% Notes (collectively, the "Outstanding Notes").

mentions.heading: Change of control repurchase obligations on Outstanding Notes
mentions.detail: 3.875% Notes repurchasable at 101% on change of control plus ratings event
mentions.quote: For example, holders of the 3.875% Notes have the right to require us to repurchase all of their 3.875% Notes upon the occurrence of certain change of control triggering events accompanied by certain ratings events (as described in the indenture governing the 3.875% Notes) at a repurchase price equal to 101% of their principal amount, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, accrued prior to, but not including, the repurchase date.

mentions.heading: Additional debt, acquisitions or buybacks could intensify debt risks
mentions.detail: Credit Agreement and 3.875% Notes limit secured debt; acquisitions or stock repurchases could intensify risks
mentions.quote: If we incur significantly more debt, this could intensify the risks described above. Our decision to use our cash for other purposes, such as to make acquisitions or to repurchase our common stock, could also intensify these risks.

mentions.heading: Note hedge and warrant transactions may adversely affect the value of our common stock
mentions.detail: Warrants dilutive above $74.34 (0% Notes) and $156.78 (0.50% Notes) share prices
mentions.quote: The warrant transactions could separately have a dilutive effect on our common stock to the extent that the market price per share of our common stock exceeds $74.34, with respect to the 0% Notes and $156.78 with respect to the 0.50% Notes.

mentions.heading: Hedge activities by option counterparties may affect the value of our common stock
mentions.detail: Option counterparties hedging 0% Notes and 0.50% Notes may buy/sell stock or derivatives, affecting share price
mentions.quote: The potential effect, if any, of these transactions and activities on the market price of our common stock will depend in part on market conditions and cannot be ascertained at this time. Any of these activities could materially adversely affect the value of our common stock.

mentions.heading: Counterparty risk with respect to the note hedge transactions
mentions.detail: Unsecured exposure to option counterparties on 0% and 0.50% Notes hedges; default raises dilution, cash payments, tax consequences
mentions.quote: Our exposure to the credit risk of the option counterparties is not secured by any collateral. If one or more of the option counterparties to one or more of our note hedge transactions becomes subject to insolvency proceedings, we will become an unsecured creditor in those proceedings with a claim equal to our exposure at the time under those transactions.

mentions.heading: Provisions in our charter documents may delay or prevent the acquisition of us
mentions.detail: Advance notice rules, blank check preferred stock, 66 2/3% supermajority to amend provisions
mentions.quote: Our certificate of incorporation and by-laws contain provisions that could make it harder for a third party to acquire us without the consent of our Board of Directors.

mentions.heading: The amount and frequency of our share repurchases may fluctuate
mentions.detail: Generic statement
mentions.quote: The amount, timing, and purchases under our share repurchase program, if any, are influenced by many factors and may fluctuate based on our operating results, cash flows, and priorities for the use of cash and because of changes in tax laws, and the market price of our common stock.

mentions.heading: Inability to successfully make or integrate strategic acquisitions, joint ventures or investments
mentions.detail: Integration of IT systems, due diligence gaps, customer reactions, key employee loss; often in less familiar markets or regions
mentions.quote: Missteps or delays in integrating our acquisitions, which could be caused by factors outside of our control, or our failure to realize the expected benefits of the acquisitions on the timeline we anticipate, could materially adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Consolidating acquired businesses may impair financial reporting
mentions.detail: Acquired businesses may lack GAAP audited statements or compatible controls, risking restatements
mentions.quote: Any revisions to, inaccuracies in or restatements of our consolidated financial statements due to accounting for our acquisitions could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

mentions.heading: If our goodwill or amortizable intangible assets become impaired, we may be required to record a significant charge to earnings.
mentions.detail: Triggers include stock price decline, reduced cash flow estimates, slower segment growth; impairments recorded in the past
mentions.quote: We have in the past recorded, and may in the future be required to record, a significant charge in our consolidated financial statements during the period in which any impairment of our goodwill or amortizable intangible assets is determined, negatively affecting our financial position and results of operations.

mentions.heading: Downturns or volatility in general economic conditions could adversely impact our business
mentions.detail: Semiconductor sales track economic cycles; possible US recession; inflation and interest rates raise costs and hit investment portfolio
mentions.quote: Historically, worldwide semiconductor industry sales have tracked the impacts of adverse economic conditions, specifically financial crises, subsequent recoveries and persistent economic uncertainty. Recent global economic uncertainty could continue and potentially result in certain economies dipping into economic recessions, including in the United States.

mentions.heading: Macroeconomic events could disrupt supply chain and operations
mentions.detail: AI technology valuation concerns, inflation, geopolitical conflict, climate and disasters could disrupt suppliers, distributors and transport
mentions.quote: In addition to general economic conditions, impacts of other macroeconomic events, such as valuation concerns related to AI technologies, continued inflation and labor market concerns, public health crises, geopolitical tensions or conflicts and risks, climate change and other severe weather and natural disasters and uncertainties in global financial markets, could materially adversely impact our operations or those of our suppliers, third party distributors and sub-contractors.

mentions.heading: We have been and may be subject to or involved in litigation or threatened litigation
mentions.detail: Generic statement; references Note 13 legal matters, possible inadequate insurance
mentions.quote: Even if we are able to estimate losses related to these actions, the ultimate amount of loss may be materially higher than our estimates. Any resolution of litigation, or threatened litigation, could involve the payment of damages or expenses by us, which may be significant or involve an agreement with terms that restrict the operation of our business.

mentions.heading: Regulatory and legislative developments related to climate change may materially adversely affect our business
mentions.detail: Complex supply chain and significant outsourced manufacturing make compliance difficult; customer and investor ESG expectations
mentions.quote: These legal and regulatory requirements, as well as some investors' heightened expectations, on corporate environmental and social responsibility practices and disclosure are subject to change, can be unpredictable and may be difficult and expensive for us to comply with, given the complexity of our supply chain and our significant outsourced manufacturing.

mentions.heading: Our global operations subject us to risks associated with domestic or international political, social, economic or other conditions.
mentions.detail: About 60% of revenue from non-US-headquartered customers; China-HQ customers ~20% and shipments into China ~50% of 2025 revenue
mentions.quote: Revenue from end customers headquartered in China represented about 20% of our revenue in 2025, while revenue from products shipped into China represented about 50% of our revenue in 2025.

mentions.heading: Our global operations subject us to risks associated with domestic or international political, social, economic or other conditions.
mentions.detail: US-China tensions; semiconductor-specific tariffs, export restrictions and sanctions could limit market access and equipment purchases
mentions.quote: Certain countries where we operate, particularly the United States and China, have experienced, and other countries may experience, geopolitical tensions and administrative measures that affect global trade and macroeconomic conditions through the imposition of tariffs, including tariffs specific to the products that we sell, import or export restrictions, trade embargoes and sanctions, restrictions on cross-border investment and other trade barriers applicable to the semiconductor industry.

mentions.heading: Our global operations subject us to risks associated with domestic or international political, social, economic or other conditions.
mentions.detail: Generic statement on U.S. dollar fluctuations and remeasurement of non-dollar transactions
mentions.quote: In addition, our global operations expose us to periods when the U.S. dollar significantly fluctuates in relation to the non-U.S. currencies in which we transact business. The remeasurement of non-U.S. dollar transactions can have an adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: We face substantial competition that requires us to respond rapidly to product development and pricing pressures.
mentions.detail: Emerging Asian competitors; China promoting domestic semiconductor industry through policy and investment
mentions.quote: For example, we may face increased competition as a result of China actively promoting and reshaping its domestic semiconductor industry through policy changes and investment, which could prevent us from competing effectively.

mentions.heading: Changes in expected demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Cyclical semiconductor market drives rapid demand swings across sectors
mentions.quote: The cyclical nature of the semiconductor market occasionally leads to significant and rapid increases and decreases in product demand.

mentions.heading: Changes in expected demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Loss or curtailment by large customers due to sourcing changes, inventory adjustments, tariffs, export controls
mentions.quote: Additionally, the loss or significant curtailment of purchases by one or more of our large customers, including curtailments due to a change in the design or manufacturing sourcing policies or practices of these customers, the timing of customer or distributor inventory adjustments, changes in demand for customer products, tariffs, export controls or other trade measures, may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Changes in expected demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Manufacturing forecasts for high service levels may cause excess or obsolete inventory, reducing margins
mentions.quote: Our manufacturing forecasts are based on multiple assumptions, and if inaccurate, could cause us to hold inadequate, excess or obsolete inventory that would reduce our profit margins and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

mentions.heading: Our operating results and our reputation could be adversely affected by cybersecurity events, breaches, disruptions or other incidents relating to our information technology systems.
mentions.detail: Could disrupt manufacturing and online services; threats include nation-state espionage and AI tools
mentions.quote: Cybersecurity or other threats to our information technology systems or the systems of our customers, suppliers and other third parties are frequent, increasingly sophisticated and constantly evolving, thereby making them more difficult to detect, mitigate and defend against.

mentions.heading: Our ability to successfully implement strategic, business and organizational changes could affect our business plans and results of operations.
mentions.detail: Generic statement on acquisitions, divestitures, capital investments and restructuring
mentions.quote: We may not achieve or sustain the expected growth, cost savings or other benefits of strategic, business and organizational changes, and charges associated with these actions could differ materially in amount and timing from our expectations.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations could be affected by natural events in the locations in which we operate.
mentions.detail: Principal manufacturing and design sites exposed to severe weather, geological events, epidemics; climate change may intensify
mentions.quote: Climate change might exacerbate these occurrences or cause natural disasters to occur with greater frequency and with more intense effects.

mentions.heading: Rapid technological change in markets we serve requires us to develop new technologies and products.
mentions.detail: Shortened product life cycles and ASP declines; R&D investments made before commercial viability assured
mentions.quote: In some cases, we might not realize a return or the expected return on our investments because they are generally made before commercial viability can be assured.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Supplier disruptions from quality excursions, conflict-free mineral access, credit market stress affecting supplier liquidity
mentions.quote: If our suppliers are unable to access credit markets and other sources of needed liquidity, we may be unable to obtain needed supplies, collect accounts receivable or access needed technology.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Key semiconductor materials sourced from limited geographies; geopolitical tensions and export controls on minerals, equipment raise cost and lead times
mentions.quote: Further, certain key materials used in semiconductor manufacturing are primarily sourced from limited geographies. Governments have adopted or proposed measures, including export controls on certain minerals, materials and equipment, that could adversely affect equipment and material availability, cost or movement.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Subcontracted wafer fab, assembly/test, advanced logic process development and facility construction; limited alternates, no long-term contracts
mentions.quote: We do not have long-term contracts with all of these suppliers, and the number of alternate suppliers is limited.

mentions.heading: We face supply chain and manufacturing risks.
mentions.detail: Ongoing manufacturing capacity investments under capital management strategy may not earn expected returns
mentions.quote: We have made and will continue to make investments in manufacturing capacity consistent with our capital management strategy, and we might not realize our expected return on those investments.

mentions.heading: Our continued success depends in part on our ability to retain, train and recruit a sufficient number of qualified employees in a competitive environment.
mentions.detail: Engineering, management, technical talent; international recruiting limited by immigration laws and policies
mentions.quote: Our ability to recruit internationally or deploy employees to various locations may be limited by immigration laws and policies, including changes to, or the administration or interpretation of, those laws and policies.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations and our reputation could be affected by warranty claims, product liability claims, product recalls or legal proceedings.
mentions.detail: Customer recalls of products containing TI parts, e.g., automotive and handheld electronics; insurance may be inadequate
mentions.quote: In addition, it is possible for a customer to recall a product containing a TI part, for example with respect to products used in automotive applications or handheld electronics, which may cause us to incur costs and expenses relating to the recall.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations could be adversely affected by distributors' promotion of competing product lines or our distributors' financial performance and operations.
mentions.detail: Under 20% of 2025 revenue via distributors carrying competing lines; distributor credit and administrative-measure risk
mentions.quote: In 2025, less than 20% of our revenue was generated from sales of our products through distributors. Our distributors carry competing product lines, and our sales could be affected if semiconductor distributors promote competing products over our products.

mentions.heading: Our margins vary.
mentions.detail: Owns much manufacturing capacity; capacity expansions raised capex and depreciation; tariffs, freight affect margins
mentions.quote: Because we own much of our manufacturing capacity, a significant portion of our operating costs is fixed. With our capacity expansions, capital expenditures and depreciation have increased.

mentions.heading: Our operations could be affected by the complex laws, rules and regulations to which our business is subject.
mentions.detail: Broad range of international, national, local laws; government inquiries could lead to enforcement actions or fines
mentions.quote: Compliance with these laws, rules and regulations may be onerous and expensive and could restrict our ability to manufacture or ship our products and operate our business.

mentions.heading: Environmental, safety and health rules affecting manufacturing jurisdictions
mentions.detail: Rules may require abatement equipment, material/process elimination, or energy/emissions fees; substitutes may be unavailable
mentions.quote: A substitute for a prohibited material or process might not be available, or might not be available at reasonable cost.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations could be affected by changes in tax-related matters.
mentions.detail: Facilities in over 30 countries; deferred tax assets realization at risk; tariff changes could affect tax rate
mentions.quote: We have facilities in more than 30 countries and as a result are subject to taxation and audit by a number of taxing authorities. Tax rates vary among the jurisdictions in which we operate.

mentions.heading: Changes in international tax laws including BEPS
mentions.detail: OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting laws' application to U.S. multinationals uncertain
mentions.quote: In addition, many countries have enacted or begun the process of enacting laws that align with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development’s Base Erosion and Profit Shifting recommendations; application of these laws to U.S.-based multinational corporations remains uncertain.

mentions.heading: Government incentives may be reduced or clawed back
mentions.detail: Received government and tax incentives for investments; subject to scrutiny, reduction, clawback or termination
mentions.quote: Such incentives could be subject to reduction, modification, clawback or termination, and such changes to these incentives could adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition and reputation.

mentions.heading: Our performance depends in part on our ability to enforce our intellectual property rights and to maintain freedom of operation.
mentions.detail: Claims from nonpracticing entities; customer indemnification obligations; licenses may be unavailable
mentions.quote: We, directly and indirectly, face infringement claims from third parties, including nonpracticing entities that have acquired patents to pursue enforcement actions against other companies.

mentions.heading: Our performance depends in part on our ability to enforce our intellectual property rights and to maintain freedom of operation.
mentions.detail: Unauthorized copying, cloning, counterfeit products bearing trademark; weaker foreign IP laws than U.S.
mentions.quote: Activities such as those listed above may affect our reputation and impede our ability to sell our products. The laws of countries where we operate may not protect our intellectual property rights to the same extent as U.S. laws.

mentions.heading: Our debt could affect our operations and financial condition.
mentions.detail: Debt securities with various rates and maturities; payments could divert funds or require refinancing or asset sales
mentions.quote: In addition, our obligation to make principal and interest payments could divert funds that otherwise might be invested in our operations or returned to shareholders, or could cause us to raise funds by, for example, issuing new debt or equity or selling assets.

mentions.heading: Our results of operations and liquidity could be affected by changes in the financial markets.
mentions.detail: Relies on bank credit lines supporting commercial paper and revolving credit facilities
mentions.quote: If we are unable to access these accounts and credit lines (for example, due to instability in the financial markets), our results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected and our ability to access the capital markets or redeem our investments could be restricted.

mentions.heading: Material impairments of our goodwill could adversely affect our results of operations.
mentions.detail: Generic statement; significant goodwill on balance sheet
mentions.quote: We have a significant amount of goodwill on our consolidated balance sheet. Charges associated with impairments of goodwill could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
